mahyado.note: In DQ III and DQ IV it targets one group of enemies. From DQ V on it targets all enemies (the HD-2D remake of DQ III also makes it all enemies).

mahyadedos.note: A top-tier incantation that appears from Dragon Quest Monsters: Joker and DQ IX onward. Its MP cost is 60 in DQ XI.

meragaia.note: A top-tier incantation that appears from Dragon Quest Monsters: Joker and DQ IX onward. Its MP cost is 52 in DQ XI.

raidein.note: First appeared in DQ III. It targets one enemy in DQ III and DQ IV, and all enemies from DQ V on. Because the line's entry-level spell, Dein, was added later, Raidein is the mid tier within its line.

piora.note: First appeared in the Dragon Quest Monsters series. In the main series it appears from DQ IX onward.

rariho.note: First appeared in DQ I. Depending on the game, it targets one enemy or one group of enemies.

rarihoma.note: First appeared in DQ IV. The target varies by game.

zaraki.note: First appeared in DQ II, earlier than Zaki.

zaoral.note: First appeared in DQ III. It revives with about half of max HP.

zaoriku.note: First appeared in DQ II. In the Famicom version of DQ II, the HP restored on revival is low.

dq-gira.desc: An entry-level incantation of the Gira line that burns enemies with a flash (of flame).
dq-gira.note: In DQ I it targets one enemy; from DQ II on it targets one group of enemies. In DQ I and DQ II it was depicted as fire or lightning, and was later reworked into a "high-energy flash." The Gira line itself does not appear in DQ IX.

dq-begirama.desc: A mid-tier incantation of the Gira line that burns a group of enemies with a flash stronger than Gira's.
dq-begirama.note: In DQ I it targets one enemy; from DQ II on it targets one group of enemies. It does not appear in DQ IX.

dq-begiragon.desc: A high-tier incantation of the Gira line that incinerates a group of enemies with a fierce flash.
dq-begiragon.note: First appeared in DQ III. It does not appear in DQ IX.

dq-giragureido.desc: The top tier of the Gira line, an incantation that scorches a group of enemies.
dq-giragureido.note: First appeared in Dragon Quest Monsters: Joker 2. In the numbered series it appears in games such as DQ X and DQ XI, and it does not exist in the main games from the Famicom era through DQ IX.

dq-hyadain.desc: An incantation of the Hyado line that freezes all enemies with cold.
dq-hyadain.note: It appears in games such as DQ III and DQ IV. It disappeared from the main games from DQ V on, when Mahyado became an all-enemies spell (it returned in the HD-2D remakes of DQ I and DQ II, among others). Sources differ: some place it in the same mid tier as Hyadaruko, others as a step between Hyadaruko and Mahyado.

dq-bagikurosu.desc: A high-tier incantation of the Bagi line that slashes a group of enemies with a giant tornado.

dq-bagimucho.desc: The top tier of the Bagi line, an incantation of a ferocious tornado.
dq-bagimucho.note: First appeared in Dragon Quest Monsters: Joker. In the main series it appears from DQ IX onward.

dq-io.desc: An entry-level incantation of the Io line that attacks all enemies with an explosion.
dq-io.note: In the games, this line is called "explosion." First appeared in DQ III. Its distinguishing trait is that it can hit all enemies even at the entry level.

dq-iora.desc: A mid-tier incantation of the Io line that attacks all enemies with a larger explosion.
dq-iora.note: In the games, this line is called "explosion." First appeared in DQ III.

dq-ionazun.desc: A high-tier incantation of the Io line that blasts all enemies away with a huge explosion.
dq-ionazun.note: In the games, this line is called "explosion." It was the first in its line to appear, in DQ II; Io and Iora were added in DQ III as lower tiers.

dq-iogurande.desc: The top tier of the Io line, an incantation of a colossal explosion.
dq-iogurande.note: In the games, this line is called "explosion." It appears from Dragon Quest Monsters: Joker and DQ IX onward.

dq-dein.desc: An entry-level incantation of the Dein line that calls down lightning.
dq-dein.note: First appeared in the Dragon Quest Monsters series. In the main series, players can use it from DQ XI (it was also added to the HD-2D remakes of DQ I through DQ III). Depending on the game, it targets one enemy or one group.

dq-jigodein.desc: The top tier of the Dein line, an incantation of a violent lightning strike.
dq-jigodein.note: First appeared in Dragon Quest Monsters: Joker. In the numbered series it appears from DQ X onward. Depending on the game, it targets a single enemy or all enemies. In DQ XI it is not a standalone spell but a combination attack by multiple party members.

dq-minadein.desc: An incantation of enormous lightning, fired by pooling the MP of the whole party.
dq-minadein.note: First appeared in DQ IV. It targets one enemy in DQ IV through DQ VII, and all enemies in DQ XI, where it is a combination attack. In DQ IV it uses the MP of all allies (a source lists the cost as 15).

dq-doruma.desc: An entry-level incantation of the Doruma line that attacks one enemy with the power of darkness.
dq-doruma.note: First appeared in Dragon Quest Monsters: Joker. In the main series it appears from DQ IX onward.

dq-dorukuma.desc: A dark attack incantation of the mid tier of the Doruma line.
dq-dorukuma.note: Appears from Dragon Quest Monsters: Joker onward.

dq-dorumoa.desc: A dark attack incantation of the high tier of the Doruma line.
dq-dorumoa.note: Appears from Dragon Quest Monsters: Joker onward.

dq-dorumadon.desc: A dark attack incantation of the top tier of the Doruma line.
dq-dorumadon.note: Appears from Dragon Quest Monsters: Joker onward.

dq-madante.desc: An incantation that unleashes all of the caster's magic power to deal massive damage to all enemies.
dq-madante.note: First appeared in DQ VI. In DQ VI and DQ VII it is treated as a special skill, not an incantation.

dq-behomara.desc: An incantation that restores HP for the whole party.

dq-behomazun.desc: An incantation that fully restores HP for the whole party.
dq-behomazun.note: First appeared in DQ III. It has a high MP cost.

dq-henatosu.desc: An incantation that lowers one enemy's attack power.
dq-henatosu.note: First appeared in DQ IX. It later appears in games such as DQ X and DQ XI.

dq-rukani.desc: An incantation that lowers one enemy's defense.

dq-rukanan.desc: An incantation that lowers the defense of a group of enemies.
dq-rukanan.note: First appeared in DQ II, earlier than Rukani. The amount lowered and the target are adjusted from game to game.

dq-bomiosu.desc: An incantation that lowers the speed of a group of enemies.

dq-manusa.desc: An incantation that wraps a group of enemies in illusions, making their normal attacks miss more often.

dq-medapani.desc: An incantation that confuses enemies, making them attack each other or waste their actions.
dq-medapani.note: First appeared in DQ III. Depending on the game, it targets one enemy or one group of enemies. Its upgraded version, Medapanīma, appears from DQ VIII.

dq-mahoton.desc: An incantation that seals the spells of a group of enemies.
dq-mahoton.note: First appeared in DQ I. In DQ X it targets one enemy.

dq-kiari.desc: An incantation that cures poison for one ally.

dq-kiariku.desc: An incantation that cures an ally's paralysis.
dq-kiariku.note: First appeared in DQ III. Depending on the game, it targets one ally or all allies. In games such as DQ VI it can also cure sleep.

dq-shanaku.note: First appeared in DQ III. Its handling differs by game: removing cursed equipment, or curing a curse as a status ailment. From DQ IX on, its role was handed to Oharai (purification) and it became limited to events.

dq-zarakima.desc: The highest-tier incantation of the Zaki line, which tries to instantly kill all enemies.
dq-zarakima.note: First appeared in DQ VI. It basically does not appear in games that have no concept of groups.

dq-mahokanta.desc: An incantation that raises a wall of light that reflects spells.
dq-mahokanta.note: First appeared in DQ III. In DQ III through DQ VIII it covers only the caster; from DQ IX on and in remakes it can be cast on one ally.

dq-fubaha.desc: An incantation that wraps the whole party to soften breath attacks such as flames and blizzards.
dq-fubaha.note: First appeared in DQ III. The way it reduces damage differs by game, and from DQ IX on, stacking it raises resistance in stages.

dq-magicbarrier.desc: An incantation that raises the whole party's resistance to attack spells.
dq-magicbarrier.note: First appeared in DQ VI. An unusual spell whose name is simply English. In DQ VI through DQ VIII it also works against elemental skills and status ailments; from DQ IX on it is narrowed to reducing damage from attack spells.

dq-rura.desc: An incantation that instantly moves you to a town or other place you have visited once.
dq-rura.note: First appeared in DQ I. How the destination is chosen differs by game. It does not appear as a spell in DQ X.

dq-riremito.desc: An incantation that escapes from a dungeon to its entrance.

dq-toherosu.desc: An incantation that keeps weak monsters away.

dq-remira.desc: An incantation that lights up a dark cave.

dq-inpasu.desc: An incantation that identifies the contents of treasure chests and the like.
dq-inpasu.note: First appeared in DQ III. From DQ V on it can also be used to appraise items.

dq-mahotora.desc: An incantation that drains MP from one enemy and adds it to your own.

dq-moshasu.desc: An incantation that transforms the caster into an ally, copying their abilities and spells.
dq-moshasu.note: First appeared in DQ III. From DQ V on it is enemy-only.

dq-doragoramu.desc: An incantation that turns the caster into a dragon to fight.
dq-doragoramu.note: Sources classify it as a transformation-type support incantation.

dq-parupunte.desc: An incantation whose effect is decided at random, so no one knows what will happen.
dq-parupunte.note: First appeared in DQ II. Sources give it its own category, "mystery spell."

dq-megante.desc: A self-sacrifice incantation that attacks all enemies in exchange for the caster's life.
dq-megante.note: First appeared in DQ II. Depending on the game, it either instantly kills enemies or deals massive damage. Sources classify it as an attack incantation, as part of the Megante line.

dq-jibaria.desc: An entry-level incantation that explodes the ground under one enemy's feet to deal Earth damage.
dq-jibaria.note: In the numbered series it appears in DQ X and DQ XI (in DQ XI, Camus learns it). In DQ X the explosion goes off under the target's feet after a delay. Its MP cost is 4 in DQ X.

dq-jibarika.desc: The mid-tier version of Jibaria, dealing more damage with the explosion under the target's feet.
dq-jibarika.note: In the numbered series it appears in DQ X and DQ XI. Its MP cost is 8 in DQ X.

dq-jibarina.desc: A high-tier incantation of the Jibaria line that attacks multiple enemies with an explosion under their feet.
dq-jibarina.note: In the numbered series it appears in DQ X and DQ XI. It targets one group of enemies in DQ XI, and is an area attack in DQ X. Its MP cost is 16 in DQ X.

dq-jibarunba.desc: The top-tier incantation of the Jibaria line, attacking multiple enemies with a large explosion of the ground.
dq-jibarunba.note: In the numbered series it appears in DQ X and DQ XI. It targets one group of enemies in DQ XI, and is an area attack in DQ X. Its MP cost is 16 in DQ X.

dq-dogan.desc: An entry-level incantation that hurls a rock to deal Earth damage to one enemy.
dq-dogan.note: Added in DQ X Ver. 7.0 as an incantation for the Ryūjutsushi.

dq-doganto.desc: The mid-tier version of Dogan, dealing more damage to one enemy with a rock.
dq-doganto.note: Added in DQ X Ver. 7.0 as an incantation for the Ryūjutsushi.

dq-dogantel.desc: A high-tier incantation of the Dogan line that deals heavy damage to one enemy with a large rock.
dq-dogantel.note: Added in DQ X Ver. 7.0 as an incantation for the Ryūjutsushi.

dq-dogantarosu.desc: The top-tier incantation of the Dogan line, dropping a giant rock on one enemy.
dq-dogantarosu.note: Added in DQ X Ver. 7.0 as an incantation for the Ryūjutsushi (learned through a skill).

dq-corallain.desc: An incantation that slams a torrent of water into multiple enemies to damage them.
dq-corallain.note: First appeared in DQ VII (all enemies). In DQ X it is a Pirate incantation, with the target and the area around it affected. It looks like a water torrent, but in DQ X it is treated as Wind (sources do not agree on its element in DQ VII). Its MP cost is 20 in DQ X.

dq-meirusutoromu.desc: An incantation that catches enemies in a swirling current of water to damage them.
dq-meirusutoromu.note: First appeared in DQ VII (one group of enemies). In DQ X it is a Pirate incantation that targets the surrounding enemies. It is enemy-only in DQ IV. It looks like a water current, but sources treat it as a Wind line and Wind element. Its MP cost is 24 in DQ X.

dq-iomata.desc: An incantation that sets off explosions at random, many times, on enemies within range.
dq-iomata.note: Confirmed in only one source. In the numbered series, the Sage learns it in DQ X (treated as Light in DQ X). The "-mata" lines first appeared in Dragon Quest Monsters: Joker 3.

dq-grandcross.desc: Attacks one group of enemies with a cross of light. Its power does not depend on Wisdom.
dq-grandcross.note: In DQ VIII it is treated as an incantation that Angelo learns. In games such as DQ VI it is a special skill, so it is listed here as a DQ VIII incantation. Its element is not confirmed in sources. The DQ VIII MP cost is not listed because sources disagree (20, 24 and 50).

dq-nifuramu.desc: Banishes enemies with light. They do not count as defeated, so no experience is gained.
dq-nifuramu.note: First appeared in DQ III. It appears in DQ IV through DQ VII, DQ XI, the HD-2D remake of DQ II, and others. Depending on the game, it targets one group of enemies up to all enemies.

dq-bashirura.desc: Blows one enemy far away and drives it out of the battle.
dq-bashirura.note: First appeared in DQ III. It appears in DQ VI, DQ VII, the HD-2D remake of DQ II, and others. It is enemy-only in DQ VIII.

dq-behoimu.desc: Restores more HP to one ally than Behoimi does.
dq-behoimu.note: First appeared in DQ IX. It appears in DQ X, DQ XI, the HD-2D remakes of DQ I and DQ III, and others. Sources treat it as a mid-tier healing incantation like Behoimi, with a recovery amount greater than Behoimi's and less than Behoma's.

dq-rihoimi.desc: Restores one ally's HP little by little over a period of time.
dq-rihoimi.note: In the numbered series it appears in DQ X, DQ XI, and the HD-2D remakes of DQ I and DQ II. It first appeared in the Monsters series.

dq-ribehoimi.desc: An upgraded version of Rihoimi with a larger recovery-over-time amount.
dq-ribehoimi.note: It appears in DQ X and DQ XI (in DQ XI, Sylvando learns it). Its MP cost is 8 in DQ XI.

dq-ribehoimu.desc: The highest tier of the recovery-over-time line, restoring a large amount of HP continuously.
dq-ribehoimu.note: First appeared in DQ X. It also appears in DQ XI.

dq-zao.desc: Revives one fallen ally with minimal HP (the success rate is low in some games).
dq-zao.note: First appeared in DQ X (revives with 1 HP). It also appears in the HD-2D remakes of DQ II and DQ III. It is a tier below Zaoraru (the existing tier number of Zaoraru has not been changed).

dq-megazaru.desc: Sacrifices the caster's life to revive the whole party and fully restore their HP.
dq-megazaru.note: First appeared in DQ IV. It appears in every game from DQ V through DQ XI.

dq-zameha.note: First appeared in DQ III. It appears in DQ IV, DQ IX, DQ X, DQ XI, the HD-2D remake of DQ II, and others. Depending on the game, it targets one ally or all allies.

dq-kiararu.note: First appeared in the Monsters series. In the numbered series it appears in DQ XI (Rab learns it).

dq-mahori.desc: Restores one ally whose spells were sealed by Mahotōn or the like.
dq-mahori.note: First appeared in DQ X. It also appears in the HD-2D remakes of DQ II and DQ III.

dq-manuha.desc: Cures one ally who has been dazed by illusions from Manūsa or the like.
dq-manuha.note: It appears in DQ X and DQ XI. Its MP cost is 2 in DQ XI as well.

dq-baishion.desc: Raises allies' attack power slightly. The increase is smaller than Baikiruto's.
dq-baishion.note: In the numbered series it appears in DQ X and DQ XI (both target one ally). In Dragon Quest Monsters: Joker it targets all allies. Its MP cost is 4 in DQ XI.

dq-zusshido.desc: Makes one ally heavier, making it easier to push enemies back and harder to be pushed.
dq-zusshido.note: A DQ X spell (an effect unique to DQ X, where characters push against each other).

dq-baha.desc: Reduces the damage one ally takes from breath attacks such as flames and blizzards.
dq-baha.note: First appeared in DQ IX (main series). It appears in DQ X and DQ XI. It is the single-target version of Fubāha.

dq-mahosute.desc: Nullifies every spell cast on you, whether from allies or enemies.
dq-mahosute.note: First appeared in DQ IV. It appears in DQ X, the HD-2D remakes of DQ I and DQ II, and others. Depending on the game, it targets self or one ally. Its MP cost is 4 in DQ X.

dq-mahotan.desc: Reflects spells aimed at you back at the caster.
dq-mahotan.note: First appeared in DQ VI. It appears in DQ VII and DQ X (in DQ X it reflects only once). It is treated as a separate line from Mahokanta. Its MP cost is 3 in DQ X.

dq-mahobaria.desc: Greatly reduces the damage the whole party takes from attack spells.
dq-mahobaria.note: It appears in DQ IX. It reduces more than Majikkubaria. Confirmed in one source plus Wikipedia.

dq-asutoron.desc: Turns the body to steel so you take no attacks, but you cannot act in the meantime.
dq-asutoron.note: First appeared in DQ III. It appears in DQ IV, DQ VI, DQ VII, DQ XI, the HD-2D remake of DQ II, and others (it is enemy-only in DQ V). Depending on the game, it targets the whole party or one member.

dq-mahokite.desc: Puts you in a state where you recover MP equal to the MP cost of any spell you receive.
dq-mahokite.note: First appeared in DQ V. It appears in DQ VI, DQ VII, DQ X, the HD-2D remake of DQ II, and others. Its user is confirmed in only one source.

dq-bomie.desc: Lowers the speed of one enemy.
dq-bomie.note: First appeared in Monsters. In the numbered series it appears in DQ IX, DQ X and DQ XI. It is the single-target version of Bomiosu.

dq-henatoru.desc: Lowers the attack power of enemies within range; the multi-target version of Henatosu.
dq-henatoru.note: First appeared in Dragon Quest Monsters: Joker 3. In the numbered series it appears in DQ X.

dq-divainsuperu.desc: Lowers enemies' resistance to spells, making attack spells work more easily.
dq-divainsuperu.note: First appeared in DQ VIII. It also appears in DQ IX, DQ X and DQ XI. Depending on the game, it targets one enemy up to an area.

dq-medapanima.desc: An upgraded version of Medapani that confuses more enemies.
dq-medapanima.note: First appeared in DQ VIII. It also appears in DQ IX, DQ X and DQ XI. Depending on the game, it targets one group of enemies up to all enemies.

dq-pesukatore.desc: Seals the dancing of one group of enemies so they cannot use dance-type actions.

dq-vereno.note: Added in DQ X Ver. 5.5. The DQ X MP cost is not listed because sources disagree (3 and 6).

dq-verenoma.desc: Inflicts strong poison (deadly poison) on enemies within range.

dq-kumono.desc: Sets up a barrier on the ground that immobilizes enemies who enter it.

dq-majasutisu.desc: Cancels all buffs and other support effects on one enemy.
dq-majasutisu.note: Appears in DQ VII (the hero learns it).

dq-gigajatisu.desc: Cancels the support effects on everyone, allies and enemies alike, and prevents casting spells for a while.
dq-gigajatisu.note: Appears in DQ VII. It is a step above Majasutisu.

dq-mahoageru.desc: Gives some of your own MP to one ally.
dq-mahoageru.note: Appears in DQ VIII (Yangus learns it).

dq-mahoyazun.desc: Splits part of your own MP evenly among all the other allies.
dq-mahoyazun.note: In the numbered series it was added in the HD-2D remake of DQ II (the Princess of Cannock; activating it has conditions). It first appeared in Dragon Quest Monsters: Joker. The MP cost is not listed because sources disagree ("half of remaining MP" and "0").

dq-toramana.desc: Protects against the harm of damaging floors such as poison swamps and barriers.
dq-toramana.note: First appeared in DQ II. It appears in DQ III through DQ VII, DQ IX, the HD-2D remakes of DQ I through DQ III, and others.

dq-ranaruta.note: First appeared in DQ III. It also appears in games such as DQ IV and DQ V.

dq-abakamu.desc: Opens locked doors (some doors will not open).
dq-abakamu.note: First appeared in DQ II. It also appears in DQ III.

dq-remuoru.desc: Makes the whole party temporarily invisible.

dq-furomi.desc: Tells you the name of your current location or the floor of the dungeon you are on.
dq-furomi.note: First appeared in DQ VI. It also appears in DQ VII.

dq-remirama.desc: Makes items and money lying nearby glow, showing where they are.
dq-remirama.note: First appeared in DQ VI. It appears in DQ VII, DQ X, the HD-2D remakes of DQ I through DQ III, and others.

blizzardo.note: Black Magic Lv1. It can also be switched to target all enemies (Super Famicom version).

blizzara.note: Black Magic Lv3. It can also be switched to target all enemies (Super Famicom version).

blizzaga.note: Black Magic Lv5. It can also be switched to target all enemies (Super Famicom version).

fire.note: Black Magic Lv1. It can also be switched to target all enemies (Super Famicom version).

fira.note: Black Magic Lv3. It can also be switched to target all enemies (Super Famicom version).

firaga.note: Black Magic Lv5. It can also be switched to target all enemies (Super Famicom version).

thunder.note: Black Magic Lv1. It can also be switched to target all enemies (Super Famicom version).

thundara.note: Black Magic Lv3. It can also be switched to target all enemies (Super Famicom version).

thundaga.note: Black Magic Lv5. It can also be switched to target all enemies (Super Famicom version).

aero.note: In FF V it is Blue Magic, not White or Black Magic (learned by Learning an enemy's ability). Sources describe it as Wind damage to a single target or all targets.

aerora.note: In FF V it is Blue Magic (learned by Learning).

cure.note: White Magic Lv1. It can also be switched to target all allies (Super Famicom version).

cura.note: White Magic Lv3. It can also be switched to target all allies (Super Famicom version). The second tier in the Famicom version of FF I is written "Kearua."

curaga.note: White Magic Lv5. It can also be switched to target all allies (Super Famicom version).

protect.note: White Magic Lv2. It reduces the physical damage taken.

haste.note: Time Magic Lv2 (not White Magic). The all-allies version is Heisuga.

sleep.note: Black Magic Lv2. It can also be switched to target all enemies (Super Famicom version).

raise.note: White Magic Lv3. It revives with only a little HP.

arise.note: White Magic Lv6. It revives with full HP.

ff-libra.desc: Examines an enemy's level, HP, weaknesses and more.

ff-poisona.note: White Magic Lv1. Sources differ on its target: single target, or switchable between single and all.

ff-silence.desc: Silences the target, sealing its magic.
ff-silence.note: White Magic Lv2. It can also be switched to target all (Super Famicom version).

ff-mini.note: White Magic Lv2. It can also be switched to target all (Super Famicom version).

ff-blink.desc: Creates an afterimage that lets the target dodge several physical attacks.

ff-esuna.desc: Cures many status ailments at once, including poison, petrification, silence and confusion.

ff-reflect.desc: Reflects magic aimed at the target back at its caster.

ff-berserk.desc: Raises attack power, but the target stops taking orders and keeps attacking.
ff-berserk.note: White Magic Lv5. It is treated as a status change (Berserk).

ff-holy.desc: A powerful attack spell of the Holy element.
ff-holy.note: White Magic Lv6. It is the only full-fledged attack spell in White Magic.

ff-dispel.desc: Removes the support effects on the target.

ff-toad.desc: Turns the target into a frog.
ff-toad.note: Black Magic Lv2. It can also be switched to target all (Super Famicom version).

ff-drain.desc: Drains the target's HP and gives it to the caster.

ff-bio.desc: Deals Poison damage and also poisons the target.
ff-bio.note: Black Magic Lv4. Its element in the game is "Poison." It can also be switched to target all enemies (Super Famicom version).

ff-slowga.desc: Slows the actions of all enemies.
ff-slowga.note: Time Magic Lv4. The all-enemies version of Surou.

ff-hastega.desc: Speeds up the actions of the whole party.
ff-hastega.note: Time Magic Lv5. The all-allies version of Heisuto.

ff-regen.desc: Puts the target in a state where HP recovers little by little for a period of time.

ff-mute.desc: Makes everyone present unable to cast magic.
ff-mute.note: Time Magic Lv2. It affects allies and enemies alike.

ff-float.desc: Lifts the target into the air so it can avoid ground-based attacks such as earthquakes.
ff-float.note: Time Magic Lv2. It can also be switched to target all (Super Famicom version).

ff-gravity.desc: Cuts a percentage of the target's current HP.
ff-gravity.note: Time Magic Lv3. Percentage damage from gravity.

ff-graviga.desc: Cuts a larger percentage of the target's HP than Gurabide.

ff-stop.desc: Stops the target's time so it cannot act.

ff-teleport.desc: Escapes from a dungeon or similar place.
ff-teleport.note: Time Magic Lv3. In battle it can also be used to flee.

ff-comet.desc: Drops a meteorite to deal Non-elemental damage.

ff-old.desc: Ages the target, gradually lowering its stats.

ff-meteor.desc: Rains multiple meteorites on all enemies at random.

ff-quick.desc: Lets the caster act again right away.

ff-banish.desc: Sends the target into another dimension, removing it.

ff-aeroga.note: Blue Magic. Learned by being hit by an enemy's ability (Learning).

ff-speed.desc: Slows the flow of time across the whole battle, giving you room to choose commands.
ff-speed.note: Time Magic Lv1. Its target is the battle itself (no distinction between allies and enemies).

ff-return.desc: Restarts the battle from its initial state.
ff-return.note: Time Magic Lv4. Its target is the battle itself.

ff-chocobo.desc: Calls a Chocobo, which kicks one enemy for Non-elemental damage.
ff-chocobo.note: Summon Magic Lv1. Occasionally a Fat Chocobo appears and attacks all enemies.

ff-sylph.desc: Drains one enemy's HP and uses it to heal the whole party.

ff-remora.desc: Clings to one enemy and paralyzes it.
ff-remora.note: Summon Magic Lv1. F-navi lists its effect as Slow, but the other two sources say paralysis.

ff-shiva.desc: Deals Ice damage to all enemies.
ff-shiva.note: Summon Magic Lv2. Its attack is called "Diamond Dust."

ff-ramuh.desc: Deals Lightning damage to all enemies.
ff-ramuh.note: Summon Magic Lv2. Its attack is called "Judgment Bolt."

ff-ifrit.desc: Deals Fire damage to all enemies.
ff-ifrit.note: Summon Magic Lv2. Its attack is called "Hellfire."

ff-titan.desc: Deals Earth damage to all enemies (it does not work on floating enemies).
ff-titan.note: Summon Magic Lv3. Its attack is called "Earthen Wrath."

ff-golem.desc: Raises a wall that blocks physical attacks on the whole party up to a set amount.
ff-golem.note: Summon Magic Lv3. Its attack is called "Earth Wall."

ff-catoblepas.note: Summon Magic Lv3. Its attack is called "Demon's Eye."

ff-carbuncle.desc: Casts Rifureku on the whole party.
ff-carbuncle.note: Summon Magic Lv4. Its attack is called "Ruby Light."

ff-syldra.desc: Deals Wind damage to all enemies.
ff-syldra.note: Summon Magic Lv4. Its attack is called "Thunderstorm," but its element is Wind.

ff-odin.desc: Instantly kills all enemies with Zantetsuken. If it fails, it deals heavy damage to one enemy instead.
ff-odin.note: Summon Magic Lv4. Its attacks are called "Zantetsuken" and "Gungnir."

ff-phoenix.desc: Fully revives one fallen ally and deals Fire damage to all enemies.
ff-phoenix.note: Summon Magic Lv5. Its attack is called "Flames of Rebirth." It targets one ally and all enemies.

ff-leviathan.desc: Deals Water damage to all enemies.
ff-leviathan.note: Summon Magic Lv5. Its attack is called "Tidal Wave."

ff-bahamut.desc: Deals heavy Non-elemental damage to all enemies.
ff-bahamut.note: Summon Magic Lv5. Its attack is called "Megaflare."

ff-doom.desc: Places a death sentence on the target, which incapacitates it when the count reaches 0.
ff-doom.note: Blue Magic (learned by Learning an enemy's ability). It works on undead as well.

ff-roulette.desc: Picks one random target from everyone, allies and enemies, and instantly kills it.
ff-roulette.note: Blue Magic (learned by Learning an enemy's ability). The target is one random unit among all allies and enemies.

ff-aquabreath.desc: Damages all enemies, and works especially well on enemies that live in deserts.
ff-aquabreath.note: Blue Magic (learned by Learning an enemy's ability). Despite the name, it is Non-elemental, not Water.

ff-lv5death.desc: Instantly kills every enemy whose level is a multiple of 5.
ff-lv5death.note: Blue Magic (learned by Learning an enemy's ability).

ff-lv4graviga.desc: Cuts a large percentage of the HP of every enemy whose level is a multiple of 4.
ff-lv4graviga.note: Blue Magic (learned by Learning an enemy's ability).

ff-lv2old.desc: Ages every enemy whose level is a multiple of 2.
ff-lv2old.note: Blue Magic (learned by Learning an enemy's ability).

ff-lv3flare.desc: Deals Furea-equivalent damage to every enemy whose level is a multiple of 3.
ff-lv3flare.note: Blue Magic (learned by Learning an enemy's ability).

ff-frogsong.desc: Turns the target into a frog.
ff-frogsong.note: Blue Magic (learned by Learning an enemy's ability). Some sources write it in hiragana as "かえるのうた."

ff-tinysong.note: Blue Magic (learned by Learning an enemy's ability).

ff-flash.desc: Blinds all enemies with a bright light.
ff-flash.note: Blue Magic (learned by Learning an enemy's ability).

ff-timeslip.desc: Ages the target and also puts it to sleep.
ff-timeslip.note: Blue Magic (learned by Learning an enemy's ability).

ff-moonflute.desc: Puts the whole party in Berserk.
ff-moonflute.note: Blue Magic (learned by Learning an enemy's ability). Like the White Magic Bāsaku, it is a status change (Berserk).

ff-deathclaw.desc: Reduces the target's HP to near death and paralyzes it.
ff-deathclaw.note: Blue Magic (learned by Learning an enemy's ability).

ff-flamethrower.note: Blue Magic (learned by Learning an enemy's ability).

ff-goblinpunch.desc: Deals Non-elemental damage on par with a normal attack, with much greater power when the target is at the same level as the caster.
ff-goblinpunch.note: Blue Magic (learned by Learning an enemy's ability).

ff-darkspark.note: Blue Magic (learned by Learning an enemy's ability).

ff-guardoff.desc: Lowers the target's defense and magic defense.
ff-guardoff.note: Blue Magic (learned by Learning an enemy's ability).

ff-transfusion.desc: The caster is incapacitated, but one ally's HP and MP are fully restored.
ff-transfusion.note: Blue Magic (learned by Learning an enemy's ability).

ff-mindblast.desc: Deals damage and inflicts paralysis and a state where HP keeps dropping.
ff-mindblast.note: Blue Magic (learned by Learning an enemy's ability).

ff-vampire.desc: Drains the target's HP and gives it to the caster.
ff-vampire.note: Blue Magic (learned by Learning an enemy's ability).

ff-magichammer.note: Blue Magic (learned by Learning an enemy's ability).

ff-mightyguard.desc: Casts Purotesu, Sheru and Rebiteto on the whole party at once.
ff-mightyguard.note: Blue Magic (learned by Learning an enemy's ability).

ff-exploder.desc: Deals damage equal to the caster's current HP to one enemy, and the caster is incapacitated.
ff-exploder.note: Blue Magic (learned by Learning an enemy's ability).

ff-hatena.desc: Deals damage equal to the caster's max HP minus its current HP.
ff-hatena.note: Blue Magic (learned by Learning an enemy's ability). Its name is four question marks (some sources write "????" in half-width characters).

ff-1000needles.note: Blue Magic (learned by Learning an enemy's ability).

ff-whitewind.desc: Restores the whole party's HP by an amount equal to the caster's current HP.
ff-whitewind.note: Blue Magic (learned by Learning an enemy's ability).

ff-missile.desc: Deals percentage damage that cuts 3/4 of the target's current HP.
ff-missile.note: Blue Magic (learned by Learning an enemy's ability).

ff1-dia.desc: Damages only undead enemies, all at once.
ff1-dia.note: White Magic Lv1. It does not work on non-undead enemies. Pidorio.com lists its element as Holy, while the other sources do not give one (the element is confirmed in only one source). gcgx says the Red Mage and Knight can also learn it.

ff1-basanda.desc: Reduces the Lightning damage the whole party takes.
ff1-basanda.note: White Magic Lv2. The amount of reduction differs by source: 1/4 (Pidorio.com) or half (bhdaa).

ff1-inbiji.desc: Makes one ally harder to see, raising its evasion.

ff1-kearua.desc: Restores more of one ally's HP than Kearu.
ff1-kearua.note: White Magic Lv3. The Famicom version writes it as "Kearua," not "Kearura."

ff1-adia.desc: Deals more damage than Dia to all undead enemies.
ff1-adia.note: White Magic Lv3. It does not work on non-undead enemies. As with Dia, its element is confirmed in only one source.

ff1-bafai.desc: Reduces the Fire damage the whole party takes.

ff1-hiiru.desc: Restores a little HP to the whole party.
ff1-hiiru.note: White Magic Lv3. An all-allies heal in a separate line from the single-target Kearu line.

ff1-fiaa.desc: Frightens all enemies so they flee.

ff1-bakorudo.desc: Reduces the cold damage the whole party takes.

ff1-bokyaru.note: White Magic Lv4. Sources differ on which jobs can learn it, so the listing follows what most sources agree on.

ff1-kearuda.desc: Restores a large amount of one ally's HP.
ff1-kearuda.note: White Magic Lv5. The Famicom version writes it as "Kearuda" (the third of four tiers: Kearu, Kearua, Kearuda, Kearuga).

ff1-dadia.desc: Deals even more damage to all undead enemies.
ff1-dadia.note: White Magic Lv5. It does not work on non-undead enemies. As with Dia, its element is confirmed in only one source.

ff1-hiira.desc: Restores more HP to the whole party than Hīru.

ff1-daterepo.desc: Escapes from a dungeon, taking the whole party outside.
ff1-daterepo.note: White Magic Lv6. The target is left blank because sources differ: "self" (Pidorio.com) and "all allies" (gcgx).

ff1-purotea.note: White Magic Lv6. It is the all-allies version of Purotesu.

ff1-inbia.note: White Magic Lv6. It is the all-allies version of Inbiji. The amount of increase differs by source: 20 (Pidorio.com) or 40 (gcgx, bhdaa).

ff1-gadia.desc: Deals the greatest damage to all undead enemies.
ff1-gadia.note: White Magic Lv7. It does not work on non-undead enemies. As with Dia, its element is confirmed in only one source.

ff1-bamajiku.desc: Grants the whole party resistance to instant death, mental and Earth attacks.
ff1-bamajiku.note: White Magic Lv7. The target is all allies in gcgx and bhdaa, but a single target in Pidorio.com. Pidorio.com lists only "instant death resistance."

ff1-rahiira.desc: Restores a large amount of HP to the whole party.

ff1-baoru.desc: Grants one ally resistance to all elements.

ff1-sheipu.note: Black Magic Lv1. gcgx says it has no effect because of a bug.

ff1-sutorai.desc: A spell meant to raise one ally's attack power.
ff1-sutorai.note: Black Magic Lv2. Many sources say it has no effect in the Famicom version because of a bug (Pidorio.com, gcgx). Pidorio.com lists its target as self.

ff1-hoorudo.note: Black Magic Lv3. The target is a single enemy in gcgx and bhdaa, but all enemies in Pidorio.com.

ff1-sheira.desc: Lowers the evasion of all enemies.
ff1-sheira.note: Black Magic Lv3. The all-enemies version of Sheipu. gcgx says that, because of a bug, it actually raises enemy evasion.

ff1-suripura.desc: Puts one enemy to sleep with high reliability.
ff1-suripura.note: Black Magic Lv4. A single-target, stronger version of Suripuru (all enemies).

ff1-kurauda.desc: Instantly kills all enemies with a poison mist.
ff1-kurauda.note: Black Magic Lv5. Sources differ on which jobs can learn it, so the listing follows what most sources agree on.

ff1-rasurou.desc: Reduces the number of times one enemy attacks.
ff1-rasurou.note: Black Magic Lv5. A single-target, stronger version of Surou (all enemies).

ff1-sangaa.desc: Attacks all enemies with powerful lightning.
ff1-sangaa.note: Black Magic Lv6. The third Lightning tier in the Famicom version is "Sangā," not "Sandaga."

ff1-kueiku.desc: Splits the ground to instantly kill all enemies.
ff1-kueiku.note: Black Magic Lv6. A spell that causes instant death rather than damage (Earth element).

ff1-sutan.note: Black Magic Lv6. Pidorio.com says it always works on enemies with 300 HP or less.

ff1-seebaa.desc: A spell meant to raise the caster's attack power and accuracy.
ff1-seebaa.note: Black Magic Lv7. Many sources say it has no effect in the Famicom version because of a bug (Pidorio.com, gcgx). Pidorio.com says the Black Mage can also learn it.

ff1-burain.note: Black Magic Lv7. Pidorio.com says only the Black Mage can learn it.

ff1-furea.desc: Deals heavy Non-elemental damage to all enemies.
ff1-furea.note: Black Magic Lv8. The Famicom version writes it as "Fureā," not "Furea."

ff1-kiru.note: Black Magic Lv8. Pidorio.com says it always works on enemies with 300 HP or less.

ff2-basuna.desc: Cures status ailments that wear off when the battle ends, such as sleep, paralysis and confusion.
ff2-basuna.note: White Magic. The target can be switched between single and all (with all, the effect is spread out). The higher the proficiency, the more ailments it can cure.

ff2-anchi.note: White Magic. The target can be switched between single and all (with all, the effect is spread out).

ff2-baria.desc: Raises a barrier that blocks elemental attacks.
ff2-baria.note: White Magic. The target can be switched between single and all (with all, the effect is spread out). ffx says it "defends against special attacks."

ff2-wooru.desc: Raises a wall that blocks magic.
ff2-wooru.note: White Magic. The target can be switched between single and all (with all, the effect is spread out). ffx says "in the Famicom version it blocks only Black Magic," while Pidorio.com says it "grants elemental defense according to proficiency."

ff2-foogu.desc: Makes the target forget, so it cannot use magic or special attacks.
ff2-foogu.note: White Magic. The target can be switched between single and all (with all, the effect is spread out).

ff2-chenji.desc: Swaps the caster's HP and MP with the target's.
ff2-chenji.note: White Magic. The target can be switched between single and all (with all, the effect is spread out).

ff2-arutema.desc: The ultimate spell, dealing Non-elemental damage with ancient power.
ff2-arutema.note: White Magic. The target can be switched between single and all (with all, the effect is spread out). In the Famicom version its power barely grows even as proficiency rises. Sources differ on its damage: about 100 (a game guide article) or about 150 (ffx). It cannot be bought in shops and is obtained in the Tower of Mysidia.

ff2-kaazu.desc: Curses the target, lowering its stats.
ff2-kaazu.note: Black Magic. The target can be switched between single and all (with all, the effect is spread out). Pidorio.com says it "halves the stats."

ff2-oora.desc: Gives a weapon power that is especially effective against a particular species.
ff2-oora.note: Black Magic. The target can be switched between single and all (with all, the effect is spread out). Pidorio.com says it "gives a weapon species-specific traits," while ffx says it "adds an element to physical attacks."

ff3-buraina.note: White Magic Lv3. In the previous game, FF I, it was written "Burana."

ff3-torunedo.desc: Uses a tornado to cut the target's HP down to near death in one stroke.
ff3-torunedo.note: White Magic Lv8. The target can be switched between single and all.

ff3-sheido.note: Black Magic Lv4. The target can be switched between single and all. Pidorio.com does not include the Red Mage (gcgx does).

ff3-ireesu.note: Black Magic Lv5. The target can be switched between single and all. gcgx says it "cancels support magic."

ff3-burekuga.desc: Turns the target to stone immediately.
ff3-burekuga.note: Black Magic Lv7. The upgraded version of Bureiku (which petrifies gradually).

ff3-esukepu.desc: Calls a Chocobo. The Conjurer flees from battle, while the Magus and Sage have it attack one enemy with a Chocobo Kick.
ff3-esukepu.note: Summon Magic Lv1. The one summoned is Chokobo (the spell name and the summoned creature's name are different). The random Black effect of the Conjurer is "nothing happens."

ff3-aisun.desc: Calls Shiva. The effect changes with the job using it, such as putting all enemies to sleep or attacking with cold.
ff3-aisun.note: Summon Magic Lv2. The one summoned is Shiva (the spell name and the summoned creature's name are different). Conjurer, White effect: puts all enemies to sleep. Black: damages one enemy (Ice per Pidorio.com, Non-elemental per Hyōri Ittai). Magus and Sage: Ice damage to all enemies.

ff3-suparuku.desc: Calls Ramuu. The effect changes with the job using it, such as paralyzing all enemies or attacking with lightning.
ff3-suparuku.note: Summon Magic Lv3. The one summoned is Ramuu (the spell name and the summoned creature's name are different). Conjurer, White effect: paralyzes all enemies. Black: Lightning damage to one enemy. Magus and Sage: Lightning damage to all enemies.

ff3-hiitora.desc: Calls Ifurīto. The effect changes with the job using it, such as healing the whole party or attacking with fire.
ff3-hiitora.note: Summon Magic Lv4. The one summoned is Ifurīto (the spell name and the summoned creature's name are different). Conjurer, White effect: restores HP to the whole party. Black: Fire damage to one enemy. Magus and Sage: Fire damage to all enemies.

ff3-haipa.desc: Calls Taitan. When used by the Magus or Sage, it attacks all enemies with the power of the earth.
ff3-haipa.note: Summon Magic Lv5. The one summoned is Taitan (the spell name and the summoned creature's name are different). Conjurer, White and Black effects: both deal Non-elemental damage to one enemy. Magus and Sage: Earth damage to all enemies.

ff3-katasuto.desc: Calls Ōdin. The effect changes with the job using it, such as raising a magic-reflecting wall over the whole party or cutting down all enemies.
ff3-katasuto.note: Summon Magic Lv6. The one summoned is Ōdin (the spell name and the summoned creature's name are different). Conjurer, White effect: raises a wall over the whole party that reflects magic once. Black: damages one enemy. Magus and Sage: instantly kills all enemies.

ff3-ribaia.desc: Calls Ribaiasan. The effect changes with the job using it, such as petrifying all enemies or attacking all enemies.
ff3-ribaia.note: Summon Magic Lv7. The one summoned is Ribaiasan (the spell name and the summoned creature's name are different). Conjurer, White effect: petrifies all enemies. Black: Wind damage to all enemies. Magus and Sage: Lightning damage to all enemies (as the sources state).

ff3-bahamuru.desc: Calls Bahamūto. When used by the Magus or Sage, it deals heavy Non-elemental damage to all enemies.
ff3-bahamuru.note: Summon Magic Lv8. The one summoned is Bahamūto (the spell name and the summoned creature's name are different). Conjurer, White effect: raises the whole party's number of attacks. Black: instantly kills one enemy. Magus and Sage: Non-elemental damage to all enemies.

ff4-pookii.desc: Turns the target into a pig. Used on an ally who is a pig, it restores them.
ff4-pookii.note: Black Magic. The target can be switched between single and all. Its user is confirmed in only one source.

ff4-doragon.desc: Calls the Mist Dragon, which attacks all enemies with its breath. Its power is determined by the user's current HP.

ff4-asura.desc: Calls Asura, who casts one of Kearuda, Reizu or Purotesu on the whole party.
ff4-asura.note: Summon Magic. Obtained by fighting in the Town of the Eidolons.

ff4-ribaia.desc: Calls Rivaia, who attacks all enemies with a tidal wave.
ff4-ribaia.note: Summon Magic. It is written "Rivaia" in the game.

ff4-goburin.desc: Calls Goburin, who attacks one enemy.
ff4-goburin.note: Summon Magic. Learned by using the summon item "Goburin."

ff4-bomu.desc: Calls Bomu, who explodes to deal heavy damage to one enemy.
ff4-bomu.note: Summon Magic. Learned by using the summon item "Bomu." The damage is determined by the user's current HP.

ff4-kokatorisu.desc: Calls Kokatorisu, who petrifies one enemy.
ff4-kokatorisu.note: Summon Magic. Learned by using the summon item "Kokatorisu."

ff4-maindof.desc: Calls Mind Flayer (Maindofurea), who damages and paralyzes one enemy.
ff4-maindof.note: Summon Magic. Learned by using the summon item "Mind Flayer." Both sources write the spell name as "MaindoF."

ff4-katon.desc: Calls up flames to attack all enemies.

ff4-suiton.desc: Attacks all enemies with a water technique.
ff4-suiton.note: Ninjutsu. Despite the name meaning water, sources all treat it as the Ice (cold) element.

ff4-raijin.note: Ninjutsu. bhdaa writes it as "雷神."

ff4-kageshibari.desc: Binds the target's shadow to paralyze it.

ff4-kemuridama.desc: Escapes from battle under cover of smoke.

ff4-bunshin.desc: Creates a clone that dodges two physical attacks.
ff4-bunshin.note: Ninjutsu. It works the same as the White Magic Burinku.

ff6-merton.desc: Deals heavy damage to all allies and enemies with a combined Fire and Wind element.
ff6-merton.note: Black Magic. Two elements, Fire and Wind (registered as fire).

ff6-reraise.desc: Puts the target in a state where it automatically revives once after being incapacitated.

ff6-imp.desc: Turns the target into a kappa (used on someone already transformed, it restores them).
ff6-imp.note: Gray Magic. Uses a new kind, "imp."

ff6-vanish.desc: Makes the target invisible so physical attacks cannot hit.

ff6-siren.note: A Magicite (Esper) summon. Its summon attack is called "Lunatic Voice" (gcgx).

ff6-midgardsormr.desc: Deals Earth damage to all enemies.
ff6-midgardsormr.note: A Magicite (Esper) summon. Its summon attack is called "Earth Surround" (gcgx).

ff6-maduin.desc: Deals Non-elemental damage to all enemies.
ff6-maduin.note: A Magicite (Esper) summon. Its summon attack is called "Chaos Wave" (gcgx).

ff6-bismarck.desc: Deals Water damage to all enemies.
ff6-bismarck.note: A Magicite (Esper) summon. Its summon attack is called "Bubble Blow" (gcgx).

ff6-caitsith.note: A Magicite (Esper) summon. Its summon attack is called "Cat Rain" (gcgx).

ff6-quetzalli.desc: The whole party performs a jump attack at once.
ff6-quetzalli.note: A Magicite (Esper) summon. Its summon attack is called "Sonic Dive" (gcgx).

ff6-valigarmanda.desc: Deals damage to all enemies with a combined Fire, Ice and Lightning element.
ff6-valigarmanda.note: A Magicite (Esper) summon. Its summon attack is called "Tri-Disaster" (gcgx).

ff6-raiden.desc: Instantly kills all enemies with a Zantetsuken more powerful than Ōdin's.
ff6-raiden.note: A Magicite (Esper) summon. Its summon attack is called "True Zantetsuken" (gcgx).

ff6-alexander.desc: Deals Holy damage to all enemies.
ff6-alexander.note: A Magicite (Esper) summon. Its summon attack is called "Holy Judgment" (gcgx).

ff6-crusader.desc: Deals heavy Non-elemental damage to all allies and enemies.
ff6-crusader.note: A Magicite (Esper) summon. Its summon attack is called "Collapse of Heaven and Earth" (gcgx). It is renamed Dūmuzudei in the Pixel Remaster.

ff6-ragnarok.desc: Turns one enemy into an item.
ff6-ragnarok.note: A Magicite (Esper) summon. Its summon attack is called "Metamorphose" (gcgx).

ff6-kirin.desc: Puts the whole party in Regen.
ff6-kirin.note: A Magicite (Esper) summon. Its summon attack is called "Holy Brighton" (gcgx).

ff6-zonaseeker.desc: Puts the whole party in Shell.
ff6-zonaseeker.note: A Magicite (Esper) summon. Its summon attack is called "Magic Shield" (gcgx).

ff6-phantom.desc: Puts the whole party in Vanish.
ff6-phantom.note: A Magicite (Esper) summon. Its summon attack is called "Vanishing Body" (gcgx).

ff6-seraph.note: A Magicite (Esper) summon. Its summon attack is called "Angel Feather" (gcgx).

ff6-unicorn.desc: Cures the whole party's status ailments.
ff6-unicorn.note: A Magicite (Esper) summon. Its summon attack is called "Heal Horn" (gcgx).

ff6-fenrir.desc: Puts the whole party in Image (clone) status.
ff6-fenrir.note: A Magicite (Esper) summon. Its summon attack is called "Howling Moon" (gcgx).

ff6-lakshmi.note: A Magicite (Esper) summon. Its summon attack is called "Enchanting Embrace" (gcgx).

ff6-cleansweep.desc: Deals Water damage to all enemies with a great wave.
ff6-cleansweep.note: A learned technique (Strago only; also called Blue Magic).

ff6-revenge.desc: Deals damage equal to the HP the user has lost.
ff6-revenge.note: A learned technique (Strago only; also called Blue Magic).

ff6-pearlwind.desc: Restores the whole party's HP by an amount equal to the user's current HP.
ff6-pearlwind.note: A learned technique (Strago only; also called Blue Magic).

ff6-l4flare.desc: Hits every enemy whose level is a multiple of 4 with Furea.
ff6-l4flare.note: A learned technique (Strago only; also called Blue Magic).

ff6-l3muddle.desc: Confuses every enemy whose level is a multiple of 3.
ff6-l3muddle.note: A learned technique (Strago only; also called Blue Magic).

ff6-reflectq.desc: Inflicts blindness, silence, slow and more on an enemy that is under Rifureku.
ff6-reflectq.note: A learned technique (Strago only; also called Blue Magic). Some sources also write it in half-width characters as "リフレク????."

ff6-lqpearl.desc: Hits enemies whose level is a multiple of the last digit of your gil with Hōrī.
ff6-lqpearl.note: A learned technique (Strago only; also called Blue Magic).

ff6-stepmine.desc: Deals damage based on the number of steps taken so far.
ff6-stepmine.note: A learned technique (Strago only; also called Blue Magic). The explanation of the formula differs by source, such as "steps divided by 32" (gcgx, opatil).

ff6-forcefield.desc: Grants immunity to damage from a randomly chosen element.
ff6-forcefield.note: A learned technique (Strago only; also called Blue Magic).

ff6-dischord.note: A learned technique (Strago only; also called Blue Magic).

ff6-sourmouth.desc: Inflicts multiple status ailments at once.
ff6-sourmouth.note: A learned technique (Strago only; also called Blue Magic).

ff6-rippler.desc: Swaps the status changes of the user and the target.
ff6-rippler.note: A learned technique (Strago only; also called Blue Magic). Uses a new kind, "status-swap."

ff6-stone.desc: Hurls stones to deal damage, sometimes confusing the target.
ff6-stone.note: A learned technique (Strago only; also called Blue Magic). Kamige Kōryaku and opatil list the target as single or all.

ff6-quasar.desc: Deals damage to all enemies that ignores magic defense.
ff6-quasar.note: A learned technique (Strago only; also called Blue Magic).

ff6-grandtrain.desc: Deals heavy damage to all enemies that ignores magic defense.
ff6-grandtrain.note: A learned technique (Strago only; also called Blue Magic).

ff7-resist.desc: Cures status ailments and makes the target immune to ailments for a while.
ff7-resist.note: The "Restore" Magic materia. opatil says single target only, while Kōryaku Daihyakka says it can be made to hit all.

ff7-quakera.desc: Deals medium damage to enemies with the power of the earth.
ff7-quakera.note: The "Earth" Magic materia. Combined with the "All" materia, it can hit all targets.

ff7-quakega.desc: Deals heavy damage to enemies with the power of the earth.
ff7-quakega.note: The "Earth" Magic materia. Combined with the "All" materia, it can hit all targets.

ff7-biora.desc: Deals medium Poison damage and also poisons the target.
ff7-biora.note: The "Poison" Magic materia. Combined with the "All" materia, it can hit all targets.

ff7-bioga.desc: Deals heavy Poison damage and also poisons the target.
ff7-bioga.note: The "Poison" Magic materia. Combined with the "All" materia, it can hit all targets.

ff7-gravira.desc: Cuts 1/2 of an enemy's current HP.

ff7-mbarrier.note: The "Barrier" Magic materia. Combined with the "All" materia, it can hit all targets.

ff7-debarrier.desc: Removes defensive effects such as Baria and Rifureku.

ff7-comet2.desc: Drops meteorites four times on random enemies for Non-elemental damage.
ff7-comet2.note: The "Comet" Magic materia. Kōryaku Daihyakka lists its cost as 24 MP (the 110 from opatil and cour89 is used).

ff7-freeze.desc: Deals Ice damage and inflicts Stop.
ff7-freeze.note: The "Seal" Magic materia. Single target only.

ff7-fullcure.note: The "Full Cure" Magic materia. Single target only.

ff7-shield.desc: Makes the target immune to physical damage and able to absorb elemental magic.

ff7-chocomog.desc: Deals Wind damage to all enemies and may inflict Stop.
ff7-chocomog.note: A Summon materia. Its summon attack is called "Special Move! / Fat Chocobo."

ff7-odin.desc: Instantly kills all enemies with Zantetsuken. Against enemies it does not work on, it deals damage with the Gungnir spear.
ff7-odin.note: A Summon materia. Its summon attack is called "Zantetsuken / Gungnir Spear."

ff7-leviathan.desc: Deals Water damage to all enemies with a great wave.
ff7-leviathan.note: A Summon materia. Its summon attack is called "Tidal Wave."

ff7-kujata.desc: Deals damage to all enemies with a combined Fire, Ice and Lightning element.
ff7-kujata.note: A Summon materia. Its summon attack is called "Tri-Disaster." Some sources list 140 MP (the 110 from Hyōri Ittai and opatil is used).

ff7-neobahamut.desc: Deals heavy damage to all enemies that ignores magic defense.
ff7-neobahamut.note: A Summon materia. Its summon attack is called "Giga Flare."

ff7-hades.desc: Deals damage to all enemies and inflicts multiple status ailments.
ff7-hades.note: A Summon materia. Its summon attack is called "Cauldron of Darkness."

ff7-typhon.desc: Deals damage to all enemies with a combined Fire, Ice, Lightning, Earth and Wind element.
ff7-typhon.note: A Summon materia. Its summon attack is called "Collapse of Heaven and Earth."

ff7-bahamutzero.desc: Deals tremendous damage to all enemies that ignores magic defense.
ff7-bahamutzero.note: A Summon materia. Its summon attack is called "Terra Flare."

ff7-kotr.desc: The Knights of the Round slash 13 times in a row, dealing heavy damage to all enemies.
ff7-kotr.note: A Summon materia. Its summon attack is called "Ultimate End."

ff7-l4suicide.desc: Cuts a large amount of HP from every enemy whose level is a multiple of 4, and shrinks them.
ff7-l4suicide.note: An enemy skill learned with the "Enemy Skill" Command materia.

ff7-angelwhisper.desc: Fully restores the target's HP and cures its status ailments.
ff7-angelwhisper.note: An enemy skill learned with the "Enemy Skill" Command materia. The target is single in Hyōri Ittai, but gameclue lists it as all.

ff7-dragonforce.note: An enemy skill learned with the "Enemy Skill" Command materia.

ff7-deathforce.desc: Makes the target immune to instant-death attacks.
ff7-deathforce.note: An enemy skill learned with the "Enemy Skill" Command materia.

ff7-flamethrower.note: An enemy skill learned with the "Enemy Skill" Command materia.

ff7-laser.desc: Cuts half of the target's current HP.
ff7-laser.note: An enemy skill learned with the "Enemy Skill" Command materia. Hyōri Ittai lists it as the Gravity element (registered as none).

ff7-matramagic.desc: Fires missiles that damage all enemies.
ff7-matramagic.note: An enemy skill learned with the "Enemy Skill" Command materia.

ff7-badbreath.desc: Inflicts poison, confusion, sleep, silence, mini and frog all at once.
ff7-badbreath.note: An enemy skill learned with the "Enemy Skill" Command materia.

ff7-beta.desc: Deals heavy Fire damage to all enemies.
ff7-beta.note: An enemy skill learned with the "Enemy Skill" Command materia.

ff7-trine.desc: Deals Lightning damage to all enemies.
ff7-trine.note: An enemy skill learned with the "Enemy Skill" Command materia.

ff7-magicbreath.desc: Deals damage to all enemies with a combined Fire, Ice and Lightning element.
ff7-magicbreath.note: An enemy skill learned with the "Enemy Skill" Command materia. A composite Fire, Ice and Lightning element (registered as none).

ff7-chocobuckle.desc: Deals damage based on the number of times you have fled from battle.
ff7-chocobuckle.note: An enemy skill learned with the "Enemy Skill" Command materia.

ff7-doom.desc: Places a death sentence on the target, which incapacitates it when the count runs out.
ff7-doom.note: An enemy skill learned with the "Enemy Skill" Command materia.

ff7-roulette.desc: Picks one random unit from allies and enemies and instantly kills it.
ff7-roulette.note: An enemy skill learned with the "Enemy Skill" Command materia.

ff7-shadowflare.note: An enemy skill learned with the "Enemy Skill" Command materia.

ff7-pandora.desc: Deals damage to all enemies that ignores magic defense.
ff7-pandora.note: An enemy skill learned with the "Enemy Skill" Command materia.

ff8-zombie.desc: Turns the target into a zombie.
ff8-zombie.note: Life Magic (classification of Jinsoku and Sheep). Uses a new kind, "zombie."

ff8-water.desc: Deals medium Water damage to one enemy.
ff8-water.note: Ice Magic (classification of Jinsoku and Sheep).

ff8-double.desc: Lets the target cast magic twice in a row in a single action.
ff8-double.note: Time Magic (classification of Jinsoku and Sheep). Uses a new kind, "multicast."

ff8-triple.desc: Lets the target cast magic three times in a row in a single action.
ff8-triple.note: Time Magic (classification of Jinsoku and Sheep).

ff8-pain.desc: Inflicts poison, silence and blindness all at once.
ff8-pain.note: Status (ST) Magic (classification of Jinsoku and Sheep).

ff8-apocalypse.desc: Deals heavy Non-elemental damage to all enemies.
ff8-apocalypse.note: It can only be used by drawing it from the final boss and casting it on the spot, and it cannot be stocked. Jinsoku classifies it as Special, and Sheep as Forbidden.

ff8-rapture.desc: Blows away all enemies and removes them from the battle.
ff8-rapture.note: A spell exclusive to Selphie's Limit Break "Slot," where it can come up. It cannot be stocked.

ff8-theend.desc: Instantly kills all enemies, ignoring resistances (it does not work on undead).
ff8-theend.note: A spell exclusive to Selphie's Limit Break "Slot," where it can come up. It cannot be stocked.

ff8-quezacotl.desc: Deals Lightning damage to all enemies.
ff8-quezacotl.note: A G.F. (Guardian Force) summon. It uses neither MP nor stock.

ff8-brothers.desc: Deals Earth damage to all enemies (it does not work on flying enemies).
ff8-brothers.note: A G.F. (Guardian Force) summon. It uses neither MP nor stock.

ff8-diablos.desc: Cuts a percentage of all enemies' HP.
ff8-diablos.note: A G.F. (Guardian Force) summon. It uses neither MP nor stock. game8 says the percentage is based on max HP.

ff8-pandemona.desc: Deals Wind damage to all enemies.
ff8-pandemona.note: A G.F. (Guardian Force) summon. It uses neither MP nor stock.

ff8-cerberus.desc: Puts the whole party in Double and Triple status.
ff8-cerberus.note: A G.F. (Guardian Force) summon. It uses neither MP nor stock.

ff8-doomtrain.desc: Deals Poison damage to all enemies and inflicts many status ailments.
ff8-doomtrain.note: A G.F. (Guardian Force) summon. It uses neither MP nor stock.

ff8-cactuar.desc: Deals damage to all enemies that ignores defense.
ff8-cactuar.note: A G.F. (Guardian Force) summon. It uses neither MP nor stock.

ff8-tonberry.note: A G.F. (Guardian Force) summon. It uses neither MP nor stock.

ff8-eden.desc: Ignores defense and deals tremendous damage to all enemies, sometimes exceeding 9999.
ff8-eden.note: A G.F. (Guardian Force) summon. It uses neither MP nor stock.

ff8-lasereye.desc: Fires a beam from the eyes to deal damage.
ff8-lasereye.note: Quistis's Limit Break "Blue Magic." It is learned by using Blue Magic items. It is available from the start.

ff8-ultrawaves.desc: Deals damage to all enemies with vibrations.
ff8-ultrawaves.note: Quistis's Limit Break "Blue Magic." It is learned by using Blue Magic items.

ff8-electrocute.desc: Deals Lightning damage to all enemies.
ff8-electrocute.note: Quistis's Limit Break "Blue Magic." It is learned by using Blue Magic items.

ff8-lvqdeath.desc: Instantly kills every enemy whose level is a multiple of the specified number.
ff8-lvqdeath.note: Quistis's Limit Break "Blue Magic." It is learned by using Blue Magic items.

ff8-degenerator.desc: Removes one enemy from the battle.
ff8-degenerator.note: Quistis's Limit Break "Blue Magic." It is learned by using Blue Magic items.

ff8-micromissiles.desc: Cuts a percentage of an enemy's current HP.
ff8-micromissiles.note: Quistis's Limit Break "Blue Magic." It is learned by using Blue Magic items.

ff8-acid.desc: Deals damage and also inflicts status ailments such as poison, blindness and silence.
ff8-acid.note: Quistis's Limit Break "Blue Magic." It is learned by using Blue Magic items.

ff8-gatlinggun.desc: Fires bullets to deal physical damage.
ff8-gatlinggun.note: Quistis's Limit Break "Blue Magic." It is learned by using Blue Magic items. A physical attack (Sheep).

ff8-firebreath.desc: Damages all enemies with a breath of fire.
ff8-firebreath.note: Quistis's Limit Break "Blue Magic." It is learned by using Blue Magic items.

ff8-badbreath.desc: Inflicts multiple status ailments on all enemies.
ff8-badbreath.note: Quistis's Limit Break "Blue Magic." It is learned by using Blue Magic items.

ff8-hominglaser.desc: Deals heavy damage with a homing beam.
ff8-hominglaser.note: Quistis's Limit Break "Blue Magic." It is learned by using Blue Magic items.

ff8-raybomb.note: Quistis's Limit Break "Blue Magic." It is learned by using Blue Magic items.

ff8-shockwavepulsar.desc: Deals heavy damage to all enemies, sometimes exceeding the 9999 cap.
ff8-shockwavepulsar.note: Quistis's Limit Break "Blue Magic." It is learned by using Blue Magic items.

ff9-faith.note: White Magic. Sources list the stat raised as "Strength" (Jinsoku) or "attack power" (opatil).

ff9-jewel.desc: Extracts a raw gemstone from an enemy.

ff9-atomos.desc: Cuts a percentage of all enemies' HP (the percentage rises with the number of amethysts you hold).
ff9-atomos.note: Summon Magic. Its summon attack is called "Gravity Object 199" (Game Eight). Until partway through the story, Garnet's MP cost is quadrupled (Jinsoku). The characters who can use it follow Jinsoku (some sources list both Garnet and Eiko).

ff9-ark.desc: Deals tremendous Darkness damage to all enemies (its power rises with the number of lapis lazuli you hold).
ff9-ark.note: Summon Magic. Its summon attack is called "Dark Fate" (Game Eight). Until partway through the story, Garnet's MP cost is quadrupled (Jinsoku). The characters who can use it follow Jinsoku (some sources list both Garnet and Eiko).

ff9-madeen.desc: Deals Holy damage to all enemies.
ff9-madeen.note: Summon Magic. Its summon attack is called "Terra Homing" (Game Eight). The characters who can use it follow Jinsoku (some sources list both Garnet and Eiko).

ff9-l4holy.desc: Deals Holy damage to every enemy whose level is a multiple of 4.
ff9-l4holy.note: Blue Magic (Quina learns it by "eating" enemies).

ff9-l3defless.desc: Lowers the defense and magic defense of every enemy whose level is a multiple of 3.
ff9-l3defless.note: Blue Magic (Quina learns it by "eating" enemies).

ff9-mightyguard.desc: Casts Sheru and Purotesu on the whole party at once.
ff9-mightyguard.note: Blue Magic (Quina learns it by "eating" enemies).

ff9-limitglove.desc: Deals 9999 damage, but only when the user's HP is 1.
ff9-limitglove.note: Blue Magic (Quina learns it by "eating" enemies).

ff9-pumpkinhead.desc: Deals damage equal to the user's max HP minus its current HP.
ff9-pumpkinhead.note: Blue Magic (Quina learns it by "eating" enemies).

ff9-night.desc: Puts all allies and enemies to sleep.
ff9-night.note: Blue Magic (Quina learns it by "eating" enemies).

ff9-twister.desc: Deals Wind damage with a wide spread, using a tornado.
ff9-twister.note: Blue Magic (Quina learns it by "eating" enemies).

ff9-earthshake.desc: Deals heavy Earth damage to all enemies with an earthquake.
ff9-earthshake.note: Blue Magic (Quina learns it by "eating" enemies).

ff9-angelsnack.desc: Uses Remedies from your inventory on the whole party to cure status ailments.
ff9-angelsnack.note: Blue Magic (Quina learns it by "eating" enemies).

ff9-frogdrop.desc: Deals damage based on Quina's level and the number of frogs caught.
ff9-frogdrop.note: Blue Magic (Quina learns it by "eating" enemies).

ff9-frost.desc: Freezes an enemy so that it shatters and is incapacitated when hit by a physical attack.
ff9-frost.note: Blue Magic (Quina learns it by "eating" enemies).

ff9-mustardbomb.desc: Puts an enemy in Heat status so that it is incapacitated when it acts.
ff9-mustardbomb.note: Blue Magic (Quina learns it by "eating" enemies).

ff10-nultide.desc: Gives the whole party a state that nullifies one Water attack.
ff10-nultide.note: White Magic. In the International version the types and effects of magic are the same, and choosing the advanced "International Sphere Grid" changes where the learning spaces are located.

ff10-watera.desc: Deals medium Water damage to one enemy.
ff10-watera.note: Black Magic. In the International version the types and effects of magic are the same, and choosing the advanced "International Sphere Grid" changes where the learning spaces are located.

ff10-waterga.desc: Deals heavy Water damage to one enemy.
ff10-waterga.note: Black Magic. In the International version the types and effects of magic are the same, and choosing the advanced "International Sphere Grid" changes where the learning spaces are located.

ff10-valefor.desc: Calls a flying bird aeon to fight.
ff10-valefor.note: Summon (a command exclusive to Yuna). You fight by directly controlling the aeon you called. The first aeon to join. The same aeons are available in the International version (the added Dark Aeons are enemy-only).

ff10-ixion.desc: Calls a lightning aeon to fight.
ff10-ixion.note: Summon (a command exclusive to Yuna). You fight by directly controlling the aeon you called. Obtained at the Djose Temple. The same aeons are available in the International version (the added Dark Aeons are enemy-only).

ff10-yojimbo.desc: Calls a bodyguard aeon, who uses techniques according to the gil you pay.
ff10-yojimbo.note: Summon (a command exclusive to Yuna). You fight by directly controlling the aeon you called. A hidden aeon. Gil is paid both when hiring him and when having him attack. The same aeons are available in the International version (the added Dark Aeons are enemy-only).

ff10-anima.desc: Calls the hidden aeon Anima to fight.
ff10-anima.note: Summon (a command exclusive to Yuna). You fight by directly controlling the aeon you called. A hidden aeon. Obtained at the Baaj Temple. The same aeons are available in the International version (the added Dark Aeons are enemy-only).

ff10-magus-sisters.desc: Calls a group of three aeons to fight.
ff10-magus-sisters.note: Summon (a command exclusive to Yuna). You fight by directly controlling the aeon you called. A hidden aeon. Obtained by meeting the conditions at the Remiem Temple. The same aeons are available in the International version (the added Dark Aeons are enemy-only).

ff11-cure2.desc: Restores a moderate amount of one ally's HP.

ff11-cure3.desc: Restores a large amount of one ally's HP.
ff11-cure3.note: White Magic. There are also higher tiers, Kearu IV through VI.

ff11-paralyze.desc: Paralyzes one enemy, sometimes preventing it from acting.

ff11-teleport-holla.desc: Instantly teleports nearby party members to the Holla rock on the La Theine Plateau.
ff11-teleport-holla.note: White Magic. There are other spells for each destination, such as Teleport-Dem and Teleport-Mea.

ff11-stone.desc: Deals damage to one enemy with the power of the earth.

ff11-firaja.desc: Deals heavy damage to the enemies around the target all at once with fire.
ff11-firaja.note: Black Magic. The "-ja" spells are area attacks above the "-ga" tier.

ff12-cleanse.note: White Magic. Disease is a state that prevents HP recovery. In The Zodiac Age it stays White Magic, and the White Mage, Red Battlemage and Knight can learn it (jobs confirmed in only one source).

ff12-esunaga.desc: Cures status ailments on the target and the allies around it all at once.
ff12-esunaga.note: White Magic. In The Zodiac Age it stays White Magic, and the White Mage and Monk can learn it (jobs confirmed in only one source).

ff12-dispelga.desc: Cancels the buffs on enemies within range.
ff12-dispelga.note: White Magic. In The Zodiac Age it stays White Magic, and the White Mage and Monk can learn it (jobs confirmed in only one source).

ff12-shock.desc: Deals heavy Non-elemental damage to one enemy.
ff12-shock.note: Black Magic. In The Zodiac Age it stays Black Magic, and the Black Mage can learn it (jobs confirmed in only one source).

ff12-ardor.desc: Deals tremendous Fire damage to enemies within range.
ff12-ardor.note: Black Magic. In The Zodiac Age it moves to Arcane Magic, and the Red Battlemage can learn it (jobs confirmed in only one source).

ff12-scathe.desc: Deals tremendous Non-elemental damage to enemies within range.
ff12-scathe.note: Black Magic. In The Zodiac Age it stays Black Magic, and the Black Mage can learn it (jobs confirmed in only one source).

ff12-immobilize.desc: Makes enemies within range unable to move.
ff12-immobilize.note: Time Magic. In The Zodiac Age it stays Time Magic, and the Time Battlemage and Red Battlemage can learn it (jobs confirmed in only one source).

ff12-disable.desc: Makes enemies within range unable to act.
ff12-disable.note: Time Magic. In FF XII, the Donaku (Disable) state lets a unit move but not act. In The Zodiac Age it stays Time Magic, and the Time Battlemage and Red Battlemage can learn it (jobs confirmed in only one source).

ff12-reflectga.desc: Raises a wall that reflects magic around the target and the allies near it.
ff12-reflectga.note: Time Magic. In The Zodiac Age it stays Time Magic, and the Time Battlemage and Machinist can learn it (jobs confirmed in only one source).

ff12-bleed.desc: Puts one enemy in a state where its HP keeps dropping rapidly.
ff12-bleed.note: Time Magic. In The Zodiac Age it stays Time Magic, and the Time Battlemage can learn it (jobs confirmed in only one source).

ff12-balance.desc: Deals damage to enemies within range equal to the difference between the caster's max HP and current HP.
ff12-balance.note: Time Magic. In The Zodiac Age it stays Time Magic, and the Black Mage and Red Battlemage can learn it (jobs confirmed in only one source).

ff12-countdown.desc: Puts one enemy in a state where its HP drops to 0 as time passes.
ff12-countdown.note: Time Magic. In The Zodiac Age it stays Time Magic, and the Time Battlemage can learn it (jobs confirmed in only one source).

ff12-protectga.desc: Raises the defense of the target and the allies around it.
ff12-protectga.note: Green Magic. In The Zodiac Age it moves to White Magic, and the White Mage, Monk and Shikari can learn it (jobs confirmed in only one source).

ff12-shellga.desc: Raises the magic defense of the target and the allies around it.
ff12-shellga.note: Green Magic. In The Zodiac Age it moves to White Magic, and the White Mage, Monk and Shikari can learn it (jobs confirmed in only one source).

ff12-blindga.desc: Blinds enemies within range, lowering their accuracy.
ff12-blindga.note: Green Magic. In The Zodiac Age it moves to Black Magic, and the Black Mage can learn it (jobs confirmed in only one source).

ff12-toxify.note: Green Magic. In The Zodiac Age it moves to Black Magic, and the Black Mage can learn it (jobs confirmed in only one source).

ff12-silencega.desc: Silences enemies within range, sealing their magic.
ff12-silencega.note: Green Magic. In The Zodiac Age it moves to Black Magic, and the Black Mage can learn it (jobs confirmed in only one source).

ff12-sleepga.desc: Puts enemies within range to sleep.
ff12-sleepga.note: Green Magic. In The Zodiac Age it moves to Black Magic, and the Black Mage and Red Battlemage can learn it (jobs confirmed in only one source).

ff12-oil.desc: Makes enemies within range take more Fire damage.
ff12-oil.note: Green Magic. In The Zodiac Age it stays Green Magic, and the White Mage, Red Battlemage, Time Battlemage, Black Mage and Machinist can learn it (jobs confirmed in only one source).

ff12-bravery.desc: Raises one ally's physical attack power.
ff12-bravery.note: Green Magic. In The Zodiac Age it moves to White Magic, and the White Mage and Red Battlemage can learn it (jobs confirmed in only one source).

ff12-dark.desc: Deals light Darkness damage to enemies within range.
ff12-dark.note: Arcane Magic. In The Zodiac Age it stays Arcane Magic, and the Red Battlemage can learn it (jobs confirmed in only one source).

ff12-darkra.desc: Deals medium Darkness damage to enemies within range.
ff12-darkra.note: Arcane Magic. In The Zodiac Age it stays Arcane Magic, and the Red Battlemage can learn it (jobs confirmed in only one source).

ff12-darkga.desc: Deals heavy Darkness damage to enemies within range.
ff12-darkga.note: Arcane Magic. In The Zodiac Age it stays Arcane Magic, and the Red Battlemage can learn it (jobs confirmed in only one source).

ff12-decoy.desc: Makes one ally a decoy that draws enemy attacks.

In The Zodiac Age it moves to Green Magic, and the White Mage, Red Battlemage, Time Battlemage, Black Mage and Machinist can learn it (jobs confirmed in only one source).

ff12-reverse.desc: Puts one ally in a state where damage taken heals and healing received damages.
ff12-reverse.note: Arcane Magic. In The Zodiac Age it moves to Green Magic, and the White Mage, Red Battlemage, Time Battlemage and Black Mage can learn it (jobs confirmed in only one source).

ff13-last-resort.desc: Uses the entire ATB gauge to deal heavy Non-elemental magic damage to enemies over a wide area.
ff13-last-resort.note: A Ravager ability. Exclusive to Hope.

ff13-ruin.desc: Deals Non-elemental magic damage to one enemy.
ff13-ruin.note: A Commando ability. Confirmed in only one source.

ff13-ruinga.desc: Deals Non-elemental magic damage to enemies within range.

ff13-bravera.desc: Greatly raises the party's physical attack power for a short time.

ff13-faithra.desc: Greatly raises the party's magic attack power for a short time.

ff13-vigilance.desc: Makes the party less likely to have their actions interrupted when hit.

ff13-enfire.desc: Adds the Fire element to the party's attacks.

ff13-enfrost.desc: Adds the Ice element to the party's attacks.

ff13-enthunder.desc: Adds the Lightning element to the party's attacks.

ff13-enwater.desc: Adds the Water element to the party's attacks.

ff13-protectra.desc: Greatly raises the party's resistance to physical attacks for a short time.

ff13-shellra.desc: Greatly raises the party's resistance to magic attacks for a short time.

ff13-imperilga.desc: Lowers the elemental resistances of enemies within range.

ff13-fogga.desc: Seals the magic of enemies within range.

ff13-painga.desc: Seals the physical attacks of enemies within range.

ff13-cursega.desc: Makes enemies within range more likely to have their actions interrupted when hit.

ff13-daze.desc: Stuns one enemy so it cannot act.

ff13-dazega.desc: Stuns enemies within range so they cannot act.

ff13-stopga.desc: Resets the ATB gauges of all allies and enemies.

ff13-brynhildr.note: Summon (TP ability). An eidolon exclusive to Sazh; when summoned it swaps places with the party and fights alongside you, and in Driving Mode it transforms into a vehicle-like form.

ff13-hecatoncheir.desc: Calls the many-armed eidolon Hekatonkeiru to fight alongside you.
ff13-hecatoncheir.note: Summon (TP ability). An eidolon exclusive to Vanille; when summoned it swaps places with the party and fights alongside you, and in Driving Mode it transforms into a vehicle-like form.

ff14-summon-bahamut.desc: Summons Demi-Bahamūto to fight alongside you.
ff14-summon-bahamut.note: A Summoner spell (learned at Lv70). It does not consume MP. Confirmed in only one source.

ff14-summon-phoenix.desc: Summons Demi-Fenikkusu to fight alongside you.

persona1-shuuraigeki.note: It has a paired spell of the same element, but they are not upper and lower tiers (Sanraigeki). Confirmed in only one source.

persona1-hikarinosabaki.desc: Deals heavy Miracle damage to multiple enemies.

persona1-delight.note: The ailment is called Blind in this game.

persona1-fukounohuladance.desc: Inflicts Bad Luck on multiple enemies with a dance.

persona1-kyouarnouta.desc: Inflicts Fear on multiple enemies with a song.

persona1-dokugasbreath.desc: Deals medium damage to multiple enemies and inflicts deadly poison.

persona1-fogbreath.desc: Deals medium damage to multiple enemies and blinds them.

persona1-dekabar.desc: Blocks one enemy's HP recovery for 3 turns.

persona1-doronpa.note: The state is called Invisible in this game. Confirmed in only one source.

persona1-droid.desc: Turns one ally into a Puppet.
persona1-droid.note: The state is called Puppet in this game. Confirmed in only one source.

persona1-quicka.desc: Puts one ally in the Counter state.

persona1-balzac.desc: Puts one ally in the Violent state.
persona1-balzac.note: The state is called Violent in this game.

persona1-madoll.desc: Puts one ally in the Runaway state.
persona1-madoll.note: The state is called Runaway in this game.

persona1-urban.desc: Puts one ally in the Wolf state.
persona1-urban.note: The state is called Wolf in this game. Confirmed in only one source.

persona1-makakaja.desc: Raises the magic power of all allies for 3 turns.

persona1-recarmdra.desc: Sacrifices the user to fully restore the HP of all allies.

persona1-penpatra.desc: Reduces the status ailments of all allies by one stage.

persona1-posumudi.desc: Cures one ally of deadly poison.

persona1-arusanga.desc: Lifts the Persona-switch ban from one ally.

persona1-honoonokabe.desc: For 3 turns, all allies absorb half of Fire magic.

persona1-suishounokabe.desc: For 3 turns, reflects magic aimed at all allies.

persona1-koutetsunokabe.desc: For 3 turns, reflects physical attacks aimed at all allies.

persona1-lunatrap.desc: Keeps enemies from escaping for 3 turns.

persona1-liftoma.desc: Negates floors that deal damage (for one full cycle of the moon).

persona1-estoma.desc: Stops you from meeting enemies of a lower level than the protagonist.

persona1-traesto.desc: Returns you to the dungeon entrance.

persona2-novasaizer.desc: Deals heavy Nuclear and Holy damage to one enemy.
persona2-novasaizer.note: A special spell exclusive to that Persona.

persona2-crescentmirror.desc: Deals heavy Almighty and Holy damage to all enemies, and may freeze them.
persona2-crescentmirror.note: A special spell exclusive to that Persona.

persona2-hierosgrypein.desc: Deals damage to all enemies, determined by the Persona's level and rank.

persona2-nirvana.desc: Uses the Holy element to instantly kill all enemies with a high chance.

persona2-alphablaster.desc: Repeatedly halves the HP of all enemies for a while.
