persona2-noroinokotoba.desc: Uses the Dark element to instantly kill all enemies with a high chance.

persona2-omegacluster.desc: Every few turns, instantly kills enemies in order, starting from the lowest level.

persona2-multidimension.desc: Ignores elements and instantly kills one enemy.
persona2-multidimension.note: The English release uses a different name (tracked separately).

persona2-anotherdimension.desc: Ignores elements and instantly kills all enemies.

persona2-poisonbreath.desc: Inflicts deadly poison on one group of enemies.

persona2-mafui.desc: Inflicts Magic Seal on one enemy, sealing its magic.
persona2-mafui.note: The ailment is called Magic Seal in this game.

persona2-magicseal.desc: Inflicts Magic Seal on one enemy. Succeeds more easily than Mafūi.

persona2-seireishoukan.note: The English-language wiki says it inflicts Magic Seal on all enemies. Here the Illusion given by Japanese strategy sites is used.

persona2-otakebi.desc: Puts all enemies in the Frenzy state.

persona2-illzone.note: The ailment is called Illusion in this game.

persona2-sunakemuri.desc: Inflicts Illusion on one enemy. Succeeds more easily than Iruzōn.

persona2-miragebreath.desc: Inflicts Illusion on one group of enemies.

persona2-sleepspell.desc: Puts one enemy to sleep. Succeeds more easily than Doruminā.

persona2-nagekiss.desc: Charms one enemy. Succeeds more easily than Marinkarin.

persona2-marvelousdance.note: The English-language wiki says it confuses all enemies. Here the Charm given by Japanese strategy sites is used.

persona2-miwakunodance.desc: Charms all enemies. Succeeds more easily than Tenjō no Mai.

persona2-yuufunnomai.desc: Greatly raises the physical and magic attack power of all allies.
persona2-yuufunnomai.note: For the kind, the closest existing key was chosen (raises attack and magic attack). The English-language wiki says it doubles them in the PS version and multiplies them by 1.5 in the PSP version.

persona2-samakaja.desc: Raises the magic defense of one ally.

persona2-balzacaia.desc: Deliberately puts one ally in the Frenzy state.

persona2-trafuri.desc: Lets you escape from battle for certain.

persona2-iyashinoshirabe.desc: Restores a little HP to all allies during battle.

persona2-jiainoinori.desc: Restores a moderate amount of HP to all allies during battle.

persona2-shouchikubai.desc: Restores HP to all allies. The amount is random, and at the maximum it also cures status ailments.

persona2-stiti.desc: Fully restores one ally's HP and cures all status ailments except Dying and Frenzy.

persona2-suristi.desc: Revives all allies who are Dying, with full HP.

persona3-ragnarok.desc: Deals massive Fire damage to one enemy.
persona3-ragnarok.note: The massive tier is a proper name without the shared stem, and only that Persona learns it. The all-enemies massive spell, Maharagidain (32 SP, Mara), was added in FES and is not in the original list. In the Reload list, the single-target massive spell is Inferuno (confirmed in only one source).

persona3-niflheim.desc: Deals massive Ice damage to one enemy and always freezes it.
persona3-niflheim.note: The massive tier is a proper name without the shared stem, and only that Persona learns it. In the Reload list, the single-target massive spell is Daiamondodasuto (confirmed in only one source).

persona3-nekodamashi.note: The ailment is called Distress in this game. The English release uses a different name (tracked separately).

persona3-barizougon.note: The ailment is called Rage in this game (it raises attack and lowers defense).

persona3-virusbreath.desc: Uses the power of poison to cut the current HP of all enemies by one quarter.
persona3-virusbreath.note: Sources describe it as proportional damage of the Poison element. Whether it also poisons the target could not be confirmed in the sources.

persona3-repatra.desc: Gets one ally back up who has been felled by Down or Slip.

persona3-burutodi.note: The English release uses a different name (tracked separately).

persona3-amrita.desc: Cures all allies of all status ailments.

persona3-rebellion.desc: Raises the critical rate of everyone, allies and enemies, for 3 turns.

persona3-revolution.desc: Greatly raises the critical rate of everyone, allies and enemies, for 3 turns.

persona4-gushanosasayaki.desc: Inflicts Seal on all enemies, sealing their magic.

persona4-aging.note: The ailment is called Aging in this game.

persona4-soulbreak.note: The ailment is called Debilitation (Suijaku) in this game.

persona4-akanokabe.desc: Gives one ally resistance to Fire for 3 turns.

persona4-shironokabe.desc: Gives one ally resistance to Ice for 3 turns.

persona4-aonokabe.desc: Gives one ally resistance to Electric for 3 turns.
persona4-aonokabe.note: The element follows Kamige Kōryaku and GameWith (Electric). Hyōri Ittai lists it as Wind.

persona4-midorinokabe.desc: Gives one ally resistance to Wind for 3 turns.
persona4-midorinokabe.note: The element follows Kamige Kōryaku and GameWith (Wind). Hyōri Ittai lists it as Electric.

pk-freeze-a.note: Mother 2. It has a certain chance to freeze enemies. In Mother 1, only Ω targets all enemies, and γ has a special effect that greatly reduces HP.

pk-freeze-b.note: Mother 2. It has a certain chance to freeze enemies. In Mother 1, only Ω targets all enemies, and γ has a special effect that greatly reduces HP.

pk-freeze-g.note: Mother 2. It has a certain chance to freeze enemies. In Mother 1, only Ω targets all enemies, and γ has a special effect that greatly reduces HP.

pk-freeze-o.note: Mother 2. It has a certain chance to freeze enemies. In Mother 1, only Ω targets all enemies, and γ has a special effect that greatly reduces HP.

pk-fire-a.note: In Mother 2 it targets one row of enemies (called a group in this site's vocabulary). In Mother 1 it targets all enemies, and PK Faiā Ω has an instant-death effect.

pk-fire-b.note: In Mother 2 it targets one row of enemies (called a group in this site's vocabulary). In Mother 1 it targets all enemies, and PK Faiā Ω has an instant-death effect.

pk-fire-g.note: In Mother 2 it targets one row of enemies (called a group in this site's vocabulary). In Mother 1 it targets all enemies, and PK Faiā Ω has an instant-death effect.

pk-fire-o.note: In Mother 2 it targets one row of enemies (called a group in this site's vocabulary). In Mother 1 it targets all enemies, and PK Faiā Ω has an instant-death effect.

pk-thunder-a.note: Mother 2. It drops one bolt of lightning on a random enemy and removes the shield of whatever it hits. Because the target is random, no scope is set.

pk-thunder-b.note: Mother 2. It drops two bolts of lightning on random enemies and removes the shield of whatever it hits. Because the target is random, no scope is set.

lifeup-o.note: Mother 2. Only Ω targets all allies. Mother 1 has five tiers, α/β/γ/π/Ω, and π and Ω are the all-allies versions.

hypnosis-a.note: In the Japanese version of Mother 2 it is Saiminjutsu α. The English release uses a different name, which cannot be confirmed in Japanese sources.

mother-pk-kiai-a.desc: An attack PSI exclusive to Ness that deals non-elemental damage to all enemies (tier α).
mother-pk-kiai-a.note: The Kiai part of the name is replaced by the name of the thing the player entered as what they think is cool at the start of the game.

mother-pk-kiai-b.desc: An attack PSI exclusive to Ness that deals non-elemental damage to all enemies (tier β).
mother-pk-kiai-b.note: The Kiai part of the name is replaced by the name of the thing the player entered as what they think is cool at the start of the game.

mother-pk-kiai-g.desc: An attack PSI exclusive to Ness that deals non-elemental damage to all enemies (tier γ).
mother-pk-kiai-g.note: The Kiai part of the name is replaced by the name of the thing the player entered as what they think is cool at the start of the game.

mother-pk-kiai-o.desc: An attack PSI exclusive to Ness that deals non-elemental damage to all enemies (tier Ω).
mother-pk-kiai-o.note: The Kiai part of the name is replaced by the name of the thing the player entered as what they think is cool at the start of the game.

mother-pk-thunder-g.desc: Drops three bolts of lightning on randomly chosen enemies.
mother-pk-thunder-g.note: Mother 2. It also removes the shield of whatever it hits. Because the target is random, no scope is set.

mother-pk-thunder-o.desc: Drops four bolts of lightning on randomly chosen enemies.
mother-pk-thunder-o.note: Mother 2. It also removes the shield of whatever it hits. PK Sandā in Mother 1 goes only up to γ, with no Ω.

mother-pk-starstorm-a.desc: Rains stars down on all enemies for heavy damage.
mother-pk-starstorm-a.note: Poo learns it through an event, not by leveling up.

mother-pk-starstorm-o.desc: Rains stars down on all enemies with more power than PK Sutāsutōmu α.
mother-pk-starstorm-o.note: In Mother 2 there are only two tiers, α and Ω. Poo learns it through an event, not by leveling up.

mother-pk-flash-a.desc: A strong light puts all enemies into states such as crying or strange.
mother-pk-flash-a.note: The game classifies it as an attack PSI, but it inflicts status changes rather than damage, so it is classified as an ailment. At higher tiers the chance of unconsciousness (instant death) rises.

mother-pk-flash-b.desc: A strong light inflicts states such as crying, strange and numbness on all enemies, and rarely knocks them unconscious.
mother-pk-flash-b.note: The game classifies it as an attack PSI, but it inflicts status changes rather than damage, so it is classified as an ailment. At higher tiers the chance of unconsciousness (instant death) rises.

mother-pk-flash-g.desc: A strong light inflicts states such as crying, strange and numbness on all enemies, and rarely knocks them unconscious.
mother-pk-flash-g.note: The game classifies it as an attack PSI, but it inflicts status changes rather than damage, so it is classified as an ailment. At higher tiers the chance of unconsciousness (instant death) rises.

mother-pk-flash-o.desc: A strong light inflicts states such as crying, strange and numbness on all enemies, and rarely knocks them unconscious.
mother-pk-flash-o.note: The game classifies it as an attack PSI, but it inflicts status changes rather than damage, so it is classified as an ailment. At higher tiers the chance of unconsciousness (instant death) rises.

mother-healing-a.desc: Cures one ally of a cold, sunstroke and sleep.

mother-healing-b.desc: Cures one ally of more ailments than α, such as poison, strange and crying.

mother-healing-g.desc: Cures one ally of nearly all status ailments, and revives an unconscious ally with a certain chance.
mother-healing-g.note: Mother 2. It also has a revival effect (the success rate is not 100%).

mother-healing-o.desc: Cures one ally's status ailments and revives them from unconsciousness for certain.
mother-healing-o.note: Mother 2. It also has a revival effect. In Mother 1 the tiers are α/β/γ/π, and recovery from unconsciousness is handled by a separate PSI, Sūpāhīringu.

mother-shield-a.desc: Puts a shield on one ally that halves damage from physical attacks.
mother-shield-a.note: Mother 2. α and Σ halve damage; β and Ω halve damage and reflect it. Σ is the all-allies version of α, and Ω is the all-allies version of β. The effect wears off after a few hits.

mother-shield-s.desc: Puts a shield on all allies that halves damage from physical attacks.
mother-shield-s.note: Mother 2. α and Σ halve damage; β and Ω halve damage and reflect it. Σ is the all-allies version of α, and Ω is the all-allies version of β. The effect wears off after a few hits. The PP cost uses the values from cour89, nJOY and kirafura (Σ 18, β 10). The gcgx list has the PP costs of Σ and β swapped.

mother-shield-b.desc: Puts a shield on one ally that halves physical damage and reflects it back at the attacker.
mother-shield-b.note: Mother 2. α and Σ halve damage; β and Ω halve damage and reflect it. Σ is the all-allies version of α, and Ω is the all-allies version of β. The effect wears off after a few hits. The PP cost uses the values from cour89, nJOY and kirafura (Σ 18, β 10). The gcgx list has the PP costs of Σ and β swapped.

mother-shield-o.desc: Puts a shield on all allies that halves physical damage and reflects it back at the attacker.
mother-shield-o.note: Mother 2. α and Σ halve damage; β and Ω halve damage and reflect it. Σ is the all-allies version of α, and Ω is the all-allies version of β. The effect wears off after a few hits.

mother-psychoshield-a.desc: Puts a shield on one ally that blocks attack PSI.
mother-psychoshield-a.note: Mother 2. α and Σ nullify attack PSI; β and Ω reflect it. Σ is the all-allies version of α, and Ω is the all-allies version of β. PK Sandā removes it. Psycho Shield in Mother 1 has two versions, α (single target) and β (all allies), and its effect is halving damage.

mother-psychoshield-s.desc: Puts a shield on all allies that blocks attack PSI.
mother-psychoshield-s.note: Mother 2. α and Σ nullify attack PSI; β and Ω reflect it. Σ is the all-allies version of α, and Ω is the all-allies version of β. PK Sandā removes it. Psycho Shield in Mother 1 has two versions, α (single target) and β (all allies), and its effect is halving damage. The PP cost uses the values from cour89, nJOY and kirafura (Σ 24, β 14). The gcgx list has the PP costs of Σ and β swapped.

mother-psychoshield-b.desc: Puts a shield on one ally that reflects attack PSI back.
mother-psychoshield-b.note: Mother 2. α and Σ nullify attack PSI; β and Ω reflect it. Σ is the all-allies version of α, and Ω is the all-allies version of β. PK Sandā removes it. Psycho Shield in Mother 1 has two versions, α (single target) and β (all allies), and its effect is halving damage. The PP cost uses the values from cour89, nJOY and kirafura (Σ 24, β 14). The gcgx list has the PP costs of Σ and β swapped.

mother-psychoshield-o.desc: Puts a shield on all allies that reflects attack PSI back.
mother-psychoshield-o.note: Mother 2. α and Σ nullify attack PSI; β and Ω reflect it. Σ is the all-allies version of α, and Ω is the all-allies version of β. PK Sandā removes it. Psycho Shield in Mother 1 has two versions, α (single target) and β (all allies), and its effect is halving damage.

mother-offenseup-a.desc: Raises the Offense (attack power) of one ally.

mother-offenseup-o.desc: Raises the Offense (attack power) of all allies.

mother-defensedown-a.desc: Lowers the Defense of one enemy.

mother-defensedown-o.desc: Lowers the Defense of all enemies.

mother-brainshock-a.desc: Makes one enemy strange, so that it acts erratically.
mother-brainshock-a.note: The status is called strange in this game. It is close to confusion, for example making the target pick the wrong target.

mother-brainshock-o.note: The status is called strange in this game. In Mother 1 the single-target version was Bureinshokku and the all-enemies version had a separate name, Bureinsaikuron.

mother-teleport-a.desc: Takes a running start and teleports instantly to a town you have visited.
mother-teleport-a.note: Mother 2. It fails if you hit an obstacle during the run-up. In Mother 1 the PSI with the same role is called Terepōtēshon. Ness learns it through an event, and Poo learns it by leveling up.

mother-teleport-b.desc: Spins on the spot and teleports instantly to a town you have visited.
mother-teleport-b.note: Mother 2. Unlike α, it can be used even where there is no straight stretch to run. Ness learns it through an event, and Poo learns it by leveling up.

blizz.desc: Deals light Ice magic damage to one enemy.

bot.desc: Deals light Fire magic damage to one enemy.

metaphor-bottler.desc: Deals medium Fire magic damage to one enemy.

metaphor-boatna.desc: Deals heavy Fire magic damage to one enemy.

metaphor-blizzer.desc: Deals medium Ice magic damage to one enemy.

metaphor-blizzaton.desc: Deals heavy Ice magic damage to one enemy.

metaphor-kande.desc: Deals light Lightning magic damage to one enemy.

metaphor-kandera.desc: Deals medium Lightning magic damage to one enemy.

metaphor-kandeon.desc: Deals heavy Lightning magic damage to one enemy.

metaphor-saiku.desc: Deals light Wind magic damage to one enemy.

metaphor-saikuro.desc: Deals medium Wind magic damage to one enemy.
metaphor-saikuro.note: Learned by the Seeker and the Magic Seeker.

metaphor-cyclone.desc: Deals heavy Wind magic damage to one enemy.

metaphor-hanma.desc: Deals light Light magic damage to one enemy.
metaphor-hanma.note: The name is written Hanma, not Hama. Unlike in Megami Tensei and Persona, it is a damage spell rather than instant death.

metaphor-hamaon.desc: Deals medium Light magic damage to one enemy.

metaphor-hamadyne.desc: Deals heavy Light magic damage to one enemy.

metaphor-mudo.desc: Deals light Darkness magic damage to one enemy.
metaphor-mudo.note: Unlike in Megami Tensei and Persona, it is a damage spell rather than instant death.

metaphor-mudoon.desc: Deals medium Darkness magic damage to one enemy.

metaphor-mudodyne.desc: Deals heavy Darkness magic damage to one enemy.

metaphor-megido.desc: Deals medium Almighty magic damage to all enemies.
metaphor-megido.note: The element is called Almighty in this game.

metaphor-megidola.desc: Deals heavy Almighty magic damage to all enemies.

metaphor-di.desc: Restores a small amount of one ally's HP.

metaphor-diama.desc: Restores a medium amount of one ally's HP.

metaphor-diamahan.desc: Restores a large amount of one ally's HP.

metaphor-medi.desc: Restores a small amount of HP to all allies.

metaphor-medica.desc: Restores a medium amount of HP to all allies.

metaphor-medical.desc: Restores a large amount of HP to all allies.

metaphor-ridine.desc: For 3 turns, restores a little of one ally's HP each time their turn comes.

metaphor-recarm.desc: Revives one downed ally with half HP.

metaphor-samarecarm.desc: Revives one downed ally with full HP.

metaphor-penpatra.desc: Cures the status ailments of all allies.

metaphor-tarukaja.desc: Raises the attack of one ally for 3 turns.

metaphor-matarukaja.desc: Raises the attack of all allies for 3 turns.

metaphor-rakukaja.desc: Raises the defense of one ally for 3 turns.

metaphor-marakukaja.desc: Raises the defense of all allies for 3 turns.

metaphor-sukukaja.desc: Raises the accuracy and evasion of one ally for 3 turns.

metaphor-masukukaja.desc: Raises the accuracy and evasion of all allies for 3 turns.

metaphor-bitaruja.desc: Raises the attack and defense of one ally by two stages for 3 turns.
metaphor-bitaruja.note: A combined buff that also raises defense.

metaphor-tarunda.desc: Lowers the attack of one enemy for 3 turns.

metaphor-rakunda.desc: Lowers the defense of one enemy for 3 turns.

metaphor-sukunda.desc: Lowers the accuracy and evasion of one enemy for 3 turns.

metaphor-bidaruda.desc: Lowers the attack and defense of one enemy by two stages for 3 turns.
metaphor-bidaruda.note: A combined debuff that also lowers defense.

metaphor-tetrakarn.desc: Puts up a barrier on one ally that reflects one Slash, Pierce or Strike attack.
metaphor-tetrakarn.note: What it reflects is physical attacks.

metaphor-makarakarn.desc: Puts up a barrier on one ally that reflects one elemental magic attack.

metaphor-dekaja.desc: Cancels the buffs on all enemies.

metaphor-dekunda.desc: Cancels the debuffs on all allies.

metaphor-shinkuuha.desc: Deals heavy Wind damage to one enemy and also lowers its attack.

metaphor-tankyuunokaze.desc: Deals heavy Wind damage to all enemies and restores MP according to the number of enemies hit.

metaphor-suiryokunoouzu.desc: Ignores enemy resistances and deals massive Wind damage to all enemies.

metaphor-tankyuunohonoo.desc: Deals heavy Fire damage to all enemies and restores MP according to the number of enemies hit.

metaphor-goukanouzu.desc: Deals medium Fire damage to one enemy and may inflict a burn.

metaphor-shinkunoenka.desc: Deals heavy Fire damage to all enemies.
metaphor-shinkunoenka.note: Learned by the Masked Dancer. The cost uses the 42 MP given by Game8 and Kamige Kōryaku (GameWith gives 20 MP).

metaphor-mekkyakunoenka.desc: Deals heavy Fire damage to all enemies and cancels their buffs.
metaphor-mekkyakunoenka.note: Learned by the Persona Master and the Royal Masked Dancer.

metaphor-hajanohikari.desc: Deals massive Light damage to one enemy.

metaphor-kegarenakiikou.desc: Deals heavy Light damage to all enemies.

metaphor-mediline.desc: Restores a little HP to allies in the same row as the user.
metaphor-mediline.note: Learned by the Magic Knight. It targets the same row of the party formation. The cost is confirmed in only one source.

metaphor-patricarm.desc: Gives one ally an effect that, once per battle, lets them survive an attack that would reduce their HP to 0, with 1 HP left.

metaphor-hyper.desc: Greatly raises the damage of the next magic attack you use.

metaphor-heatriser.desc: Raises the attack, defense, accuracy and evasion of one ally at once for 3 turns.
metaphor-heatriser.note: Learned by the Soul Hacker. There is also a Synthesis version.

metaphor-randamaiza.desc: Lowers the attack, defense, accuracy and evasion of one enemy at once for 3 turns.
metaphor-randamaiza.note: Learned by the Trickster. There is also a Synthesis version.

metaphor-tetrabreak.note: Learned by the Seeker. There is also a Synthesis version.

metaphor-fairy.desc: Summons a fairy that deals medium Ice damage to all enemies.
metaphor-fairy.note: A summon spell learned by the Devil Summoner.

metaphor-fairykai.desc: Summons a fairy that deals heavy Ice damage to all enemies and inflicts frostbite with a high chance.
metaphor-fairykai.note: A summon spell learned by the Royal Summoner.

metaphor-ryuujin.desc: Summons a dragon god that deals colossal Fire damage to all enemies and cancels their buffs.
metaphor-ryuujin.note: A summon spell learned by the Royal Summoner. There is also a Synthesis version.

metaphor-ryuujinkai.desc: Summons a dragon god that deals massive Fire damage to all enemies and lowers their attack and defense.
metaphor-ryuujinkai.note: A summon spell learned by the Royal Summoner.

metaphor-washijishi.desc: Summons a griffin that deals heavy Wind damage to all enemies and lowers their attack.
metaphor-washijishi.note: A summon spell learned by the Summoner.

metaphor-mazou.desc: Summons a magic statue that deals heavy Fire damage to one enemy and may inflict a burn.
metaphor-mazou.note: A summon spell learned by the Summoner. It becomes usable once you obtain its vessel.

metaphor-majuu.desc: Summons a fiend beast that deals heavy Fire damage to one enemy and may inflict a burn.
metaphor-majuu.note: A summon spell learned by the Devil Summoner. It becomes usable once you obtain its vessel.

metaphor-yama.desc: Summons a night demon that ignores enemy resistances to deal heavy Ice damage to all enemies and may inflict frostbite.
metaphor-yama.note: A summon spell learned by the Devil Summoner. It becomes usable once you obtain its vessel.

metaphor-kishin.desc: Summons an oni god that deals medium Lightning damage to one enemy 2 to 4 times.
metaphor-kishin.note: A summon spell learned by the Royal Summoner. There is also a Synthesis version.

metaphor-youjuu.desc: Summons a spirit beast that deals medium Lightning damage to all enemies.
metaphor-youjuu.note: A summon spell learned by the Devil Summoner. It becomes usable once you obtain its vessel.

metaphor-majin.desc: Summons a demon god that deals massive Light damage to all enemies and may inflict daze.
metaphor-majin.note: A summon spell learned by the Royal Summoner. There is also a Synthesis version.

metaphor-dokukei.desc: Summons a poison chicken that deals medium Darkness damage to all enemies and may inflict deadly poison.
metaphor-dokukei.note: A summon spell learned by the Summoner. It becomes usable once you obtain its vessel. The reading could not be confirmed in the sources.

metaphor-fushiou.desc: Summons an undead king that deals colossal Darkness damage to one enemy and may also kill it instantly.
metaphor-fushiou.note: A summon spell learned by the Royal Summoner. There is also a Synthesis version.

metaphor-shoukiou.desc: Summons a goblin king that makes a Slash attack on one enemy that always lands as a critical hit.
metaphor-shoukiou.note: A summon spell learned by the Summoner. It becomes usable once you obtain its vessel. The reading could not be confirmed in the sources.

metaphor-kotsukokukishi.desc: Summons a skeletal black knight that deals heavy Slash damage to all enemies.
metaphor-kotsukokukishi.note: A summon spell learned by the Summoner. It becomes usable once you obtain its vessel. The reading could not be confirmed in the sources. The cost uses the 28 MP given by Game8 and Bōmemo (Kamige Kōryaku gives 38 MP).

metaphor-genma.desc: Summons a phantom fiend that deals heavy Pierce damage to one enemy and lowers its defense.
metaphor-genma.note: A summon spell learned by the Devil Summoner. It becomes usable once you obtain its vessel.

metaphor-yougan.desc: Summons a lava beast that deals medium Almighty damage to all enemies.
metaphor-yougan.note: A summon spell learned by the Summoner. It becomes usable once you obtain its vessel.

metaphor-yakouchou.desc: Summons a luminous butterfly that cures one ally's status ailments and restores a little HP over 3 turns.
metaphor-yakouchou.note: A summon spell learned by the Summoner.

metaphor-houjoushin.desc: Summons a harvest god that fully restores the HP of all allies and also revives downed allies with full HP.
metaphor-houjoushin.note: A summon spell learned by the Royal Summoner.

metaphor-megami.desc: Summons a goddess that fully restores one ally's HP.
metaphor-megami.note: A summon spell learned by the Devil Summoner. It becomes usable once you obtain its vessel.

metaphor-datenshi.desc: Summons a fallen angel that puts up a barrier on one ally that reflects one Slash, Pierce or Strike attack.
metaphor-datenshi.note: A summon spell learned by the Devil Summoner. Confirmed in only one source.

saga1-cure.desc: A magic book that restores one ally's HP.
saga1-cure.note: The Game Boy version writes the name with sho in kana; some strategy sources write it with the kanji for book. Monsters cannot equip it, so they cannot use it.

saga1-fire.desc: A magic book that attacks one group of enemies with fire.
saga1-fire.note: The Game Boy version writes the name with sho in kana; some strategy sources write it with the kanji for book. Monsters cannot equip it, so they cannot use it.

saga1-blizzard.desc: A magic book that attacks one group of enemies with cold.
saga1-blizzard.note: The Game Boy version writes the name with sho in kana; some strategy sources write it with the kanji for book. Monsters cannot equip it, so they cannot use it.

saga1-thunder.desc: A magic book that attacks one group of enemies with lightning.
saga1-thunder.note: The Game Boy version writes the name with sho in kana; some strategy sources write it with the kanji for book. Monsters cannot equip it, so they cannot use it.

saga1-cloud.desc: A magic book that damages one group of enemies with the power of poison.
saga1-cloud.note: The element in this game is poison. The Game Boy version writes the name with sho in kana; some strategy sources write it with the kanji for book. Monsters cannot equip it, so they cannot use it.

saga1-flare.desc: A magic book that deals non-elemental explosive damage to all enemies.
saga1-flare.note: The Game Boy version writes the name with sho in kana; some strategy sources write it with the kanji for book. Monsters cannot equip it, so they cannot use it.

saga1-sleep.desc: A magic book that puts one group of enemies to sleep.
saga1-sleep.note: The Game Boy version writes the name with sho in kana; some strategy sources write it with the kanji for book. Monsters cannot equip it, so they cannot use it.

saga1-break.desc: A magic book that turns one group of enemies to stone.
saga1-break.note: The Game Boy version writes the name with sho in kana; some strategy sources write it with the kanji for book. Monsters cannot equip it, so they cannot use it.

saga1-death.desc: A magic book that instantly kills one group of enemies.
saga1-death.note: The Game Boy version writes the name with sho in kana; some strategy sources write it with the kanji for book. Monsters cannot equip it, so they cannot use it.

saga1-nenbutsu.desc: A magic book that damages only one group of undead enemies.
saga1-nenbutsu.note: It is one of the magic books (spell books), but its name ends in hon rather than sho. GameCenterGX writes it with the kanji for book (Nenbutsu no Sho). It has no effect on non-undead enemies. The sources do not state its element. The number of uses is not entered because sources differ (10, 20 or 30 uses). Monsters cannot equip it, so they cannot use it.

saga2-cure.desc: A magic book that restores one ally's HP.
saga2-cure.note: When a Mecha equips it, its number of uses is halved, but it recovers at an inn. Monsters cannot equip it.

saga2-fire.desc: A magic book that attacks one group of enemies with fire.
saga2-fire.note: When a Mecha equips it, its number of uses is halved, but it recovers at an inn. Monsters cannot equip it.

saga2-blizzard.desc: A magic book that attacks one group of enemies with cold.
saga2-blizzard.note: When a Mecha equips it, its number of uses is halved, but it recovers at an inn. Monsters cannot equip it.

saga2-thunder.desc: A magic book that attacks one group of enemies with lightning.
saga2-thunder.note: When a Mecha equips it, its number of uses is halved, but it recovers at an inn. Monsters cannot equip it.

saga2-cloud.desc: A magic book that damages one group of enemies with the power of poison.
saga2-cloud.note: The element in this game is poison. When a Mecha equips it, its number of uses is halved, but it recovers at an inn. Monsters cannot equip it.

saga2-flare.desc: A magic book that deals non-elemental explosive damage to all enemies.
saga2-flare.note: When a Mecha equips it, its number of uses is halved, but it recovers at an inn. Monsters cannot equip it.

saga2-sleep.desc: A magic book that puts one group of enemies to sleep.
saga2-sleep.note: When a Mecha equips it, its number of uses is halved, but it recovers at an inn. Monsters cannot equip it.

saga2-break.desc: A magic book that turns one group of enemies to stone.
saga2-break.note: When a Mecha equips it, its number of uses is halved, but it recovers at an inn. Monsters cannot equip it.

saga2-death.desc: A magic book that instantly kills one group of enemies.
saga2-death.note: When a Mecha equips it, its number of uses is halved, but it recovers at an inn. Monsters cannot equip it.

saga2-nenbutsu.desc: A magic book that damages only one group of undead enemies.
saga2-nenbutsu.note: It is one of the magic books (spell books), but its name ends in hon rather than sho. It has no effect on non-undead enemies. The sources do not state its element. When a Mecha equips it, its number of uses is halved, but it recovers at an inn. Monsters cannot equip it.

saga3-protes.desc: Raises the defense of one ally. Stackable.

saga3-cure.desc: Restores about 30% of one ally's HP.
saga3-cure.note: White Magic. Level 1. Damages undead. Healing increases in the order Kearu (Lv 1), Kearura (Lv 3), Kearuga (Lv 5).

saga3-sleep.desc: Puts one enemy to sleep. Used on an ally, it wakes them up.

saga3-blizzard.note: Black Magic. Level 1. A lower-tier spell that cannot be made to hit a group.

saga3-muon.desc: Lets the party move over water on the field.
saga3-muon.note: Ancient Magic. Level 1, 0 MP. Cannot be used in other dimensions. Robots have 0 MP, but they can still use this spell because it costs nothing.

saga3-summon.desc: Lets the party move on and under water.
saga3-summon.note: Ancient Magic. Level 1, 0 MP. Robots have 0 MP, but they can still use this spell because it costs nothing.

saga3-spark.desc: Blinds one enemy. Used on an ally, it cures blindness.

saga3-aero.note: White Magic. Level 2. A lower-tier spell that cannot be made to hit a group. Sources differ on the element name: "wind" or "tornado."

saga3-poison.desc: Poisons one enemy. Used on an ally, it cures poison.

saga3-fire.note: Black Magic. Level 2. A lower-tier spell that cannot be made to hit a group.

saga3-heal.desc: Restores about 30% of HP to all allies.
saga3-heal.note: Ancient Magic. Level 2. Its upgrade is Hīrā (about 60%).

saga3-hypno.desc: Curses one enemy. Used on an ally, it cures the curse.

saga3-brain.desc: Confuses one enemy. Used on an ally, it cures confusion.

saga3-cura.desc: Restores about 60% of one ally's HP.

saga3-paradi.desc: Paralyzes one enemy. Used on an ally, it cures paralysis.

saga3-thunder.note: Black Magic. Level 3. A lower-tier spell that cannot be made to hit a group. The in-game element name is lightning.

saga3-metamor.desc: Transforms the party into a monster while traveling, letting them talk to monsters.

saga3-hurricane.note: Ancient Magic. Level 3. An Ancient Magic spell created by fusion (synthesis). Ingredients: Wind + Water.

saga3-stone.desc: Turns one enemy to stone. Used on an ally, it cures petrification.

saga3-quake.desc: Attacks all enemies with an earthquake.
saga3-quake.note: White Magic. Level 4. The in-game element name is earthquake.

saga3-blizzaga.desc: Attacks one enemy or one group with intense cold.
saga3-blizzaga.note: Black Magic. Level 4. The upgrade of Burizado, and it can target either a single enemy or a group.

saga3-tachyon.desc: Attacks all enemies with a tornado.
saga3-tachyon.note: Ancient Magic. Level 4. An Ancient Magic spell created by fusion (synthesis). Ingredients: Wind + Earth.

saga3-healer.desc: Restores about 60% of HP to all allies.

saga3-haste.desc: Raises the attack power of one ally. Stackable.
saga3-haste.note: White Magic. Level 5. Despite its name, it raises attack power, not speed.

saga3-curaga.note: White Magic. Level 5. Cannot be made to hit all allies.

saga3-erase.desc: Cancels stat boosts and reductions on the target.

saga3-firaga.desc: Attacks one enemy or one group with intense flames.
saga3-firaga.note: Black Magic. Level 5. The upgrade of Faia, and it can target either a single enemy or a group.

saga3-damian.desc: Cures all status ailments on one ally. Used on an enemy, it inflicts status ailments.
saga3-damian.note: Ancient Magic. Level 5. An Ancient Magic spell created by fusion (synthesis). Ingredients: Water + Earth.

saga3-aura.note: Ancient Magic. Level 5. An Ancient Magic spell created by fusion (synthesis). Ingredients: Wind + Fire.

saga3-esuna.desc: Cures the status ailments of one ally (except knockout).

saga3-tornado.desc: Attacks one enemy or one group with a tornado.
saga3-tornado.note: White Magic. Level 6. The upgrade of Earo, and it can target either a single enemy or a group.

saga3-teleport.desc: Escapes from a dungeon. In battle, it instead instantly kills one enemy.

saga3-thundaga.desc: Attacks one enemy or one group with intense lightning.
saga3-thundaga.note: Black Magic. Level 6. The upgrade of Sandā, and it can target either a single enemy or a group.

saga3-chaos.desc: Revives one knocked-out ally. Used on an enemy, it causes instant death.
saga3-chaos.note: Ancient Magic. Level 6. An Ancient Magic spell created by fusion (synthesis). Ingredients: Earth + Earth.

saga3-meteor.desc: Attacks all enemies with an earthquake.
saga3-meteor.note: Ancient Magic. Level 6. An Ancient Magic spell created by fusion (synthesis). Ingredients: Fire + Earth.

saga3-reflect.desc: Reflects magic, only during the turn it is cast.

saga3-raise.desc: Revives one knocked-out ally with about 30% HP.
saga3-raise.note: White Magic. Level 7. Causes instant death on undead.

saga3-bio.desc: Deals non-elemental damage to one enemy or one group.

saga3-meza.note: Ancient Magic. Level 7. An Ancient Magic spell created by fusion (synthesis). Ingredients: Fire + Water.

saga3-dogra.desc: Escapes from a dungeon. In battle, it instead instantly kills enemies.
saga3-dogra.note: Ancient Magic. Level 7. An Ancient Magic spell created by fusion (synthesis). Ingredients: Wind + Wind.

saga3-holy.desc: Deals heavy non-elemental damage to all enemies.
saga3-holy.note: White Magic. Level 8. Treated as non-elemental in sources.

saga3-magma.desc: Attacks one enemy or one group with an earthquake.

saga3-flare.desc: Deals heavy non-elemental damage to all enemies.

saga3-ashura.desc: Deals heavy non-elemental damage to all enemies.
saga3-ashura.note: Ancient Magic. Level 8. An Ancient Magic spell created by fusion (synthesis). Ingredients: Fire + Fire.

saga3-miroku.desc: Revives one knocked-out ally with full HP.
saga3-miroku.note: Ancient Magic. Level 8. An Ancient Magic spell created by fusion (synthesis). Ingredients: Water + Water. Causes instant death on undead.

fireball.note: Fire Arts. Targets all enemies in the SFC version.

rsaga-self-burning.desc: Wraps the caster in flames, gaining fire protection.

rsaga-fire-wall.desc: Attacks a vertical column of enemies with flames.
rsaga-fire-wall.note: Fire Arts. Targets one vertical column of enemies.

rsaga-hinotori.desc: Looses a firebird that attacks all enemies with flames.

rsaga-yakitsukusu.desc: Attacks one enemy with flames, and may kill it instantly.
rsaga-yakitsukusu.note: Fire Arts. Some sources write it as "焼き尽くす."

rsaga-iyashi-no-mizu.note: Water Arts. Some sources write it as "癒しの水."

rsaga-chikara-no-mizu.desc: Raises the strength of one ally.

rsaga-rain-call.desc: Calls rain and attacks all enemies with water.

rsaga-dokukeshi-no-mizu.desc: Cures the status ailments of one ally (except petrification).
rsaga-dokukeshi-no-mizu.note: Water Arts. Some sources write it as "毒消しの水."

rsaga-water-gun.desc: Attacks one enemy with a jet of water.

rsaga-abura-jigoku.desc: Lowers the speed and dexterity of all enemies.
rsaga-abura-jigoku.note: Water Arts. Some sources write it as "油地獄."

rsaga-uzushio.desc: Attacks all enemies with a whirlpool.
rsaga-uzushio.note: Water Arts. Some sources write it as "渦潮."

rsaga-diamond-spear.desc: Attacks one enemy with the power of earth.
rsaga-diamond-spear.note: Earth Arts. Some sources write it as "ダイヤモンドスピア."

rsaga-diamond-weapon.desc: Raises the attack power of one ally.
rsaga-diamond-weapon.note: Earth Arts. Some sources write it as "ダイヤモンドウエポン."

rsaga-diamond-armor.desc: Raises the defense of one ally.

rsaga-earth-heal.desc: Restores the caster's HP and also increases natural recovery.

rsaga-ice-javelin.desc: Attacks one enemy with a spear of ice.
rsaga-ice-javelin.note: Wind Arts. Sources list its element as wind and ice.

rsaga-lightning.desc: Attacks a horizontal row of enemies with lightning.
rsaga-lightning.note: Wind Arts. Targets one horizontal row of enemies. Sources list its element as wind and lightning.

rsaga-blood-froze.desc: Freezes the blood of one enemy, killing it instantly.

rsaga-fubuki.desc: Attacks all enemies with a blizzard.
rsaga-fubuki.note: Wind Arts. Some sources write it as "吹雪." Sources list its element as wind and ice.

rsaga-flash.desc: Dazzles all enemies with a bright light.

rsaga-starlight-wall.desc: Attacks a vertical column of enemies with light.
rsaga-starlight-wall.note: Light Arts. Targets one vertical column of enemies.

rsaga-kage-shibari.desc: Binds the shadow of one enemy, paralyzing it.
rsaga-kage-shibari.note: Dark Arts. Some sources write it as "影縛り." This school cannot be bought in shops. Dark and Evil Arts are not sold at the spell shop, and party members cannot normally learn them in regular play (sources describe them as "basically enemy-only" or "used only by the Red Mage"), so no user is listed.

rsaga-horror.desc: Puts one enemy into a panic.
rsaga-horror.note: Dark Arts. The in-game status name is panic. Dark and Evil Arts are not sold at the spell shop, and party members cannot normally learn them in regular play (sources describe them as "basically enemy-only" or "used only by the Red Mage"), so no user is listed.

rsaga-black-fire.desc: Attacks one enemy with dark flames.
rsaga-black-fire.note: Dark Arts. Dark and Evil Arts are not sold at the spell shop, and party members cannot normally learn them in regular play (sources describe them as "basically enemy-only" or "used only by the Red Mage"), so no user is listed.

rsaga-dark-wall.desc: Attacks a vertical column of enemies with dark power.
rsaga-dark-wall.note: Dark Arts. Targets one vertical column of enemies. Dark and Evil Arts are not sold at the spell shop, and party members cannot normally learn them in regular play (sources describe them as "basically enemy-only" or "used only by the Red Mage"), so no user is listed.

rsaga-black-sphere.note: Dark Arts. Dark and Evil Arts are not sold at the spell shop, and party members cannot normally learn them in regular play (sources describe them as "basically enemy-only" or "used only by the Red Mage"), so no user is listed.

rsaga-dark-web.desc: Attacks all enemies with dark power.
rsaga-dark-web.note: Dark Arts. Dark and Evil Arts are not sold at the spell shop, and party members cannot normally learn them in regular play (sources describe them as "basically enemy-only" or "used only by the Red Mage"), so no user is listed.

rsaga-poison-gas.desc: Poisons all enemies with a toxic mist.
rsaga-poison-gas.note: Evil Arts. This school cannot be bought in shops. Dark and Evil Arts are not sold at the spell shop, and party members cannot normally learn them in regular play (sources describe them as "basically enemy-only" or "used only by the Red Mage"), so no user is listed.

rsaga-life-drain.note: Evil Arts. Dark and Evil Arts are not sold at the spell shop, and party members cannot normally learn them in regular play (sources describe them as "basically enemy-only" or "used only by the Red Mage"), so no user is listed.

rsaga-weakness.desc: Lowers all the stats of one enemy at once.
rsaga-weakness.note: Evil Arts. Dark and Evil Arts are not sold at the spell shop, and party members cannot normally learn them in regular play (sources describe them as "basically enemy-only" or "used only by the Red Mage"), so no user is listed.

rsaga-death-hand.desc: Deals fire damage to one enemy, and may kill it instantly.
rsaga-death-hand.note: Evil Arts. Dark and Evil Arts are not sold at the spell shop, and party members cannot normally learn them in regular play (sources describe them as "basically enemy-only" or "used only by the Red Mage"), so no user is listed.

rsaga-bougyohou.desc: Reduces the physical and art damage the caster takes.

rsaga-hajahou.desc: Deals light damage to all undead-type enemies.
rsaga-hajahou.note: Ki Arts. Effective only against undead-type enemies.

rsaga-seiki-shougekihou.desc: Releases ki to deal non-elemental damage to one enemy.

rsaga-energy-bolt.desc: Fires a non-elemental bolt of magic power at one enemy.

rsaga-slow.desc: Lowers the speed of one enemy.

rsaga-weapon-bless.desc: Raises the attack power of one ally.

rsaga-armor-bless.desc: Raises the defense of one ally.

rsaga-quick.desc: Raises the speed of all allies.

rsaga-energy-storm.desc: Deals non-elemental damage to all enemies.

rsaga-higenjutsu.desc: Attacks one enemy with illusory flames.
rsaga-higenjutsu.note: Illusion Arts. The reading is unconfirmed.

rsaga-hagenjutsu.desc: Cancels illusion arts such as Ryūgenjutsu.

rsaga-genmujutsu.desc: Dazzles all enemies with an illusory mist.

rsaga-raigenjutsu.desc: Attacks a vertical column of enemies with illusory lightning.
rsaga-raigenjutsu.note: Illusion Arts. Targets one vertical column of enemies.

rsaga-fire-weapon.desc: Gives one ally's weapon the fire element.

rsaga-elemental-fire.desc: Summons a fire elemental to fight.
rsaga-elemental-fire.note: Fire Arts. The Fire, Water, Earth and Wind Arts each have a spell called Erementaru, and each school summons a different spirit.

rsaga-elemental-water.desc: Summons a water elemental to fight.
rsaga-elemental-water.note: Water Arts. The Fire, Water, Earth and Wind Arts each have a spell of the same name.

rsaga-elemental-earth.desc: Summons an earth elemental to fight.
rsaga-elemental-earth.note: Earth Arts. The Fire, Water, Earth and Wind Arts each have a spell of the same name.

rsaga-elemental-wind.desc: Summons a wind elemental to fight.
rsaga-elemental-wind.note: Wind Arts. The Fire, Water, Earth and Wind Arts each have a spell of the same name.

rsaga-camouflage.desc: Blends into the surroundings to protect oneself.
rsaga-camouflage.note: Earth Arts. Descriptions of the effect differ by source (GameCenterGX: makes the caster less likely to be targeted; Tora no Su: forced defense).

rsaga-earth-hand.desc: Lowers the speed and dexterity of all enemies.
rsaga-earth-hand.note: Earth Arts. Tora no Su lists it as lowering dexterity and speed, but GameCenterGX says "no effect (probably a setting error)."

rsaga-cold-weapon.desc: Gives one ally's weapon the cold element.

rsaga-wind-barrier.desc: Makes one ally harder to hit with a protective wind.
rsaga-wind-barrier.note: Wind Arts. Sources word it differently: "evasion up" or "hit rate down."

rsaga-simulacrum.desc: Summons a snowman with the same abilities as the target.

rsaga-light.desc: Changes the battlefield terrain to light.
rsaga-light.note: Light Arts. Targets the terrain (the whole field).

rsaga-invisi.desc: Makes one ally invisible, making them harder to hit.
rsaga-invisi.note: Light Arts. Descriptions of the effect differ by source (GameCenterGX: evasion up; Tora no Su: forced defense).

rsaga-star-sword.desc: Creates the Star Sword, a sword of light, and equips it.

rsaga-darkness.desc: Changes the battlefield terrain to darkness.
rsaga-darkness.note: Dark Arts. Targets the terrain (the whole field). Dark and Evil Arts are not sold at the spell shop, and party members cannot normally learn them in regular play (sources describe them as "basically enemy-only" or "used only by the Red Mage"), so no user is listed.

rsaga-dark-sword.desc: Creates the Dark Sword, a sword of darkness, and equips it.
rsaga-dark-sword.note: Dark Arts. Dark and Evil Arts are not sold at the spell shop, and party members cannot normally learn them in regular play (sources describe them as "basically enemy-only" or "used only by the Red Mage"), so no user is listed.

rsaga-injury.desc: Deals damage to one enemy based on its HP.
rsaga-injury.note: Evil Arts. Can also target distant enemies. The sources do not state its element. Dark and Evil Arts are not sold at the spell shop, and party members cannot normally learn them in regular play (sources describe them as "basically enemy-only" or "used only by the Red Mage"), so no user is listed.

rsaga-agony.note: Evil Arts. Some sources write it as "アゴニィ." Dark and Evil Arts are not sold at the spell shop, and party members cannot normally learn them in regular play (sources describe them as "basically enemy-only" or "used only by the Red Mage"), so no user is listed.

rsaga-evil-spirit.desc: Possesses one enemy with an evil spirit.
rsaga-evil-spirit.note: Evil Arts. The in-game status name is "possession" (憑依). Dark and Evil Arts are not sold at the spell shop, and party members cannot normally learn them in regular play (sources describe them as "basically enemy-only" or "used only by the Red Mage"), so no user is listed.

rsaga-animate.desc: Turns one enemy into a puppet.
rsaga-animate.note: Evil Arts. The in-game status name is "marionette" (マリオネット). Dark and Evil Arts are not sold at the spell shop, and party members cannot normally learn them in regular play (sources describe them as "basically enemy-only" or "used only by the Red Mage"), so no user is listed.

rsaga-musouhou.desc: Empties the mind, making attacks against the caster harder to land.
rsaga-musouhou.note: Ki Arts. Sources word it differently: "evasion up" or "hit rate down."

rsaga-spell-enhance.desc: Boosts one ally's magic power, raising the strength of their arts.

rsaga-gentai-senshijutsu.desc: Summons an illusory warrior with the same abilities as the caster.

rsaga-ryugenjutsu.desc: Summons an illusory dragon to attack the enemy.
rsaga-ryugenjutsu.note: Illusion Arts. The target differs by source (GameCenterGX: all enemies; Tora no Su: the protagonist), so scope was left blank.

sf-taiyou-kousen.note: Sun Arts. Effective only against undead.

sf-starlight-heal.desc: Restores HP to one ally and cures poison.

sf-flash-fire.desc: Attacks all enemies with a flash and heat, and may blind them.
sf-flash-fire.note: Sun Arts. Sources list its element as heat.

sf-hikari-no-ken.desc: Creates a sword of light and wields it, also raising stats.

sf-choufuu.desc: Attacks all enemies with a violent wind.
sf-choufuu.note: Sun Arts. Advanced art (requires aptitude). Sources list its element as a combination of wind, lightning and cold.

sf-power-snatch.desc: Drains HP from one enemy and lowers its strength.

sf-shadow-net.desc: Paralyzes all enemies with a net of shadow.

sf-dark-sphere.desc: Damages one enemy and removes the buffs on it.
sf-dark-sphere.note: Shadow Arts. Advanced art (requires aptitude). Its element could not be confirmed in sources.

sf-shadow-servant.desc: Creates a shadow double of the caster, doubling their attacks.

sf-energy-chain.desc: Binds one enemy with chains of magic power.
sf-energy-chain.note: Magic Arts. Success rate depends on stats such as intelligence and magic power.

sf-implosion.desc: Deals heat damage to one enemy and may knock it unconscious.
sf-implosion.note: Magic Arts. Sources list its element as heat.

sf-psycho-armor.desc: Strengthens the defenses of one ally.

sf-gate.desc: Moves the party to a region it has visited before.

sf-psychic-prison.desc: Seals one enemy's arts, and it takes a counterattack if it tries to use them.

sf-vermilion-sands.desc: Damages all enemies and may blind them.

sf-fascination.note: Enchantment Arts. Success rate depends on charm.

sf-genmu-no-ichigeki.desc: Attacks one enemy with an illusory blow.

sf-garasu-no-tate.desc: Blocks physical attacks with a glass shield and counterattacks.

sf-mirror-shade.desc: Creates illusory copies of the caster to spread out attacks.

sf-tsurugi.desc: Slashes one enemy with the power of the Sword card.

sf-tate.desc: Raises the defense of all allies.

sf-hai.desc: Cures the status ailments of one ally (except unconsciousness and sleep).

sf-shinigami.desc: Instantly kills all enemies. If it fails, the caster loses LP.

sf-tou.desc: Uses up all remaining JP to deal heavy damage to one enemy.
sf-tou.note: Arcana. Advanced art (requires aptitude). The reading is unconfirmed. The cost is all the JP the caster has left when it is used.

sf-shouri-no-rune.desc: Raises the weapon attack power of one ally.

sf-katsuryoku-no-rune.desc: Restores a little of one ally's HP every turn.

sf-hogo-no-rune.desc: Hides one ally so they are less likely to be targeted (does not protect against attacks that hit everyone).

sf-kaihou-no-rune.desc: Makes one ally immune to sleep, paralysis and petrification.

sf-datsuryoku-no-rune.desc: Greatly lowers the strength of one enemy.

sf-teitai-no-rune.desc: Petrifies one enemy along with the caster.
sf-teitai-no-rune.note: Rune Arts. Advanced art (requires aptitude). The cost is all the JP the caster has left when it is used.

sf-kokki.desc: Restores the caster's HP and cures status ailments.

sf-kakusei.desc: Greatly raises all of the caster's stats, but doubles the WP and JP cost.

sf-jusatsu.desc: Curses one enemy to instant death. If it fails, the caster loses LP.
sf-jusatsu.note: Evil Arts. It cannot be learned by purchase or aptitude, but Zozma can use it as a starting art (the higher Evil Arts are enemy-only).

sf-vapor-blast.desc: Attacks one enemy. Strong against airborne enemies.

sf-reverse-gravity.desc: Reverses gravity to attack all enemies.

sf-vortex.desc: Cancels the status effects and art effects on all enemies and allies.

sf-delay-order.desc: Lowers the speed of one enemy.

sf-time-leap.desc: Seals the actions of one enemy.

sf-chaos-stream.desc: Inflicts multiple status ailments on all enemies.
sf-chaos-stream.note: Time Arts. Includes unconsciousness, blindness, paralysis, poison, petrification and sleep.

sf-jikanshoku.desc: Petrifies one enemy and also lowers its speed.

sf-overdrive.desc: Stops time so that only the caster acts, many times over.
sf-overdrive.note: Time Arts. Advanced art (requires aptitude). Some sources write it as "オーヴァドライブ."

sf-nightmare.desc: Damages one enemy and puts it to sleep.
sf-nightmare.note: Illusion Arts. This school cannot be bought in shops.

sf-cockatrice.desc: Damages one enemy and petrifies it.
sf-cockatrice.note: Illusion Arts. This school cannot be bought in shops.

sf-sacrifice.desc: Spends 1 LP to restore HP to all allies.
sf-sacrifice.note: Life Arts. In the remastered version, Blue and Rouge from Fuse's scenario are also said to be able to use it.

sf-revivar.desc: Gives one ally an effect that fully restores them once, automatically, when they would be knocked out.
sf-revivar.note: Life Arts. In the remastered version, Blue and Rouge from Fuse's scenario are also said to be able to use it.

sf-flash-flood.desc: Washes away all enemies with a flash flood.
sf-flash-flood.note: Sun Arts. It is sometimes written "フラッシュフロッド" in sources, but all three sources we could check use "フラッシュフラッド."

sf-hide-behind.desc: Temporarily turns one enemy to face backward.
sf-hide-behind.note: Shadow Arts. Activates first, before other actions (Fast Trick).

sf-kinka.desc: Fools the enemy with an illusion of gold coins, keeping them from acting.
sf-kinka.note: Arcana. The target differs by source (Kami Kōryaku wiki: all enemies; Ultima: a single enemy), so scope was left blank. The reading is unconfirmed.

sf-majutsushi.desc: Creates a double of the caster that takes one enemy attack.
sf-majutsushi.note: Arcana. Advanced art (requires aptitude). The reading is unconfirmed.

sf-gusha.desc: Lowers the power of attacks received by everyone, enemies and allies alike.
sf-gusha.note: Arcana. Advanced art (requires aptitude). It also affects enemies. The reading is unconfirmed.

sf-kabe-no-rune.desc: Creates a wall around one ally that blocks incoming attacks (pierce element) once.

sf-tamashii-no-rune.desc: Burns the caster's soul to greatly raise all stats for a while.
sf-tamashii-no-rune.note: Rune Arts. Advanced art (requires aptitude). Ultima says the target is a single ally and that it costs LP.

sf-ongyou.desc: Hides the caster so they cannot be targeted by enemy attacks.
sf-ongyou.note: Mind Arts. The reading is unconfirmed.

sf-seimei-hadou.desc: Fires life energy to attack one enemy. Strong against undead.
sf-seimei-hadou.note: Mind Arts. Advanced art (requires aptitude). The in-game elements are "ki" and "status."

sf-zatsureigeki.desc: Sets minor spirits on one enemy to damage it, sometimes stopping its movement.
sf-zatsureigeki.note: Evil Arts. It cannot be learned by purchase or aptitude, and only Zozma can use it, as a starting art. The in-game element is "ki."

sf-tsuukaku-baizou.desc: Deals damage to each enemy equal to the damage it has already taken (with a cap).
sf-tsuukaku-baizou.note: Evil Arts. A starting art for Zozma. Damage is capped at 666.

sf-gekitsuu.desc: Makes all enemies feel an illusion of pain and stops their movement (deals no damage).
sf-gekitsuu.note: Evil Arts. A starting art for Zozma. Activates first, before other actions. The in-game status is stun.

sf-light-shift.desc: Turns the battlefield into a field of sunlight.
sf-light-shift.note: Sky Arts. Makes abilities such as photosynthesis easier to trigger.

sf-dark-shift.desc: Turns the battlefield into a field of darkness, hindering HP recovery.

sf-time-twister.desc: Lets one ally act a second time in the same turn.

sf-kuroneko.desc: Damages one enemy with an illusion of a black cat and confuses it.

sf-jackal.desc: Damages one enemy with an illusion of a jackal and poisons it.

sf-reaper.desc: Damages one enemy with an illusion of the Reaper and knocks it unconscious (incapacitated).

rsaga2-fireball.desc: Burns one enemy with a fireball.
rsaga2-fireball.note: Fire Arts. Sources list its element as heat. As the art level rises, nearby enemies also take a little damage.

rsaga2-self-burning.desc: Wraps the caster in flames to resist heat and counterattack enemies that attack directly.

rsaga2-flame-whip.desc: Lashes one enemy with a whip of fire, and may paralyze it.

rsaga2-kokutenha.desc: Directly cuts into one enemy's life force (LP), aiming to defeat it.
rsaga2-kokutenha.note: Fire Arts. Sources describe it as damage to LP with an instant-death effect.

rsaga2-reviva.desc: Gives one ally an effect that automatically revives them even if they are knocked out.

rsaga2-seimei-no-mizu.note: Water Arts. As the art level rises, it also cures sleep and paralysis.

rsaga2-genki-no-mizu.desc: Cures the status ailments of one ally (except petrification).

rsaga2-kirigakure.desc: Hides one ally in mist so enemies are less likely to target them.

rsaga2-mizumai.desc: Raises one ally's defense with a film of water.
rsaga2-mizumai.note: Water Arts. Sources say it raises physical and heat defense.

rsaga2-quick-time.desc: Changes the flow of time so only your side acts while the enemy cannot move.
rsaga2-quick-time.note: Water Arts. Sources give the target as "all allies." It seals the enemy's actions.

rsaga2-kongouriki.desc: Raises the strength of one ally.

rsaga2-ashigarame.desc: Entangles the legs of all enemies and stops their movement.
rsaga2-ashigarame.note: Earth Arts. The in-game status is stun (unconsciousness).

rsaga2-earth-heal.desc: Restores one ally's HP with the power of the earth.
rsaga2-earth-heal.note: Earth Arts. As the art level rises, it also cures confusion, charm and more.

rsaga2-stone-shower.desc: Attacks all enemies with a rain of stones.
rsaga2-stone-shower.note: Earth Arts. Sources list its element as bash.

rsaga2-kongoujun.desc: Creates a shield around one ally to block physical attacks.
rsaga2-kongoujun.note: Earth Arts. The reading is unconfirmed.

rsaga2-wind-cutter.desc: Slashes one enemy with a blade of wind.
rsaga2-wind-cutter.note: Wind Arts. Sources list its elements as slash and shot.

rsaga2-air-screen.desc: Raises one ally's defense with a film of air.
rsaga2-air-screen.note: Wind Arts. Sources say it raises physical and lightning defense.

rsaga2-missile-guard.desc: Protects all allies from ranged attacks such as arrows.
rsaga2-missile-guard.note: Wind Arts. Sources say it nullifies shot-element damage.

rsaga2-tairyoku-kyuushuu.desc: Drains one enemy's HP and gives it to the caster.

rsaga2-fuujinken.desc: Creates a sword of wind and equips it, enabling its own special techniques.

rsaga2-light-ball.desc: Attacks all enemies with a ball of light, and may dazzle them.
rsaga2-light-ball.note: Celestial Arts. Sources list its element as status.

rsaga2-gekkou.desc: Restores one ally's HP with moonlight.
rsaga2-gekkou.note: Celestial Arts. As the art level rises, it also cures blindness.

rsaga2-taiyou-kousen.desc: Strikes one enemy with sunlight. Very effective against undead.
rsaga2-taiyou-kousen.note: Celestial Arts. Sources list its element as heat.

rsaga2-sword-barrier.desc: A barrier protecting the caster that blocks slashing attacks.
rsaga2-sword-barrier.note: Celestial Arts. Sources say it nullifies slash-element damage (swords and claws).

rsaga2-galaxy.desc: Attacks all enemies with the power of the stars. Ignores defense.
rsaga2-galaxy.note: Celestial Arts. Sources list it as non-elemental. AppMedia writes it as "ギャラクシー."

rsaga2-pain.desc: Attacks one enemy by inflicting pain, and may knock it unconscious.
rsaga2-pain.note: Nether Arts. Sources list it as non-elemental.

rsaga2-horror.desc: Instills fear to confuse one enemy.

rsaga2-claw-extend.desc: Grows claws from the arms and equips them, enabling their own special techniques.

rsaga2-deadly-drive.desc: Lowers all the stats of all enemies at once.

rsaga2-shadow-servant.desc: Summons the caster's shadow to mimic their actions. When the caster takes a physical attack, the shadow takes the hit in their place and disappears.
rsaga2-shadow-servant.note: Nether Arts. RRPG and AppMedia write it as "シャドーサーバンド."

rsaga2-honoo-no-kabe.desc: Protects all allies from heat and cold with a wall of flame.
rsaga2-honoo-no-kabe.note: Combination art (Fire Arts + Earth Arts). As the art level rises, it counterattacks enemies that attack. kouryaku.sub.jp writes it as "火の壁."

rsaga2-heat-hand.desc: Imbues the fists with heat, enabling their own martial techniques.

rsaga2-neppuu.desc: Attacks all enemies with a hot wind and lowers their speed.
rsaga2-neppuu.note: Combination art (Fire Arts + Wind Arts). Sources list its element as heat.

rsaga2-fire-storm.desc: Burns all enemies with a storm of fire.
rsaga2-fire-storm.note: Combination art (Fire Arts + Wind Arts). Sources list its element as heat.

rsaga2-elixir.desc: Restores one ally's HP and cures status ailments.

rsaga2-ryuumyaku.desc: Draws in the power of the earth to raise all of the caster's stats at once. The effect ends when the caster attacks.

rsaga2-cyclone-squeeze.desc: Crushes one enemy in a tornado, and may knock it unconscious.
rsaga2-cyclone-squeeze.note: Combination art (Water Arts + Wind Arts). Sources list its element as status. kouryaku.sub.jp writes it as "サイクロンスクイーズ."

rsaga2-shourai.desc: Calls down lightning on one enemy, and the blast also reaches nearby enemies.
rsaga2-shourai.note: Combination art (Water Arts + Wind Arts). Sources list its element as lightning.

rsaga2-saint-fire.desc: Attacks a row of enemies with holy flames. Very effective against undead and demons.
rsaga2-saint-fire.note: Combination art (Fire Arts + Celestial Arts). Sources list its element as status. The row differs by source (GameCenterGX: a horizontal row; kouryaku.sub.jp: a vertical column), so scope was left blank.

rsaga2-crimson-flare.desc: Burns one enemy with crimson flames, and may blind it and lower its mental power.
rsaga2-crimson-flare.note: Combination art (Fire Arts + Celestial Arts). Sources list its elements as heat and status.

rsaga2-diamond-dust.desc: Attacks all enemies with ice particles.
rsaga2-diamond-dust.note: Combination art (Water Arts + Celestial Arts). Sources list its elements as bash and cold.

rsaga2-prism-light.desc: Confuses all enemies with a seven-colored light.

rsaga2-arc-thunder.desc: Strikes one enemy with lightning, and the blast also reaches nearby enemies.
rsaga2-arc-thunder.note: Combination art (Earth Arts + Celestial Arts). Sources list its element as lightning.

rsaga2-hikari-no-kabe.desc: Reduces the damage all allies take with a wall of light.
rsaga2-hikari-no-kabe.note: Combination art (Earth Arts + Celestial Arts). As the art level rises, it counterattacks enemies that attack.

rsaga2-yousei-kou.desc: Wraps the caster in the light of fairies, raising their speed.

rsaga2-taiyou-fuu.desc: Attacks all enemies with the wind of the sun.
rsaga2-taiyou-fuu.note: Combination art (Wind Arts + Celestial Arts). Sources list its elements as heat and lightning.

rsaga2-hellfire.note: Combination art (Fire Arts + Nether Arts). Sources list its elements as heat and cold.

rsaga2-ghost-light.desc: Charms one enemy with an eerie light.

rsaga2-poisonous-blow.desc: Attacks one enemy with a poisoned blow and poisons it.
rsaga2-poisonous-blow.note: Combination art (Water Arts + Nether Arts). Sources list its element as strike.

rsaga2-ill-storm.desc: Poisons all enemies with a storm of sickness.

rsaga2-sandstorm.desc: Attacks all enemies with a sandstorm, and may blind them.
rsaga2-sandstorm.note: Combination art (Earth Arts + Nether Arts). Sources list its elements as slash and shot.

rsaga2-wraith-form.desc: Turns the caster into a spirit, who cannot be hit by physical attacks but can only use arts.

rsaga2-dark-sphere.desc: Attacks one enemy with a sphere of darkness. The more HP the enemy currently has, the more it takes away.
rsaga2-dark-sphere.note: Combination art (Wind Arts + Nether Arts). Sources say the damage is based on the target's current HP. The sources do not state its element.

rsaga2-vortex.desc: Creates a vortex that cancels the art effects on the field.

rsaga3-wind-dart.desc: Attacks one enemy with an arrow of wind. As the art level rises, more arrows hit.
rsaga3-wind-dart.note: Azure Dragon Arts. The first art learned when you take up Azure Dragon Arts. Sources list its element as pierce.

rsaga3-dancing-leaf.desc: Wraps the target in dancing leaves, blocking physical attacks with a certain probability.
rsaga3-dancing-leaf.note: Azure Dragon Arts. Automatic recovery is also added if the terrain matches. The target differs by source (GameCenterGX and RRPG: one ally; tvgamedb: the caster), so scope was left blank. super-famicom.jp describes it as "HP recovery and defense up."

rsaga3-thorn-bind.desc: Attacks all enemies with thorns, and may knock them unconscious.
rsaga3-thorn-bind.note: Azure Dragon Arts. Sources list its element as pierce.

rsaga3-tornado.desc: Attacks all enemies with a tornado. Very effective against flying enemies.
rsaga3-tornado.note: Azure Dragon Arts. Sources list its element as pierce.

rsaga3-ryuujin-kourin.desc: Calls down the Dragon God into the caster's body, letting life force absorb the damage they take and letting them use techniques at no cost.
rsaga3-ryuujin-kourin.note: Azure Dragon Arts. The highest-tier art. tvgamedb gives its cost as 8 (not adopted). super-famicom.jp says "all stats rise greatly."

rsaga3-air-slash.desc: Cuts one enemy with a blade of wind. Very effective against flying enemies.
rsaga3-air-slash.note: Vermilion Bird Arts. The first art learned when you take up Vermilion Bird Arts. Sources list its element as slash. As the art level rises, it reaches a horizontal row.

rsaga3-hard-fire.desc: Raises the speed of one ally.

rsaga3-self-burning.desc: Wraps the caster in flames to block heat and counterattack enemies that attack directly.

rsaga3-feather-seal.desc: Hides the target behind feathers so enemies cannot target them.
rsaga3-feather-seal.note: Vermilion Bird Arts. Does not protect against area attacks. tvgamedb writes it as "フェザーシールド." The target differs by source (GameCenterGX and RRPG: one ally; tvgamedb: the caster), so scope was left blank.

rsaga3-bird-song.desc: Deals small damage to everyone, enemies and allies alike, with a bird's song, and makes casting arts harder.
rsaga3-bird-song.note: Vermilion Bird Arts. Sources list its element as sound wave. super-famicom.jp also lists an effect that wakes sleeping characters.

rsaga3-fire-wall.desc: Protects all allies from heat and cold with a wall of flame.
rsaga3-fire-wall.note: Vermilion Bird Arts. As the art level rises, it counterattacks the row of the enemy that attacked, with flames. tvgamedb writes it as "ファイアーウォール."

rsaga3-reviva.desc: Gives one ally an effect that revives them even if they are knocked out.
rsaga3-reviva.note: Vermilion Bird Arts. The highest-tier art.

rsaga3-stone-bullet.desc: Attacks one enemy with a hail of stones. As the art level rises, it reaches all enemies.
rsaga3-stone-bullet.note: White Tiger Arts. The first art learned when you take up White Tiger Arts. Sources list its element as strike.

rsaga3-berserk.desc: Greatly raises the strength and stamina of one ally.

rsaga3-crack.desc: Attacks a row of enemies with a fissure in the ground, and may knock them unconscious.
rsaga3-crack.note: White Tiger Arts. Sources list its element as pierce. The row differs by source (GameCenterGX and RRPG: a horizontal row; super-famicom.jp: a vertical column), so scope was left blank.

rsaga3-stone-skin.desc: Gradually turns the caster's body to stone, raising physical defense.

rsaga3-earth-heal.desc: Restores one ally's HP with the power of the earth.
rsaga3-earth-heal.note: White Tiger Arts. As the art level rises, it also cures mental ailments such as confusion.

rsaga3-touch-gold.desc: Turns one enemy to gold, defeating it and converting it to money.

rsaga3-chou-juuryoku.desc: Crushes enemies with gravity and lowers their speed. The heavier the enemy, the greater the damage.
rsaga3-chou-juuryoku.note: White Tiger Arts. The highest-tier art. Sources list its elements as strike and status. The target differs by source (GameCenterGX and RRPG: one enemy; tvgamedb: all enemies), so scope was left blank.

rsaga3-squall.desc: Attacks all enemies with violent rain.
rsaga3-squall.note: Black Tortoise Arts. The first art learned when you take up Black Tortoise Arts. Sources list its element as water.

rsaga3-seimei-no-mizu.note: Black Tortoise Arts. As the art level rises, it also cures sleep and paralysis.

rsaga3-shinpi-no-mizu.desc: Cures the status ailments of one ally (except petrification).

rsaga3-water-pole.desc: Wraps one ally in a shield of water, blocking physical attacks with a certain probability.
rsaga3-water-pole.note: Black Tortoise Arts. Automatic recovery is also added if the terrain matches. tvgamedb writes it as "ウォーターボール" and gives the target as the caster. super-famicom.jp describes it as "defense up and a small HP recovery."

rsaga3-sparkling-mist.desc: Lowers the accuracy of all enemies with a charged mist.

rsaga3-thunder-clap.desc: Attacks all enemies with thunder and makes casting arts harder.
rsaga3-thunder-clap.note: Black Tortoise Arts. Sources list its element as lightning.

rsaga3-quick-time.desc: Stops time for the enemy so that only your side acts for a while.
rsaga3-quick-time.note: Black Tortoise Arts. The highest-tier art. Uses all remaining JP.

rsaga3-sunshine.desc: Attacks all enemies with sunlight. Very effective against undead.
rsaga3-sunshine.note: Sun Arts. The first art learned when you take up Sun Arts. Sources list its element as heat.

rsaga3-heat-wave.desc: Attacks all enemies with a heat haze and lowers their speed.
rsaga3-heat-wave.note: Sun Arts. Sources list its element as heat. RRPG writes it as "ヒートヴェイヴ."

rsaga3-star-fixer.desc: Attacks one enemy with the power of the stars, and may paralyze it.
rsaga3-star-fixer.note: Sun Arts. Sources list its element as heat.

rsaga3-daybreak.desc: Cuts through space with the light of dawn, aiming to instantly kill all enemies.
rsaga3-daybreak.note: Sun Arts. GameCenterGX and RRPG say instant death, while super-famicom.jp and tvgamedb say unconsciousness (stun). Instant death was adopted.

rsaga3-taiyou-fuu.desc: Attacks all enemies with the wind from a small sun, and may confuse them.
rsaga3-taiyou-fuu.note: Sun Arts. Sources list multiple elements, including heat. Some sources say it is very effective against flying enemies. It can be learned only in the East. Where it is sold differs by source (super-famicom.jp: Kōkyō; tvgamedb: Genjō).

rsaga3-saiseikou.desc: Greatly restores one ally's HP and cures status ailments (except petrification).
rsaga3-saiseikou.note: Sun Arts. It can be learned only in the East. Where it is sold differs by source (super-famicom.jp: Kōkyō; tvgamedb: Genjō).

rsaga3-genjitsu.desc: Creates an illusion of the caster, making attacks easier to dodge.
rsaga3-genjitsu.note: Sun Arts. It can be learned only in the East. Where it is sold differs by source (super-famicom.jp: Kōkyō; tvgamedb: Genjō).

rsaga3-shadow-bolt.desc: Attacks one enemy with a mass of darkness and makes casting arts harder.
rsaga3-shadow-bolt.note: Moon Arts. The first art learned when you take up Moon Arts. Sources list its element as status.

rsaga3-moon-glow.desc: Raises one ally's speed and defense against arts with moonlight.

rsaga3-soul-freeze.desc: Freezes all enemies with cold, and may paralyze them.
rsaga3-soul-freeze.note: Moon Arts. Sources list its element as cold.

rsaga3-moonshine.desc: Greatly restores one ally's HP with moonlight.
rsaga3-moonshine.note: Moon Arts. As the art level rises, it also cures blindness.

rsaga3-tsukuyomi-no-kagami.desc: Cuts one enemy's HP by a proportion with the power of a mirror.
rsaga3-tsukuyomi-no-kagami.note: Moon Arts. Sources word it differently: "damage based on HP" or "halves HP." It does not work on undead. It can be learned only in the East. Where it is sold differs by source (super-famicom.jp: Kōkyō; tvgamedb: Genjō).

rsaga3-genwakukou.desc: Charms all enemies with an eerie light.
rsaga3-genwakukou.note: Moon Arts. It can be learned only in the East. Where it is sold differs by source (super-famicom.jp: Kōkyō; tvgamedb: Genjō).

rsaga3-shadow-servant.desc: Summons the caster's shadow to mimic their actions, doubling their attacks.
rsaga3-shadow-servant.note: Moon Arts. It can be learned only in the East. Where it is sold differs by source (super-famicom.jp: Kōkyō; tvgamedb: Genjō).

sf2-needle-shot.desc: Flings sharp needles to slash one enemy.
sf2-needle-shot.note: Tree Arts. A combination art of Tree + Stone. Damage element: slash. The users field lists characters who know it from the start (confirmed in only one source).

sf2-bush-fire.desc: Sets a thicket ablaze, burning the surrounding enemies together.
sf2-bush-fire.note: Tree Arts. A combination art of Tree + Fire. Damage element: heat. The users field lists characters who know it from the start (confirmed in only one source).

sf2-seimei-no-mizu.desc: Restores one ally's HP and reverts changes to their stats.
sf2-seimei-no-mizu.note: Tree Arts. A combination art of Tree + Water. The users field lists characters who know it from the start (confirmed in only one source).

sf2-woodstock.desc: Slashes one enemy with the power of wood. Very effective against plant enemies.
sf2-woodstock.note: Tree Arts. A combination art of Tree + Beast. Damage element: slash. The users field lists characters who know it from the start (confirmed in only one source).

sf2-sleep.desc: Puts the surrounding enemies to sleep.
sf2-sleep.note: Tree Arts. A combination art of Tree + Fire (the duel command is Tree, Tree, Fire).

sf2-kaze-to-ki-no-uta.desc: Shakes the hearts of all enemies with a song, causing fear and confusion.
sf2-kaze-to-ki-no-uta.note: Tree Arts. A combination art of Tree + Sound. It can be learned only through post-battle learning. Stacked fear turns into confusion.

sf2-delta-petra.desc: Slashes the enemies ahead with blades of stone, and may petrify them.
sf2-delta-petra.note: Stone Arts. A combination art of Stone + Tree. Damage element: slash. The users field lists characters who know it from the start (confirmed in only one source).

sf2-magma-plosion.desc: Spews up lava to burn the surrounding enemies.
sf2-magma-plosion.note: Stone Arts. A combination art of Stone + Fire. Damage element: heat.

sf2-water-hammer.desc: Slams a mass of water into one enemy, also unsettling its mind.
sf2-water-hammer.note: Stone Arts. A combination art of Stone + Water. Damage elements: strike and water. Inflicts fear, which turns into confusion when stacked. The users field lists characters who know it from the start (confirmed in only one source).

sf2-guard-beast.desc: Summons a guardian beast of stone to protect one ally from attacks.
sf2-guard-beast.note: Stone Arts. A combination art of Stone + Beast (the command is Stone, Stone, Beast).

sf2-rock-armor.desc: Raises one ally's Defence with armor of rock.
sf2-rock-armor.note: Stone Arts. A combination art made of Stone alone (the command is Stone, Stone, Stone).

sf2-seimei-no-ibuki.desc: Awakens one ally's vitality and cures status ailments.
sf2-seimei-no-ibuki.note: Fire Arts. A combination art of Fire + Tree. The users field lists characters who know it from the start (confirmed in only one source).

sf2-flame-naga.desc: Burns the surrounding enemies with a serpent of fire. Very effective against frog enemies.
sf2-flame-naga.note: Fire Arts. A combination art of Fire + Beast. Damage element: heat. The users field lists characters who know it from the start (confirmed in only one source).

sf2-fire-storm.desc: Burns away all enemies with a storm of fire.
sf2-fire-storm.note: Fire Arts. A combination art of Fire + Beast. Kami Game Kōryaku lists it as Fire + Tree, but the Fire + Beast of two sources was adopted. Damage element: heat. The users field lists characters who know it from the start (confirmed in only one source).

sf2-shousatsu.desc: Burns one enemy with raging flames, and may defeat it in one blow.
sf2-shousatsu.note: Fire Arts. A combination art of Fire, Tree and Stone (the command is Fire, Fire, Tree, Stone). Damage element: heat.

sf2-tamashii-no-uta.desc: Rouses all allies with a song so they recover HP every turn, and also raises Morale.
sf2-tamashii-no-uta.note: Fire Arts. A combination art of Fire, Beast and Sound. It can be learned only through post-battle learning.

sf2-doku-onpa.desc: Attacks all enemies with poison-laced sound waves, and may poison them.
sf2-doku-onpa.note: Water Arts. A combination art of Water + Sound. Damage element: sound wave. The users field lists characters who know it from the start (confirmed in only one source).

sf2-aqua-viper.desc: Sends a serpent of water racing through a row of enemies. Very effective against frog enemies.
sf2-aqua-viper.note: Water Arts. A combination art of Water + Beast. Damage element: water. The users field lists characters who know it from the start (confirmed in only one source).

sf2-shourai.desc: Calls down lightning to strike one enemy.
sf2-shourai.note: Water Arts. A combination art of Water + Sound (the command is Water, Water, Sound). Damage element: electric.

sf2-permanence.desc: Keeps the stat changes and conditions on one target exactly as they are, for a long time.
sf2-permanence.note: Water Arts. A combination art of Water, Stone and Tree (the command is Water, Water, Stone, Tree). It can be used on enemies too.

sf2-tenrai.desc: Strikes one enemy with a powerful bolt of lightning from the heavens.
sf2-tenrai.note: Water Arts. A combination art of Water, Sound and Tree (the command is Water, Water, Sound, Tree). It resembles a stronger version of Shōrai, but because the sources do not confirm any lineage between them, it is registered as a separate art. Damage element: electric.

sf2-sonic-burner.desc: Fires heat-charged sound waves ahead, attacking enemies together.
sf2-sonic-burner.note: Sound Arts. A combination art of Sound + Fire. Damage element: a mix of heat and sound wave. The users field lists characters who know it from the start (confirmed in only one source).

sf2-spoil-wave.desc: Lowers the Psycho of a row of enemies with sound waves.
sf2-spoil-wave.note: Sound Arts. A combination art of Sound + Water. It can be learned only through post-battle learning. One entry in the RRPG list can be read as Sound + Stone, but the Sound + Water of two sources was adopted.

sf2-oto-no-seiiki.desc: Wraps one ally in a clear sound, raising their Magic.
sf2-oto-no-seiiki.note: Sound Arts. A combination art of Sound + Stone.

sf2-ishi-no-kioku.desc: Calls up the memory of stone with sound, turning one enemy to stone.
sf2-ishi-no-kioku.note: Sound Arts. A combination art of Sound + Stone (the command is Sound, Sound, Stone).

sf2-seika.desc: Attacks all enemies with a pure song. Very effective against undead.
sf2-seika.note: Sound Arts. A combination art of Sound, Tree and Beast. Damage element: sound wave.

sf2-mindscape.desc: Raises the Quick of all allies.
sf2-mindscape.note: Beast Arts. A combination art of Beast + Tree. The users field lists characters who know it from the start (confirmed in only one source).

sf2-howling-heaven.desc: Attacks all enemies with a beast's echoing howl and lowers their Morale.
sf2-howling-heaven.note: Beast Arts. A combination art of Beast + Sound. It can be learned only through post-battle learning. Some sources write it as "ハウリングヘブン." Some sources say the stat it lowers is Magic, but the Morale of two sources was adopted. Damage element: sound wave.
