kh-fira.note: Standard magic. Its tier rises each time you obtain a "power of fire." The cost is in MP gauge units. The original (Japanese) version is MP 1/2, and later versions are said to be MP 1 (even sources for FINAL MIX differ between 1/2 and 1).

kh-firaga.desc: The top of the Faia line; fires the strongest ball of fire.
kh-firaga.note: Standard magic. Its tier rises each time you obtain a "power of fire." The cost is in MP gauge units. The original (Japanese) version is MP 1/2, and later versions are said to be MP 1 (even sources for FINAL MIX differ between 1/2 and 1).

kh-blizzara.desc: Fires a stronger cold blast than Burizado.

kh-blizzaga.desc: The top of the Burizado line; the strongest cold attack.

kh-thundaga.desc: The top of the Sandā line; drops strong lightning over a wide area.

kh-cure.desc: Restores HP for Sora or one party member.
kh-cure.note: Defense magic. In the original version, Kearuga fully restores HP, but in FINAL MIX the amount restored was toned down.

kh-cura.note: Defense magic. In the original version, Kearuga fully restores HP, but in FINAL MIX the amount restored was toned down.

kh-curaga.note: Defense magic. In the original version, Kearuga fully restores HP, but in FINAL MIX the amount restored was toned down.

kh-aero.desc: Surrounds one character with a wind barrier that halves the damage they take for a set time.
kh-aero.note: Defense magic. Reduces damage taken by means of a wind barrier.

kh-aerora.desc: In addition to Earo's effect, damages enemies that touch the barrier.
kh-aerora.note: Defense magic. Reduces damage taken by means of a wind barrier.

kh-aeroga.desc: In addition, the barrier can deflect enemy attacks.
kh-aeroga.note: Defense magic. Reduces damage taken by means of a wind barrier.

kh-gravity.desc: Drops a gravity sphere that cuts the HP of enemies in range by a percentage.
kh-gravity.note: Advanced magic. In this game it deals percentage-based gravity damage (later games are said to treat it as Earth-element).

kh-gravira.desc: A stronger gravity attack than Gurabide.
kh-gravira.note: Advanced magic. In this game it deals percentage-based gravity damage (later games are said to treat it as Earth-element).

kh-graviga.desc: The top of the Gurabide line; the strongest gravity attack.
kh-graviga.note: Advanced magic. In this game it deals percentage-based gravity damage (later games are said to treat it as Earth-element).

kh-stop.desc: Stops enemies within a circular area for a set time.
kh-stop.note: Advanced magic. Damage dealt while enemies are stopped lands all at once when the effect ends. The 2nd and 3rd tiers are written Sutopura and Sutopuga, not "Sutoppura."

kh-stopra.desc: Has a wider area of effect than Sutoppu.
kh-stopra.note: Advanced magic. Damage dealt while enemies are stopped lands all at once when the effect ends. The 2nd and 3rd tiers are written Sutopura and Sutopuga, not "Sutoppura."

kh-stopga.desc: The top of the Sutoppu line; stops enemies over an even wider area.
kh-stopga.note: Advanced magic. Damage dealt while enemies are stopped lands all at once when the effect ends. The 2nd and 3rd tiers are written Sutopura and Sutopuga, not "Sutoppura."

kh-simba.desc: Summons Simba, who attacks the enemies ahead with a charged roar.
kh-simba.note: MP cost 2. Donald and Goofy leave while the summon is active. Summoning stone: "Earth's Radiance."

kh-genie.desc: Summons Genie, who unleashes technique after technique on nearby enemies.
kh-genie.note: MP cost 2. Donald and Goofy leave while the summon is active.

kh-bambi.desc: Summons Bambi, who produces orbs and items that restore MP.
kh-bambi.note: MP cost 1. Donald and Goofy leave while the summon is active. Summoning stone: "Nature's Radiance."

kh-dumbo.desc: Rides Dumbo, who sprays water from his trunk to attack enemies.
kh-dumbo.note: MP cost 3 (Kōryaku no Tora says 2). Donald and Goofy leave while the summon is active. Summoning stone: "Water's Radiance."

kh-tinkerbell.desc: Summons Tinker Bell, who keeps restoring HP while summoned and revives you once when you fall.
kh-tinkerbell.note: MP cost 3. The name refers to Tinker Bell, and some sources write her name in full. Unlike the other summons, Donald and Goofy do not leave, and there is no time limit on the summon.

kh-mushu.desc: Summons Mushu, who spits fireballs at enemies.
kh-mushu.note: MP cost 3. Donald and Goofy leave while the summon is active. Summoning stone: "Flame's Radiance."

nier-kuro-no-dan.desc: Fires magic bullets that can be shot in rapid succession. Charging makes them homing.
nier-kuro-no-dan.note: Name as written in NieR Replicant ver.1.22474487139... (2021). The game has no element categories, so el is none.

nier-kuro-no-genei.desc: Sends a phantom flying forward to slash. Charging makes it hit multiple enemies around you.
nier-kuro-no-genei.note: Name as written in NieR Replicant ver.1.22474487139... (2021). The game has no element categories, so el is none.

nier-kuro-no-te.desc: Creates a giant hand that pounds the enemies ahead.
nier-kuro-no-te.note: Name as written in NieR Replicant ver.1.22474487139... (2021). The game has no element categories, so el is none.

nier-kuro-no-yari.desc: Fires a spear that reaches far and pierces enemies. Charging increases the number of spears.
nier-kuro-no-yari.note: Name as written in NieR Replicant ver.1.22474487139... (2021). The game has no element categories, so el is none.

nier-kuro-no-senbu.desc: Creates blades that orbit you and attack enemies that come near.
nier-kuro-no-senbu.note: Name as written in NieR Replicant ver.1.22474487139... (2021). The game has no element categories, so el is none.

nier-kuro-no-shokei.desc: Thrusts spears up from the ground to pierce enemies.
nier-kuro-no-shokei.note: Name as written in NieR Replicant ver.1.22474487139... (2021). The game has no element categories, so el is none.

nier-kuro-no-gouheki.desc: Raises a wall that blocks enemy magic bullets.
nier-kuro-no-gouheki.note: Name as written in NieR Replicant ver.1.22474487139... (2021). Charging makes it a wall that moves with you.

nier-kuro-no-boushoku.desc: Reflects enemy magic bullets. Charging absorbs the bullets and turns them into an attack.
nier-kuro-no-boushoku.note: Name as written in NieR Replicant ver.1.22474487139... (2021).

seiken2-icesaber.desc: Imbues a party member's weapon with the power of water, sometimes turning struck enemies into snowmen.
seiken2-icesaber.note: Magic of the spirit Undine (used by Primm).

seiken2-refresh.desc: Cures a party member's status ailments all at once.
seiken2-refresh.note: Magic of the spirit Undine (used by Primm).

seiken2-healwater.desc: Restores a party member's HP with the power of water.
seiken2-healwater.note: Magic of the spirit Undine (used by Primm).

seiken2-stonesaber.desc: Imbues a party member's weapon with the power of earth, sometimes petrifying enemies.
seiken2-stonesaber.note: Magic of the spirit Gnome (used by Primm).

seiken2-quick.desc: Raises a party member's speed (evasion and accuracy) with the power of the earth.
seiken2-quick.note: Magic of the spirit Gnome (used by Primm). The stat raised is described differently by source (wt-navi: accuracy and evasion up 25%; gcgx: evasion and attack speed up; Game Kōryaku Memo: speed up).

seiken2-protect.desc: Raises a party member's defense with the power of bedrock.
seiken2-protect.note: Magic of the spirit Gnome (used by Primm).

seiken2-thundersaber.desc: Imbues a party member's weapon with the power of wind (lightning).
seiken2-thundersaber.note: Magic of the spirit Jinn (used by Primm).

seiken2-balloon.desc: Traps an enemy in a balloon so it can barely move.
seiken2-balloon.note: Magic of the spirit Jinn (used by Primm). The status is named differently by source (gcgx, Kōryaku no Kanzume and Game Kōryaku Memo say "confusion"; wt-navi says "balloon state").

seiken2-detect.desc: Checks an enemy's HP and weaknesses, and also reveals treasure chest traps.
seiken2-detect.note: Magic of the spirit Jinn (used by Primm).

seiken2-flamesaber.desc: Imbues a party member's weapon with the power of fire, sometimes setting struck enemies ablaze.
seiken2-flamesaber.note: Magic of the spirit Salamander (used by Primm).

seiken2-firecocktail.desc: Engulfs an enemy in flames to deal damage and lower its attack.
seiken2-firecocktail.note: Magic of the spirit Salamander (used by Primm). It also deals damage, but it is treated mainly as one of Primm's support spells for lowering attack.

seiken2-blazewall.desc: Surrounds enemies with pillars of fire to deal damage and set them ablaze.
seiken2-blazewall.note: Magic of the spirit Salamander (used by Primm).

seiken2-holysaber.desc: Imbues a party member's weapon with the power of light.
seiken2-holysaber.note: Magic of the spirit Wisp (used by Primm).

seiken2-saintbeam.desc: Burns enemies with a holy beam. One of Primm's few attack spells.
seiken2-saintbeam.note: Magic of the spirit Wisp (used by Primm).

seiken2-twinklebarrier.desc: Wraps the party in a dome of light that blocks weapon attacks.
seiken2-twinklebarrier.note: Magic of the spirit Wisp (used by Primm). gcgx describes it as a barrier that reduces damage, while Game Kōryaku Memo says it blocks weapon attacks.

seiken2-moonsaber.desc: Imbues a party member's weapon with the power to drain HP from enemies they strike.
seiken2-moonsaber.note: Magic of the spirit Luna (used by Primm).

seiken2-rush.desc: Raises a party member's attack with the power of the moon.
seiken2-rush.note: Magic of the spirit Luna (used by Primm). Game Kōryaku Memo says it increases the number of attacks and their power in exchange for lower evasion.

seiken2-energyball.desc: Makes a party member's attacks more likely to land critical hits.
seiken2-energyball.note: Magic of the spirit Luna (used by Primm). gcgx and wt-navi say it guarantees critical hits, while Game Kōryaku Memo says it hands over power gauge, so the described effect differs by source.

seiken2-revive.desc: Revives a downed party member with the life force of trees.
seiken2-revive.note: Magic of the spirit Dryad (used by Primm).

seiken2-countermagic.desc: Raises a barrier that reflects enemy magic back as is.
seiken2-countermagic.note: Magic of the spirit Dryad (used by Primm).

seiken2-freeze.desc: Hits an enemy with a mass of cold water to deal damage.
seiken2-freeze.note: Magic of the spirit Undine (used by Popoi). It looks like ice, but its element is Undine (water).

seiken2-acidstorm.desc: Deals damage with a heavy rain of acid and lowers the enemy's defense.
seiken2-acidstorm.note: Magic of the spirit Undine (used by Popoi). It also deals damage, but it is treated mainly as a defense-lowering spell.

seiken2-spoit.desc: Drains an enemy's HP and adds it to your own.
seiken2-spoit.note: Magic of the spirit Undine (used by Popoi).

seiken2-earthquake.desc: Causes an earthquake that damages enemies.
seiken2-earthquake.note: Magic of the spirit Gnome (used by Popoi).

seiken2-diamissile.desc: Rains down diamond grains to damage enemies.
seiken2-diamissile.note: Magic of the spirit Gnome (used by Popoi).

seiken2-speeddown.desc: Entangles an enemy in vines and lowers its speed.
seiken2-speeddown.note: Magic of the spirit Gnome (used by Popoi). gcgx describes the status as "weight," while wt-navi says it lowers evasion.

seiken2-airblast.desc: Slashes enemies with blades of vacuum.
seiken2-airblast.note: Magic of the spirit Jinn (used by Popoi).

seiken2-thunderbolt.note: Magic of the spirit Jinn (used by Popoi). It looks like lightning, but its element is Jinn (wind).

seiken2-silence.note: Magic of the spirit Jinn (used by Popoi). Despite the name, gcgx, wt-navi, Kōryaku no Kanzume and Game Kōryaku Memo all describe the effect as "confusion."

seiken2-fireball.desc: Hurls a fireball to damage an enemy.
seiken2-fireball.note: Magic of the spirit Salamander (used by Popoi).

seiken2-explode.desc: Causes a high-heat explosion that damages enemies.
seiken2-explode.note: Magic of the spirit Salamander (used by Popoi).

seiken2-lavawave.desc: Makes lava burst from the ground to burn enemies.
seiken2-lavawave.note: Magic of the spirit Salamander (used by Popoi).

seiken2-evilgate.desc: Unleashes a wave of darkness that deals heavy damage based on the enemy's HP.
seiken2-evilgate.note: Magic of the spirit Shade (used by Popoi). The damage is determined from the enemy's current HP and maximum HP (gcgx).

seiken2-darkforce.desc: Damages enemies with a wave of darkness.
seiken2-darkforce.note: Magic of the spirit Shade (used by Popoi).

seiken2-antimagic.desc: Erases support magic placed on an enemy.
seiken2-antimagic.note: Magic of the spirit Shade (used by Popoi).

seiken2-bodychange.desc: Turns an enemy into a low-level monster.
seiken2-bodychange.note: Magic of the spirit Luna (used by Popoi).

seiken2-absorb.desc: Drains an enemy's MP and adds it to your own.
seiken2-absorb.note: Magic of the spirit Luna (used by Popoi).

seiken2-lunatic.desc: Causes a mysterious effect on all enemies and allies, and no one can tell what will happen.
seiken2-lunatic.note: Magic of the spirit Luna (used by Popoi). Possible effects include raising or lowering stats, changing form, confusion and HP recovery (Game Kōryaku Memo).

seiken2-sleepflower.desc: Sends petals swirling to put enemies to sleep.
seiken2-sleepflower.note: Magic of the spirit Dryad (used by Popoi).

seiken2-burst.desc: Makes the life force of trees explode inside an enemy's body.
seiken2-burst.note: Magic of the spirit Dryad (used by Popoi).

seiken2-mana.desc: Turns Randi's Holy Sword into the true "Mana Sword."
seiken2-mana.note: Magic of the spirit Dryad, usable by both Primm and Popoi. It only has an effect when Randi has the sword equipped in the final boss battle.

seiken3-heallight.desc: Restores allies' HP with the power of light.
seiken3-heallight.note: Wisp (Light) element. Usable by all 13 classes (users lists only some).

seiken3-tinklerain.desc: Cures allies' status ailments with a rain of light.
seiken3-tinklerain.note: Wisp (Light) element. Usable by all 8 classes (users lists only some).

seiken3-holyball.desc: A low-tier Light attack spell that hurls a ball of light.
seiken3-holyball.note: Wisp (Light) element. Usable by all 10 classes (users lists only some).

seiken3-saintbeam.desc: A mid-tier Light attack spell that burns enemies with a holy beam.

seiken3-saintsaber.desc: Gives an ally's weapon the Light element.

seiken3-magicshield.note: Wisp (Light) element. opatil says it raises magic defense by 20%.

seiken3-turnundead.desc: Wipes out only the undead among the enemies in a single blow.
seiken3-turnundead.note: Has no effect on anything other than the undead.

seiken3-diamissile.desc: A low-tier Earth attack spell that fires grains of gemstone.
seiken3-diamissile.note: Gnome (Earth) element. Usable by all 7 classes (users lists only some).

seiken3-earthquake.desc: A mid-tier Earth attack spell that causes an earthquake.

seiken3-stonecloud.desc: A high-tier Earth attack spell that wraps enemies in a cloud of stone and can petrify them.

seiken3-diasaber.desc: Gives an ally's weapon the Earth element.
seiken3-diasaber.note: Gnome (Earth) element. Usable by all 6 classes (users lists only some).

seiken3-speeddown.note: Gnome (Earth) element. Both gcgx and opatil say it is evasion that goes down.

seiken3-airblast.desc: A low-tier Wind attack spell that fires blades of gusting wind.
seiken3-airblast.note: Jinn (Wind) element. Usable by all 7 classes (users lists only some).

seiken3-thunderstorm.desc: A mid-tier Wind attack spell that summons a storm of lightning.
seiken3-thunderstorm.note: Jinn (Wind) element. It looks like lightning, but its element is Jinn (Wind).

seiken3-stunwind.desc: A high-tier Wind attack spell that strikes enemies with fierce wind and can silence them.
seiken3-stunwind.note: Jinn (Wind) element. nJOY writes the name as スタンウインド.

seiken3-thundersaber.desc: Gives an ally's weapon the Wind (lightning) element.
seiken3-thundersaber.note: Jinn (Wind) element. Usable by all 6 classes (users lists only some).

seiken3-speedup.note: Jinn (Wind) element. Both gcgx and opatil say it is evasion that goes up.

seiken3-icesmash.desc: A low-tier Water attack spell that drops a block of ice.
seiken3-icesmash.note: Undine (Water) element. It looks like ice, but its element is Undine (Water). Usable by all 7 classes (users lists only some).

seiken3-megasplash.desc: A mid-tier Water attack spell that drenches enemies with a huge amount of water.

seiken3-coldblaze.desc: A high-tier Water attack spell that wraps enemies in freezing cold and can turn them into snowmen.
seiken3-coldblaze.note: Undine (Water) element. The element is Undine (Water).

seiken3-icesaber.desc: Gives an ally's weapon the Water (ice) element.
seiken3-icesaber.note: Undine (Water) element. Usable by all 6 classes (users lists only some).

seiken3-mindup.note: Undine (Water) element. Both gcgx and opatil describe it as a magic defense boost.

seiken3-fireball.desc: A low-tier Fire attack spell that hurls a fireball.
seiken3-fireball.note: Salamander (Fire) element. Usable by all 7 classes (users lists only some).

seiken3-explode.desc: A mid-tier Fire attack spell that causes an explosion.

seiken3-blazewall.desc: A high-tier Fire attack spell that surrounds enemies with a wall of flame and can set them ablaze.

seiken3-flamesaber.desc: Gives an ally's weapon the Fire element.
seiken3-flamesaber.note: Salamander (Fire) element. Usable by all 6 classes (users lists only some).

seiken3-minddown.note: Salamander (Fire) element. Both gcgx and opatil describe it as a magic defense reduction.

seiken3-demonbreath.desc: Burns all enemies with a demon's fiery breath.
seiken3-demonbreath.note: Salamander (Fire) element. MP and element are confirmed in only one source (gcgx; it does not appear in opatil's list). The classes that learn it are also confirmed by nJOY and plasmasphere.

seiken3-evilgate.desc: A low-tier Darkness attack spell that opens a gate of darkness to attack enemies.
seiken3-evilgate.note: Shade (Darkness) element. Usable by all 7 classes (users lists only some).

seiken3-darkforce.desc: A mid-tier Darkness attack spell that hurls the power of darkness.

seiken3-deathspell.desc: A high-tier Darkness spell that instantly kills one enemy with a death curse.
seiken3-deathspell.note: Shade (Darkness) element. It is the third tier of the Darkness attack spells, but it is placed in a separate line because its effect is instant death.

seiken3-darksaber.desc: Gives an ally's weapon the Darkness element.

seiken3-blackcurse.desc: Lowers several of an enemy's stats at once with a curse.

seiken3-antimagic.desc: Cancels the effects of magic on an enemy.

seiken3-moonsaber.desc: Gives an ally's weapon the power to drain HP from the enemies it strikes.

seiken3-lifebooster.note: Luna (Moon) element. opatil says it raises maximum HP by 20%.

seiken3-energyball.desc: A spell that is supposed to make allies' attacks more likely to be critical hits.
seiken3-energyball.note: Luna (Moon) element. The effect does not work in the SFC version (gcgx says "the effect is not implemented" and opatil says "effectively no effect").

seiken3-bodychange.desc: Changes an enemy into something else.

seiken3-lunatic.note: Luna (Moon) element. Its effect differs from the same-named spell in Secret of Mana (random effects). opatil says it lowers maximum HP by 20%.

seiken3-transshape.desc: Makes an ally transparent so that they take no physical attacks.
seiken3-transshape.note: Luna (Moon) element. gcgx calls it the "invisible" status, while opatil says it nullifies physical attacks.

seiken3-sleepflower.desc: Puts enemies to sleep with the scent of flowers.

seiken3-poisonbubble.desc: Inflicts deadly poison on an enemy with poison bubbles.
seiken3-poisonbubble.note: Dryad (Wood) element. gcgx says it also restores the user's MP.

seiken3-leafsaber.desc: Gives an ally's weapon the power to drain MP from the enemies it strikes.

seiken3-countermagic.desc: Raises a barrier that reflects enemy magic.

seiken3-hikou.desc: Strikes pressure points on the body to raise your own attack.
seiken3-hikou.note: gcgx says it raises attack by 1/3, while opatil says attack up 30%. opatil classifies it under "other skills," not magic.

seiken3-doublespell.desc: A grand spell of the Light class Grandevina that deals heavy damage to all enemies.

seiken3-rainbowdust.desc: A grand spell of the Ākumeiji class that attacks all enemies with rainbow-colored light.

seiken3-ancient.desc: A grand spell of the Meigasu class that deals heavy damage to all enemies with ancient power.
seiken3-ancient.note: plasmasphere writes the name as エインシェント.

seiken3-unicornhead.desc: Summons a unicorn's head to attack one enemy.

seiken3-machinegolem.desc: Summons a mechanical giant to attack one enemy.

seiken3-ghoul.desc: Summons a ghoul to attack one enemy.

seiken3-ghost.desc: Summons a ghost to attack one enemy.

seiken3-gremlin.desc: Summons the imp Gremlin to attack one enemy.

seiken3-greatdemon.desc: Summons a great demon to attack one enemy.
seiken3-greatdemon.note: plasmasphere writes the name as グレードデーモン.

seiken3-freya.desc: Summons the goddess Freya to damage all enemies and shrink them.

seiken3-marduk.desc: Summons the god Marduk to damage all enemies and silence them.

seiken3-jormungand.desc: Summons the great serpent Jormungand to damage all enemies and inflict deadly poison.

seiken3-lamiannaga.desc: Summons Ramiannāga to attack all enemies.

seiken3-shuriken.note: gcgx says it also lowers accuracy. opatil classifies it as a "throwing special attack" special attack.

seiken3-suiton.desc: Deals damage with water-controlling ninjutsu and lowers the enemy's attack.
seiken3-suiton.note: Undine (Water) element. opatil classifies it as a "ninjutsu special attack" special attack.

seiken3-katon.desc: Deals damage with fire-controlling ninjutsu and lowers the enemy's magic defense.
seiken3-katon.note: Salamander (Fire) element. opatil classifies it as a "ninjutsu special attack" special attack.

seiken3-doton.desc: Deals damage with earth-controlling ninjutsu and lowers the enemy's speed.
seiken3-doton.note: Gnome (Earth) element. opatil classifies it as a "ninjutsu special attack" special attack.

seiken3-raijin.desc: Deals damage with lightning-summoning ninjutsu and lowers the enemy's defense.
seiken3-raijin.note: Jinn (Wind) element. It looks like lightning, but its element is Jinn (Wind). opatil classifies it as a "ninjutsu special attack" special attack.

seiken3-yumiya.desc: Shoots an enemy with a set-up bow and arrow.
seiken3-yumiya.note: opatil classifies it as a "trap special attack" special attack.

seiken3-spike.desc: Attacks by thrusting spikes up from the ground and lowers accuracy.
seiken3-spike.note: opatil classifies it as a "trap special attack" special attack.

seiken3-gansekirakka.desc: Attacks by dropping a rock from overhead.
seiken3-gansekirakka.note: opatil classifies it as a "trap special attack" special attack.

seiken3-jirai.desc: Attacks by detonating a land mine.
seiken3-jirai.note: opatil classifies it as a "trap special attack" special attack.

seiken3-dokugiribreath.desc: Deals damage by spraying poison mist and inflicts deadly poison.
seiken3-dokugiribreath.note: opatil classifies it as a "ninjutsu special attack" special attack.

seiken3-kaenbreath.desc: Burns enemies by breathing fire from the mouth.
seiken3-kaenbreath.note: The element in the sources is non-elemental (-), but it is set to fire because it is a flame attack. opatil classifies it as a "ninjutsu special attack" special attack.

seiken3-fukumibari.desc: Spits a needle held in the mouth to deal damage and silence the target.
seiken3-fukumibari.note: gcgx writes the name as ふくみ針. nJOY, opatil and plasmasphere write 含み針.

seiken3-kyoukikougeki.desc: Strikes with a hidden weapon and reduces maximum HP.
seiken3-kyoukikougeki.note: opatil classifies it as a "throwing special attack" special attack.

seiken3-blackrain.desc: Attacks all enemies with a rain of darkness.
seiken3-blackrain.note: Shade (Darkness) element. opatil classifies it as a "ninjutsu special attack" special attack.

seiken3-silverdarts.note: Wisp (Light) element. opatil classifies it as a "throwing special attack" special attack.

seiken3-cuttermissile.note: opatil classifies it as a "throwing special attack" special attack.

seiken3-engetsurin.note: Shade (Darkness) element. opatil classifies it as a "throwing special attack" special attack.

seiken3-rocketlauncher.note: Salamander (Fire) element. gcgx writes the name as ロケットランチャ, while nJOY, opatil and plasmasphere write ロケットランチャー. opatil classifies it as a "throwing special attack" special attack.

seiken3-axebomber.note: opatil classifies it as a "throwing special attack" special attack.

seiken3-grenadebomb.note: Dryad (Wood) element. The element is Wood. gcgx says it also restores the user's MP. The target is single according to nJOY and opatil, but gcgx's Rōgu page says all enemies. opatil classifies it as a "throwing special attack" special attack.

makamaka-aisu.desc: Deals small damage to one enemy with cold.
makamaka-aisu.note: The protagonist can use it from the start.

makamaka-daburuaisu.desc: Deals medium damage to one enemy with cold.
makamaka-daburuaisu.note: Learned at Lv10. Confirmed in only one source (GAME CENTER GX's transformation move list).

makamaka-megatonaisu.desc: Deals heavy damage to one enemy with a giant block of ice.

makamaka-furiza.desc: Deals small damage to all enemies with cold.
makamaka-furiza.note: Learned at Lv6. Confirmed in only one source (GAME CENTER GX's transformation move list).

makamaka-burizado.desc: Deals medium damage to all enemies with cold.
makamaka-burizado.note: Learned at Lv24. Confirmed in only one source (GAME CENTER GX's transformation move list).

makamaka-burisutomu.desc: Deals heavy damage to all enemies with fierce cold.

makamaka-hiru.desc: Restores a little of one ally's HP.
makamaka-hiru.note: Learned at Lv5. Used in a glitch that increases TP when cast while moving.

makamaka-berihiru.desc: Restores a moderate amount of one ally's HP.
makamaka-berihiru.note: The girlfriend has it from the start, and the protagonist learns it at Lv12. GAME CENTER GX writes the protagonist's version as Berihīru (the TP cost and healing amount are the same as the girlfriend's Berīhīru). Because the play diary also calls the protagonist's move Berīhīru, they are merged into one entry as the same move.

makamaka-besutohiru.desc: Restores a large amount of one ally's HP.
makamaka-besutohiru.note: Learned at Lv15. Confirmed in only one source (GAME CENTER GX's transformation move list).

makamaka-hirupati.desc: Restores a moderate amount of all allies' HP.
makamaka-hirupati.note: The protagonist learns it at Lv32 and the girlfriend at Lv22. The same guide site's "Tips, Tricks and Glitches" page also gives the TP cost as 16 (not counted as a separate source because it is the same site). Confirmed in only one source (GAME CENTER GX's transformation move list).

makamaka-terepoto.note: The protagonist learns it at Lv14 and the girlfriend at Lv21. There is a glitch where, in effect, only the protagonist's transformation moves can be used while moving. Confirmed in only one source (GAME CENTER GX's transformation move list).

makamaka-antienemi.desc: Stops enemies from appearing for a while.
makamaka-antienemi.note: Learned at Lv26. The effect lasts 50 steps. Confirmed in only one source (GAME CENTER GX's transformation move list).

makamaka-suterusu.desc: Stops enemies from appearing for a while.
makamaka-suterusu.note: Learned at Lv34. The sources give the same "50 steps" as Anchienemī, and we could not confirm why the TP cost differs. Confirmed in only one source (GAME CENTER GX's transformation move list).

makamaka-sodoatakku.desc: Deals small damage to one group of enemies with a sword.
makamaka-sodoatakku.note: Learned at Lv3. Confirmed in only one source (GAME CENTER GX's transformation move list).

makamaka-sodokurasshu.desc: Readies a sword and charges one group of enemies for medium damage.

makamaka-sodobiggubban.desc: Charges one group of enemies with a sword for heavy damage.

makamaka-zakodasuto.desc: Wipes out weak enemies all at once.
makamaka-zakodasuto.note: Learned at Lv8. Targets enemies of Lv5 or below. The Hissatsuwaza Jiten (special-move dictionary) and the play diary write "zako" in katakana (the three moves Zakodasuto, Zakodesutoroi and Jenosaidozako). Here the spelling follows GAME CENTER GX.

makamaka-zakodesutoroi.desc: Wipes out enemies, including somewhat stronger ones, all at once.
makamaka-zakodesutoroi.note: Learned at Lv22. Targets enemies of Lv12 or below. The Hissatsuwaza Jiten (special-move dictionary) and the play diary write "zako" in katakana (the three moves Zakodasuto, Zakodesutoroi and Jenosaidozako). Here the spelling follows GAME CENTER GX.

makamaka-jenosaidozako.desc: Wipes out enemies, including fairly strong ones, all at once.
makamaka-jenosaidozako.note: Learned at Lv40. Targets enemies of Lv32 or below. The Hissatsuwaza Jiten (special-move dictionary) and the play diary write "zako" in katakana (the three moves Zakodasuto, Zakodesutoroi and Jenosaidozako). Here the spelling follows GAME CENTER GX.

makamaka-hottoboru.desc: Deals small damage to one group of enemies with a fireball.
makamaka-hottoboru.note: Learned at Lv6. The Hissatsuwaza Jiten gives the target as "one enemy," which conflicts with GAME CENTER GX's "group." The play diary says soldiers of the Nyabanyaba tribe in the past-life world also use it.

makamaka-faiyaboru.desc: Deals medium damage to one group of enemies with a fireball.
makamaka-faiyaboru.note: Learned at Lv16. Confirmed in only one source (GAME CENTER GX's transformation move list).

makamaka-magumaboru.desc: Deals heavy damage to one group of enemies with a superheated magma shot.
makamaka-magumaboru.note: Learned at Lv27. The Hissatsuwaza Jiten gives the target as "one enemy," which conflicts with GAME CENTER GX's "group."

makamaka-kaen.desc: Deals small damage to all enemies with flame.
makamaka-kaen.note: Available from the start. Confirmed in only one source (GAME CENTER GX's transformation move list).

makamaka-daikaen.desc: Deals medium damage to all enemies with flame.
makamaka-daikaen.note: Learned at Lv12. Confirmed in only one source (GAME CENTER GX's transformation move list).

makamaka-shakunetsukaen.desc: Deals heavy damage to all enemies with pillars of fire.
makamaka-shakunetsukaen.note: Learned at Lv32. The Hissatsuwaza Jiten writes it in kanji as 灼熱火炎.

makamaka-dokukieru.note: Learned at Lv12. Works on both poison and deadly poison. Confirmed in only one source (GAME CENTER GX's transformation move list).

makamaka-tachinaoru.desc: Cures all of one ally's in-battle status ailments at once.
makamaka-tachinaoru.note: Learned at Lv13. Cures Boneless, Off Guard, confusion and paralysis. Confirmed in only one source (GAME CENTER GX's transformation move list).

makamaka-shibirekousen.note: Available from the start. Confirmed in only one source (GAME CENTER GX's transformation move list).

makamaka-shibirebimu.note: Learned at Lv14. Confirmed in only one source (GAME CENTER GX's transformation move list).

makamaka-shibiresupaku.desc: Paralyzes all enemies with a dazzling light.

makamaka-rinnenokabe.desc: Makes the lead ally invulnerable for a time.
makamaka-rinnenokabe.note: Learned at Lv28. The effect applies only to the character at the front of the formation and lasts 3 turns, including the turn it is used. Confirmed in only one source (GAME CENTER GX's transformation move list).

makamaka-denkinojikken.desc: Deals small damage to one enemy with electricity.

makamaka-honoonojikken.desc: Deals small damage to all enemies with flame.
makamaka-honoonojikken.note: Available from the start. Damage is 45 in GAME CENTER GX and "around 50" in the play diary.

makamaka-fubukinojikken.desc: Deals heavy damage to all enemies with a blizzard.
makamaka-fubukinojikken.note: Learned at Lv36. The play diary writes it in kanji as 吹雪の実験.

makamaka-kaifukunochie.desc: Restores a little of one ally's HP.
makamaka-kaifukunochie.note: Available from the start. Confirmed in only one source (GAME CENTER GX's transformation move list).

makamaka-igakunochie.desc: Cures all of one ally's status ailments at once.
makamaka-igakunochie.note: Learned at Lv3. Cannot cure being knocked out (groggy). Confirmed in only one source (GAME CENTER GX's transformation move list).

makamaka-dasshutsunochie.note: Learned at Lv5. There is a glitch where, in effect, only the protagonist's transformation moves can be used while moving. Confirmed in only one source (GAME CENTER GX's transformation move list).

makamaka-inubue.desc: Deals small damage to one group of enemies with a whistle technique.
makamaka-inubue.note: Available from the start. Confirmed in only one source (GAME CENTER GX's transformation move list).

makamaka-toribue.desc: Deals small damage to one group of enemies with a whistle technique.
makamaka-toribue.note: Learned at Lv4. Confirmed in only one source (GAME CENTER GX's transformation move list).

makamaka-sarubue.desc: Deals heavy damage to one group of enemies with a whistle technique.
makamaka-sarubue.note: Learned at Lv33. Confirmed in only one source (GAME CENTER GX's transformation move list).

makamaka-yubiwomawasu.desc: Makes all enemies Boneless and saps their attack.
makamaka-yubiwomawasu.note: Learned at Lv6. In the game it inflicts the Boneless status ailment (attacks barely work; the sources say it only works on males). Confirmed in only one source (GAME CENTER GX's transformation move list).

makamaka-yubiwosasu.desc: Puts all enemies Off Guard and lowers their defense.
makamaka-yubiwosasu.note: Learned at Lv9. In the game it inflicts the Off Guard status ailment (defense is halved). Confirmed in only one source (GAME CENTER GX's transformation move list).

makamaka-tsubamegaeshi.desc: Deals medium damage to one enemy with a sword.
makamaka-tsubamegaeshi.note: Available from the start. Confirmed in only one source (GAME CENTER GX's transformation move list).

makamaka-hayabusagaeshi.desc: Slashes quickly, dealing medium damage to one group of enemies.
makamaka-hayabusagaeshi.note: Learned at Lv11. The Hissatsuwaza Jiten writes it as はやぶさ返し and gives the target as "one enemy." The target follows GAME CENTER GX and the play diary, which say "group."

makamaka-ashuragaeshi.desc: Slashes one enemy for extra-large damage.
makamaka-ashuragaeshi.note: Learned at Lv40. The Hissatsuwaza Jiten writes it as あしゅら返し.

makamaka-senpuugiri.desc: Deals small damage to all enemies with a sword.
makamaka-senpuugiri.note: Learned at Lv13. Confirmed in only one source (GAME CENTER GX's transformation move list).

makamaka-engetsugiri.desc: Deals medium damage to all enemies with a sword.
makamaka-engetsugiri.note: Learned at Lv18. The Hissatsuwaza Jiten writes it as 円月斬り.

makamaka-dotougiri.desc: Slashes all enemies one after another for heavy damage.
makamaka-dotougiri.note: Learned at Lv37. Has an added paralysis effect. The Hissatsuwaza Jiten writes it as 怒涛斬り.

makamaka-atomikkuburo.desc: Deals medium Electric damage to one enemy with a ball of light.
makamaka-atomikkuburo.note: Available from the start. Has an added paralysis effect.

makamaka-fotonburo.desc: Deals medium Electric damage to one enemy with a powerful ball of light.
makamaka-fotonburo.note: Learned at Lv14. Has an added paralysis effect.

makamaka-mirakuruburo.desc: Deals heavy Electric damage to one enemy with a finishing ball of light.
makamaka-mirakuruburo.note: Learned at Lv30. Has an added confusion effect (however, GAME CENTER GX's status explanation says confusion is unused data).

makamaka-purazumasupaku.desc: Deals small damage to all enemies with an electric shock.
makamaka-purazumasupaku.note: Available from the start. Confirmed in only one source (GAME CENTER GX's transformation move list).

makamaka-takionsupaku.desc: Deals medium damage to all enemies with a flash of electric shock.
makamaka-takionsupaku.note: Learned at Lv19. Has an added paralysis effect.

makamaka-omegasupaku.desc: Deals heavy damage to all enemies with an intense flash of electric shock.

makamaka-aisushotto.desc: Deals small damage to one group of enemies with a freezing beam.

makamaka-magumashotto.desc: Deals medium damage to one group of enemies with a superheated beam.

makamaka-maindoshotto.desc: Deals medium damage to one group of enemies with a mental wave.
makamaka-maindoshotto.note: Learned at Lv22. Its in-game element is "Mind." Has an added confusion effect (however, GAME CENTER GX's status explanation says confusion is unused data).

makamaka-heroherobimu.desc: Lowers the attack of one group of enemies.
makamaka-heroherobimu.note: Learned at Lv13. Can be stacked (play diary).

makamaka-funyarakabimu.desc: Lowers the defense of one group of enemies.
makamaka-funyarakabimu.note: Learned at Lv16. Confirmed in only one source (GAME CENTER GX's transformation move list).

makamaka-noronorobimu.desc: Lowers the speed of one group of enemies.
makamaka-noronorobimu.note: Learned at Lv17. Confirmed in only one source (GAME CENTER GX's transformation move list).

makamaka-baria.note: Learned at Lv13. Confirmed in only one source (GAME CENTER GX's transformation move list).

makamaka-orabaria.desc: Makes all allies immune to elemental attacks.
makamaka-orabaria.note: Learned at Lv21. Lasts 3 turns, including the turn it is used. Confirmed in only one source (GAME CENTER GX's transformation move list).

makamaka-firudobaria.desc: Makes all allies immune to physical and elemental attacks.
makamaka-firudobaria.note: Learned at Lv28. Lasts 3 turns, including the turn it is used. The play diary also writes it as フィールドバリアー and says some non-elemental special attacks cannot be blocked. The boss Dr. Makamaka also uses it.

makamaka-kaifukupawa.note: Learned at Lv20. Confirmed in only one source (GAME CENTER GX's transformation move list).

makamaka-terepotopawa.note: Learned at Lv24. There is a glitch where Uruuru Boy can barely use transformation moves while moving.

makamaka-supapawa.desc: Greatly raises your own attack, defense and speed.
makamaka-supapawa.note: Learned at Lv26. Confirmed in only one source (GAME CENTER GX's transformation move list).

makamaka-kizunaoshi.note: Available from the start. Confirmed in only one source (GAME CENTER GX's transformation move list).

makamaka-ookeganaoshi.desc: Restores a good amount of one ally's HP.
makamaka-ookeganaoshi.note: Available from the start. Confirmed in only one source (GAME CENTER GX's transformation move list).

makamaka-kanpekinaoshi.desc: Restores a large amount of one ally's HP.
makamaka-kanpekinaoshi.note: Available from the start. Confirmed in only one source (GAME CENTER GX's transformation move list).

makamaka-minnanoteate.desc: Restores a moderate amount of all allies' HP.
makamaka-minnanoteate.note: Learned at Lv25. Confirmed in only one source (GAME CENTER GX's transformation move list).

makamaka-saikounoteate.desc: Restores a large amount of all allies' HP.
makamaka-saikounoteate.note: Learned at Lv32. Confirmed in only one source (GAME CENTER GX's transformation move list).

makamaka-ainokunekune.desc: Revives one knocked-out ally in perfect condition.
makamaka-ainokunekune.note: It is not learned by leveling; you get it in an event by talking to Nasutāsha at the hospital in the past-life world. It also fully restores HP and removes status ailments (play diary). The play diary writes it as 愛のクネクネ.

makamaka-dokunochiryou.note: Available from the start. Works on both poison and deadly poison. Confirmed in only one source (GAME CENTER GX's transformation move list).

makamaka-kazenochiryou.note: Available from the start. Confirmed in only one source (GAME CENTER GX's transformation move list).

makamaka-shokkuchiryou.desc: Cures all of one ally's in-battle status ailments at once.
makamaka-shokkuchiryou.note: Available from the start. Cures Boneless, Off Guard, confusion and paralysis. Confirmed in only one source (GAME CENTER GX's transformation move list).

makamaka-masuichusha.note: Learned at Lv24. The Gēm Tōshi.com walkthrough chart writes it as ますいちゅうしゃ. The GAME CENTER GX spelling is used here.

makamaka-nousatsupozu.desc: Makes all enemies Boneless and saps their attack.
makamaka-nousatsupozu.note: Learned at Lv25. In the game it inflicts the Boneless status ailment (90% success rate). Confirmed in only one source (GAME CENTER GX's transformation move list).

makamaka-zettaiansei.note: Learned at Lv36. 80% success rate. Confirmed in only one source (GAME CENTER GX's transformation move list).

makamaka-faitoippatsu.note: Learned at Lv26. Confirmed in only one source (GAME CENTER GX's transformation move list).

makamaka-dasshuippatsu.note: Learned at Lv26. Confirmed in only one source (GAME CENTER GX's transformation move list).

makamaka-gadoippatsu.note: Learned at Lv26. Confirmed in only one source (GAME CENTER GX's transformation move list).

makamaka-faitorenpatsu.note: Learned at Lv34. Confirmed in only one source (GAME CENTER GX's transformation move list).

makamaka-dasshurenpatsu.note: Learned at Lv34. The boost (+10) is smaller than the single-target version (+20). Confirmed in only one source (GAME CENTER GX's transformation move list).

makamaka-gadorenpatsu.note: Learned at Lv34. Confirmed in only one source (GAME CENTER GX's transformation move list).

makamaka-dopingu.desc: Raises the power of one ally's critical hits.
makamaka-dopingu.note: Learned at Lv28. Power is doubled. In this game, "special moves" means critical hits, and this raises their power. The effect lasts 4 turns, including the turn it is used. Confirmed in only one source (GAME CENTER GX's transformation move list).

makamaka-supadopin.desc: Greatly raises the power of one ally's critical hits.
makamaka-supadopin.note: Learned at Lv38. Power is tripled. In this game, "special moves" means critical hits, and this raises their power. The effect lasts 4 turns, including the turn it is used. Confirmed in only one source (GAME CENTER GX's transformation move list).

makamaka-haipadopin.desc: Raises the power of one ally's critical hits enormously.
makamaka-haipadopin.note: Learned at Lv40. Power is quintupled. In this game, "special moves" means critical hits, and this raises their power. The effect lasts 4 turns, including the turn it is used. Confirmed in only one source (GAME CENTER GX's transformation move list).

makamaka-roukahashizukani.note: Learned at Lv30. Confirmed in only one source (GAME CENTER GX's transformation move list).

makamaka-kenkahayamete.note: Learned at Lv30. Confirmed in only one source (GAME CENTER GX's transformation move list).

makamaka-rirakkushitene.note: Learned at Lv30. Confirmed in only one source (GAME CENTER GX's transformation move list).

makamaka-tsuppari.desc: Deals medium damage to one enemy with a palm thrust.
makamaka-tsuppari.note: Available from the start. Confirmed in only one source (GAME CENTER GX's transformation move list).

makamaka-ootsuppari.desc: Deals medium damage to one enemy with a powerful palm thrust.
makamaka-ootsuppari.note: Learned at Lv32. The Hissatsuwaza Jiten writes it as 大つっぱり.

makamaka-toripurutsuppari.desc: Deals heavy damage to one enemy with a triple palm-thrust combo.

makamaka-kamashi.desc: Deals small damage to one group of enemies with a body slam.
makamaka-kamashi.note: Available from the start. Confirmed in only one source (GAME CENTER GX's transformation move list).

makamaka-buchikamashi.desc: Deals medium damage to one group of enemies with a body slam.
makamaka-buchikamashi.note: Learned at Lv33. Confirmed in only one source (GAME CENTER GX's transformation move list).

makamaka-bukkamashi.desc: Crashes in with a huge body, dealing heavy damage to one group of enemies.

makamaka-shikofumi.desc: Stomps like a sumo wrestler to shake the ground, dealing small damage to all enemies.
makamaka-shikofumi.note: Available from the start. Confirmed in only one source (GAME CENTER GX's transformation move list).

makamaka-shikofumibomu.note: Learned at Lv37. 60% success rate. Confirmed in only one source (GAME CENTER GX's transformation move list).

makamaka-shikofumibonba.desc: Defeats weak enemies all at once.
makamaka-shikofumibonba.note: Learned at Lv39. 60% success rate. The Hissatsuwaza Jiten describes it as a move that splits the ground with a stomp and drops enemies into it.

makamaka-jikanippai.desc: Slightly raises your own attack, defense and speed.
makamaka-jikanippai.note: Available from the start. Confirmed in only one source (GAME CENTER GX's transformation move list).

makamaka-shiomaki.desc: Lowers the defense and speed of one group of enemies.
makamaka-shiomaki.note: Learned at Lv31. It lowers speed at the same time. Confirmed in only one source (GAME CENTER GX's transformation move list).

makamaka-sekushipozu.desc: Deals mental damage to all enemies and can inflict status ailments.
makamaka-sekushipozu.note: Learned at Lv35. Its in-game element is "Mind." Has added Boneless, Off Guard, confusion and paralysis effects.

makamaka-renzokuuchi.desc: Fires a gun in rapid succession, dealing medium damage to one group of enemies.
makamaka-renzokuuchi.note: Available from the start. Confirmed in only one source (GAME CENTER GX's transformation move list).

makamaka-midareuchi.desc: Fires wildly, dealing medium damage to all enemies.
makamaka-midareuchi.note: Available from the start. Confirmed in only one source (GAME CENTER GX's transformation move list).

makamaka-hachinosuuchi.desc: Sprays gunfire, dealing heavy damage to all enemies.
makamaka-hachinosuuchi.note: Learned at Lv35. The Hissatsuwaza Jiten writes it as 蜂の巣撃ち.

makamaka-nirami.desc: Glares to lower all enemies' attack and defense.
makamaka-nirami.note: Available from the start. Has an added paralysis effect. Confirmed in only one source (GAME CENTER GX's transformation move list).

makamaka-hikiage.note: Available from the start. Because of a glitch, it does not actually use any TP (GAME CENTER GX).

makamaka-hissatsushotto.desc: Shoots a vital spot to defeat one weak enemy.
makamaka-hissatsushotto.note: Learned at Lv33. Always works on weak enemies and never on bosses. The Hissatsuwaza Jiten writes it as 必殺ショット.

tales-faiaboru.desc: Fires several fireballs at the enemies ahead.
tales-faiaboru.note: Magic. Fire element. Usable from the start. The number of fireballs grows as the level rises. The spelling Faiabōru follows Game Log and the glossary dictionary (the glossary says the SFC version uses Faiāboru, and the PS version onward uses Faiabōru). Majestic Fantasian and kouryaku.sub.jp's PS version table write it as Faiāboru.

tales-aisuniidoru.desc: Attacks enemies by raining down many ice needles.
tales-aisuniidoru.note: Magic. Water element in this game. Usable from the start. The number of needles grows as the level rises.

tales-sutoonburasuto.desc: Attacks enemies by raining down many stones.
tales-sutoonburasuto.note: Magic. Earth element. Added in the PS version. In the past, it is on the bookshelf in Klarth's house in Yūkuriddo; in the future, it is bought in Rōnvarei (250 Gald according to Game Log).

tales-raitoningu.desc: Attacks one enemy by dropping a small bolt of lightning.
tales-raitoningu.note: Magic. Lightning element. Bought in Benetsia for 200 Gald. In the SFC version the cost is TP 4.

tales-sutoomu.desc: Attacks enemies by whipping up a strong wind across the whole screen.
tales-sutoomu.note: Magic. Wind element. Bought in Benetsia for 1000 Gald. The range is one screen according to Majestic Fantasian and medium according to Game Log.

tales-gureibu.desc: Attacks by thrusting stone spears up from under the enemy's feet.
tales-gureibu.note: Magic. Earth element. Obtained in the Cave of Spirits. It was an early spell in the SFC version (TP 4), but in the PS version Sutōnburasuto was added and Gureibu became a mid-tier spell.

tales-aisutoneedo.desc: Attacks an enemy and its surroundings by creating an ice tornado.
tales-aisutoneedo.note: Magic. Water element in this game. In the past it is on the bookshelf in Klarth's house; in the future it is bought in Rōnvarei (800 Gald according to Game Log). The range is 1/4 screen according to Majestic Fantasian, narrow according to Game Log, and around the enemy according to kouryaku.sub.jp.

tales-irapushon.desc: Attacks an enemy and its surroundings by raining down fireballs.
tales-irapushon.note: Magic. Fire element. Obtained in the Cave of Scorching Sands. In the SFC version the cost is TP 8, and it is obtained elsewhere (such as from the village chief of Beruadamu).

tales-torakutaabiimu.desc: Attacks an enemy and its surroundings with non-elemental power. Has no effect on flying enemies.
tales-torakutaabiimu.note: Magic. Non-elemental. Bought for 4000 Gald at the magic research lab in Alvanista Castle.

tales-sandaabureedo.desc: Attacks enemies on the screen by dropping blades of lightning.
tales-sandaabureedo.note: Magic. Lightning element. Bought for 12000 Gald at the magic research lab in Alvanista Castle. In the SFC version the cost is TP 12. The range is one screen according to Majestic Fantasian and medium according to Game Log.

tales-saikuron.desc: Slashes an enemy and its surroundings repeatedly with blades of wind.
tales-saikuron.note: Magic. Wind element. Added in the PS version. In the past you get it from the village chief of Beruadamu after talking to the mayor of Benetsia; in the future you get it in the town of Migēru.

tales-rei.desc: Attacks enemies on the screen by raining down beams of light.
tales-rei.note: Magic. Light element. Learned in an event in the Tower of the 12 Constellations. In the SFC version the cost is TP 15.

tales-faiasutoomu.desc: Attacks enemies on the screen by whipping up a storm of flames.
tales-faiasutoomu.note: Magic. Fire element. In the past you get it in Daosu Castle; in the future, in the Cave of Scorching Sands. kouryaku.sub.jp writes it as Faiāsutōmu.

tales-rokkumaunten.desc: Drops rocks and finishes by crushing an enemy and its surroundings with a boulder.
tales-rokkumaunten.note: Magic. Earth element. Added in the PS version. In the past you get it in Daosu Castle; in the future, in the Erosion Cave.

tales-meirusutoroomu.desc: Attacks enemies on the screen by creating a huge whirlpool.
tales-meirusutoroomu.note: Magic. Water element. Added in the PS version. Obtained in the Erosion Cave in the future.

tales-tenpesuto.desc: Attacks enemies by creating a tornado that covers the screen.
tales-tenpesuto.note: Magic. Wind element. Added in the PS version. Obtained in Demitel's mansion in the future.

tales-aasukueiku.desc: Attacks enemies on the screen by causing a huge earthquake.
tales-aasukueiku.note: Magic. Earth element. Added in the PS version. Obtained in the forest around the ninja village in the future.

tales-indegunishon.desc: Attacks enemies on the screen by dropping powerful lightning from the heavens.
tales-indegunishon.note: Magic. Lightning element. Learned in an event after the aerial battle in the Valhalla War. All four sources consulted (Majestic Fantasian SFC and PS versions, Game Log, kouryaku.sub.jp and rrpg.jp) write it as Indegunishon. This differs from the spelling Indiguneishon in later games.

tales-eguzupuroodo.desc: Attacks enemies on the screen with a huge explosion.
tales-eguzupuroodo.note: Magic. Fire element. Obtained in the Tower of Flame in the future. In the SFC version the cost is TP 25.

tales-goddoburesu.desc: Attacks enemies on the screen with strong wind pressure from above.
tales-goddoburesu.note: Magic. Wind element. Obtained in the ancient city of Thor. In the SFC version the cost is TP 18.

tales-taidaruweebu.desc: Attacks enemies on the screen by causing a huge tidal wave.
tales-taidaruweebu.note: Magic. Water element. Obtained in the Ice Cave in the future. In the SFC version the cost is TP 25.

tales-burakkuhooru.desc: Creates a space of darkness that deals heavy damage to an enemy.
tales-burakkuhooru.note: Magic. Darkness element. Obtained on the 18th basement floor of the Morlia Mine in the future. The TP cost is 42 in Majestic Fantasian and Game Log and 35 in kouryaku.sub.jp. In the SFC version it was an instant-death spell that finished off enemies with reduced HP.

tales-meteosuoomu.desc: Rains down meteors, attacking enemies where they land and around them.
tales-meteosuoomu.note: Magic. Non-elemental. Obtained in Daosu Castle in the future. The TP cost is 50 in Majestic Fantasian and Game Log and 40 in kouryaku.sub.jp (40 in the SFC version). This differs from the spelling Meteosuwōmu in later games.

tales-biggubann.desc: Causes a huge explosion that hits all enemies, including those off screen.
tales-biggubann.note: Magic. Light element. Added in the PS version. Obtained in the Dwarf temple at the bottom of the Morlia Mine in the future. kouryaku.sub.jp writes it as Bikkubanu.

tales-faasutoeido.desc: Restores a little of one ally's HP.
tales-faasutoeido.note: Hōjutsu art. Restores about 30% of maximum HP. Usable outside battle. Majestic Fantasian and Game Log say it is usable from the start, and kouryaku.sub.jp says it is learned at LV3 (LV3 in the SFC version).

tales-pikohan.desc: Drops a toy hammer to knock out one enemy.
tales-pikohan.note: Hōjutsu art. Learned at LV5. Being knocked out stops an enemy's actions and casting.

tales-chaaji.note: Hōjutsu art. Learned at LV8. Added in the PS version. Restores about 5 TP.

tales-diipumisuto.desc: Lowers enemies' accuracy with a mist.
tales-diipumisuto.note: Hōjutsu art. Learned at LV11 (LV8 in the SFC version).

tales-hiiru.desc: Restores a moderate amount of one ally's HP.
tales-hiiru.note: Hōjutsu art. Learned at LV14. Restores about 60% of maximum HP. Usable outside battle.

tales-ashiddorein.desc: Lowers enemies' defense by raining down acid.
tales-ashiddorein.note: Hōjutsu art. Learned at LV17. The range is one screen of enemies according to Majestic Fantasian and kouryaku.sub.jp and medium according to Game Log. In the SFC version the cost is TP 7.

tales-anchidooto.note: Hōjutsu art. Learned at LV20. Usable outside battle.

tales-sairensu.note: Hōjutsu art. Learned at LV23 (LV29 in the SFC version).

tales-naasu.note: Hōjutsu art. Learned at LV26. Restores about 45% of maximum HP according to Majestic Fantasian and Game Log, and about 50% according to kouryaku.sub.jp. Usable outside battle.

tales-shaapunesu.note: Hōjutsu art. Learned at LV29. Added in the PS version. The boost is about 30% according to Majestic Fantasian.

tales-rikabaa.desc: Cures one ally's poison, paralysis and petrification.
tales-rikabaa.note: Hōjutsu art. Learned at LV32. Usable outside battle. In the SFC version it targets all allies.

tales-disuperu.desc: Removes the effects of spells on all allies.
tales-disuperu.note: Hōjutsu art. Learned at LV35. Majestic Fantasian and Game Log describe it as "removes the effects of spells," while kouryaku.sub.jp says it "cures debuffs such as defense down."

tales-kyua.desc: Restores nearly all of one ally's HP.
tales-kyua.note: Hōjutsu art. Learned at LV38. Usable outside battle.

tales-pikopikohanmaa.desc: Knocks out groups of enemies by raining down toy hammers.
tales-pikopikohanmaa.note: Hōjutsu art. Learned at LV41. The range is one screen of enemies according to Majestic Fantasian and kouryaku.sub.jp and medium according to Game Log. In the SFC version the cost is TP 16.

tales-bariaa.note: Hōjutsu art. Learned at LV44. In the SFC version it targets all allies.

tales-reizudeddo.note: Hōjutsu art. Learned at LV47. Restores 50% of maximum HP according to Game Log and kouryaku.sub.jp. The TP cost is 26 according to Game Log and kouryaku.sub.jp, and 14 in Majestic Fantasian's PS version table (26 in its SFC version table). Usable outside battle.

tales-rizarekushon.note: Hōjutsu art. Learned at LV50. Restores about 65% of maximum HP. Usable outside battle. LV54 in the SFC version.

tales-taimusutoppu.desc: Stops time for all enemies for a few seconds.
tales-taimusutoppu.note: Hōjutsu art. Learned at LV53. Added in the PS version. The duration is 6 seconds according to Majestic Fantasian and 5 seconds according to kouryaku.sub.jp. Some enemies are unaffected.

tales-shirufu.desc: Summons the wind spirit Shirufu, who slashes one enemy repeatedly.
tales-shirufu.note: Summoning art. Wind element. The pact is made in the Valley of Shirufu in the past (the ring is an opal). The TP cost is 8 in Majestic Fantasian and Game Log and 5 in kouryaku.sub.jp (5 in the SFC version).

tales-undiine.desc: Summons the water spirit Undīne, who slashes enemies with blades of water.
tales-undiine.note: Summoning art. Water element. The pact is made in the Erosion Cave in the past (aquamarine). The TP cost is 12 in Majestic Fantasian and Game Log and 8 in kouryaku.sub.jp. The range is medium according to Game Log and one screen of enemies according to kouryaku.sub.jp.

tales-noomu.desc: Summons the earth spirit Nōmu, who attacks enemies on the screen.
tales-noomu.note: Summoning art. Earth element. The pact is made in the Cave of Spirits in the past (ruby). The TP cost is 16 in Majestic Fantasian and Game Log and 14 in kouryaku.sub.jp.

tales-ifuriito.desc: Summons the fire spirit Ifurīto, who attacks enemies with many fireballs.
tales-ifuriito.note: Summoning art. Fire element. The pact is made in the Cave of Scorching Sands in the past (garnet). The TP cost is 20 in Majestic Fantasian and Game Log and 16 in kouryaku.sub.jp.

tales-makusuweru.desc: Summons the spirit of the elements Makusuweru, who attacks enemies by bouncing his clones around.
tales-makusuweru.note: Summoning art. Non-elemental. The pact is made in the Morlia Mine in the past (turquoise).

tales-runa.desc: Summons the moon spirit Runa, who attacks enemies by raining down light.
tales-runa.note: Summoning art. Light element. The pact is made in the Tower of the 12 Constellations in the past (moonstone).

tales-shadou.desc: Summons the darkness spirit Shadou, who attacks enemies on the screen.
tales-shadou.note: Summoning art. Darkness element. The pact is made in the Cave of Darkness in the future (amethyst). The TP cost is 30 in Majestic Fantasian and Game Log and 25 in kouryaku.sub.jp.

tales-asuka.desc: Summons the light spirit Asuka, who attacks enemies on the screen.
tales-asuka.note: Summoning art. Light element. The pact is made in the ancient city of Thor in the future (topaz). The TP cost is 30 in Majestic Fantasian and Game Log and 28 in kouryaku.sub.jp.

tales-voruto.desc: Summons the lightning spirit Voruto, who attacks enemies on the screen.
tales-voruto.note: Summoning art. Lightning element. The pact is made in the Cave of Voruto in the future (sardonyx). The TP cost is 26 in Majestic Fantasian and Game Log and 32 in kouryaku.sub.jp.

tales-orijin.desc: Summons Orijin, the king of spirits, who attacks enemies on the screen.
tales-orijin.note: Summoning art. Non-elemental. The pact is made in the Trent Forest in the future (diamond). The TP cost is 36 in Majestic Fantasian and Game Log and 40 in kouryaku.sub.jp.

tales-guremurinreaa.desc: Summons Guremurinreā, whose swarm gangs up on and pummels each enemy.
tales-guremurinreaa.note: Summoning art. The element is none according to Game Log and kouryaku.sub.jp, and Darkness according to Majestic Fantasian. The pact is made in the lower levels of the Morlia Mine in the future (sapphire). The TP cost is 42 in Majestic Fantasian and Game Log and 45 in kouryaku.sub.jp.

tales-puruuto.desc: Summons the underworld spirit Purūto, who showers enemies with many dark flames.
tales-puruuto.note: Summoning art. Darkness element. Added in the PS version (replacing the chameleon of the SFC version). The pact is made in the lower levels of the Morlia Mine in the future (emerald in the PS version; lapis lazuli from the GBA version on).

kiseki-sutonhanma.desc: Drops a mass of rock to damage one enemy.
kiseki-sutonhanma.note: Earth Art. Required element value: Earth 1 (total on the same line).

kiseki-asuransu.desc: Thrusts a spear of rock up from the ground to damage one enemy.
kiseki-asuransu.note: Earth Art. Required element value: Earth 5 (total on the same line).

kiseki-petoroburesu.desc: Damages one enemy and has a 20% chance to petrify it.
kiseki-petoroburesu.note: Earth Art. Required element value: Earth 3 (total on the same line).

kiseki-sutoninpakuto.desc: Deals Earth damage in a medium circle centered on the enemy.
kiseki-sutoninpakuto.note: Earth Art. Required element value: Earth 3, Space 2 (total on the same line).

kiseki-taitanikkuroa.desc: Deals Earth damage to all enemies.
kiseki-taitanikkuroa.note: Earth Art. Required element value: Earth 8, Space 4 (total on the same line).

kiseki-asugado.desc: Gives one ally a ward that completely blocks one attack.
kiseki-asugado.note: Earth Art. Required element value: Earth 2 (total on the same line).

kiseki-asuuoru.desc: Gives allies in a small circle a ward that completely blocks one attack.
kiseki-asuuoru.note: Earth Art. Required element value: Earth 4 (total on the same line). Its effect is the area version of Āsugādo, but the sources do not treat it as part of the same line, so it is listed as a separate line.

kiseki-kuresuto.note: Earth Art. Required element value: Earth 4, Water 3, Space 2, Mirage 1 (total on the same line).

kiseki-akuaburido.desc: Hits one enemy with a mass of water for damage.
kiseki-akuaburido.note: Water Art. Required element value: Water 1 (total on the same line).

kiseki-buruinpakuto.desc: Damages one enemy with the power of water.
kiseki-buruinpakuto.note: Water Art. Required element value: Water 5 (total on the same line).

kiseki-daiyamondodasuto.desc: Deals cold damage in a small circle at a chosen spot, with a 20% chance to freeze.
kiseki-daiyamondodasuto.note: Water Art. Required element value: Water 4, Wind 2, Space 1 (total on the same line). The spelling Daiyamondodasuto follows Hyōri Ittai and Kiseki Wiki. Kōryaku Jōhō Center writes it as Daiamondodasuto.

kiseki-tia.note: Water Art. Required element value: Water 1 (total on the same line).

kiseki-tiara.note: Water Art. Required element value: Water 4 (total on the same line).

kiseki-tiararu.note: Water Art. Required element value: Water 6 (total on the same line).

kiseki-ratia.desc: Restores 200 HP each to allies in a small circle.
kiseki-ratia.note: Water Art. Required element value: Water 2, Space 1 (total on the same line). The area version of Tia.

kiseki-ratiara.desc: Restores 1000 HP each to allies in a medium circle.
kiseki-ratiara.note: Water Art. Required element value: Water 5, Space 2 (total on the same line). The area version of Tiara.

kiseki-kyuria.desc: Cures all of one ally's status ailments other than knockout.
kiseki-kyuria.note: Water Art. Required element value: Water 4, Mirage 2 (total on the same line).

kiseki-rakyuria.desc: Cures all status ailments other than knockout for allies in a large circle.
kiseki-rakyuria.note: Water Art. Required element value: Water 8, Space 2, Mirage 4 (total on the same line). The area version of Kyuria.

kiseki-serasu.desc: Revives one knocked-out ally and restores 100 HP.
kiseki-serasu.note: Water Art. Required element value: Water 4, Earth 2, Mirage 1 (total on the same line).

kiseki-faiaboruto.desc: Fires a fireball to damage one enemy.
kiseki-faiaboruto.note: Fire Art. Required element value: Fire 1 (total on the same line).

kiseki-faiaborutokai.desc: Deals Fire damage in a medium circle centered on the enemy.
kiseki-faiaborutokai.note: Fire Art. Required element value: Fire 3, Wind 1, Space 1 (total on the same line). The area version of Faiaboruto.

kiseki-furearo.desc: Damages one enemy with an arrow of flame.
kiseki-furearo.note: Fire Art. Required element value: Fire 3 (total on the same line).

kiseki-napamuburesu.desc: Deals heavy damage to one enemy with fierce flames.
kiseki-napamuburesu.note: Fire Art. Required element value: Fire 6 (total on the same line).

kiseki-supairarufurea.desc: Burns a medium circle centered on the enemy with swirling flames.
kiseki-supairarufurea.note: Fire Art. Required element value: Fire 5, Wind 2, Space 2 (total on the same line). Kiseki Wiki gives the required Wind value as 1.

kiseki-borukanikkureibu.desc: Deals heavy damage in a medium circle centered on the enemy with erupting lava.
kiseki-borukanikkureibu.note: Fire Art. Required element value: Fire 8, Earth 4, Space 2 (total on the same line).

kiseki-forute.note: Fire Art. Required element value: Fire 4, Wind 3, Space 2, Mirage 1 (total on the same line).

kiseki-easutoraiku.desc: Damages one enemy with a blade of wind.
kiseki-easutoraiku.note: Wind Art. Required element value: Wind 1 (total on the same line).

kiseki-eariaru.desc: Deals damage by creating a tornado in a medium circle at a chosen spot.
kiseki-eariaru.note: Wind Art. Required element value: Wind 4 (total on the same line).

kiseki-earosutomu.desc: Deals damage by creating a storm in a large circle at a chosen spot.
kiseki-earosutomu.note: Wind Art. Required element value: Wind 8 (total on the same line).

kiseki-raitoningu.desc: Deals damage with lightning that pierces along a straight line, with a 20% chance to seal Crafts (Craft Seal).
kiseki-raitoningu.note: Wind Art. Required element value: Wind 4, Space 2 (total on the same line). It looks like lightning, but its element is Wind.

kiseki-purazumaueibu.desc: Deals damage with an electric shock that pierces along a wide straight line, with a 20% chance to seal Crafts (Craft Seal).
kiseki-purazumaueibu.note: Wind Art. Required element value: Wind 8, Space 4 (total on the same line). It looks like lightning, but its element is Wind.

kiseki-shirufengado.desc: Raises one ally's evasion-related stat (AGL) by 50%.
kiseki-shirufengado.note: Wind Art. Required element value: Wind 2 (total on the same line).

kiseki-shirufenuingu.note: Wind Art. Required element value: Wind 6 (total on the same line). The spelling Shirufen'uingu follows Kōryaku Jōhō Center and Kiseki Wiki. Hyōri Ittai writes it as Shirufenwingu.

kiseki-sorubura.desc: Damages one enemy and has a 20% chance to knock it out cold (stun).
kiseki-sorubura.note: Time Art. Required element value: Time 1 (total on the same line). Time element. It does not fit any of the site's standard elements, so it is set to none.

kiseki-shadousupia.desc: Damages one enemy with a spear of shadow, with a 20% chance of instant knockout.
kiseki-shadousupia.note: Time Art. Required element value: Time 5 (total on the same line). Time element. It does not fit any of the site's standard elements, so it is set to none.

kiseki-herugeto.desc: Deals damage in a small circle centered on the enemy, with a 20% chance to stun.
kiseki-herugeto.note: Time Art. Required element value: Time 4, Space 2, Mirage 1 (total on the same line). Time element. It does not fit any of the site's standard elements, so it is set to none. Kiseki Wiki does not list the stun effect.

kiseki-howaitogehena.desc: Deals heavy damage in a medium circle at a chosen spot, with a 20% chance to stun.
kiseki-howaitogehena.note: Time Art. Required element value: Time 8, Space 4, Mirage 2 (total on the same line). Time element. It does not fit any of the site's standard elements, so it is set to none.

kiseki-kurokkuappu.desc: Raises one ally's speed (SPD) by 25% and makes their turn come around sooner.
kiseki-kurokkuappu.note: Time Art. Required element value: Time 1 (total on the same line).

kiseki-kurokkuappukai.note: Time Art. Required element value: Time 9 (total on the same line). An upgraded version of Kurokkuappu.

kiseki-anchiseputo.desc: Puts one enemy in a sealed state so that it cannot use Arts.
kiseki-anchiseputo.note: Time Art. Required element value: Time 3 (total on the same line).

kiseki-anchiseputooru.desc: Puts enemies in a medium circle at a chosen spot in a sealed state so that they cannot use Arts.
kiseki-anchiseputooru.note: Time Art. Required element value: Time 11 (total on the same line). The area version of Anchiseputo.

kiseki-kaosuburando.note: Mirage Art. Required element value: Mirage 5 (total on the same line). Kōryaku Jōhō Center classifies it as an attack spell, but it lists no damage and the only effect is confusion.

kiseki-seinto.desc: Raises one ally's attack (STR) and defense (DEF) by 25% each.
kiseki-seinto.note: Mirage Art. Required element value: Mirage 4, Earth 3, Fire 3, Water 2, Wind 2, Space 2 (total on the same line). Kiseki Wiki gives the required values as Mirage 4, Earth 1, Fire 3, Water 1, Wind 1, Space 2.

suikoden-shi-no-yubisaki.desc: Instantly kills one enemy (does not work on bosses).
suikoden-shi-no-yubisaki.note: A Lv 1 spell of the Soul Eater. The Japanese name is confirmed only in Game8 (a guide based on the HD Remaster); the spelling in the PS version (kana or kanji) is unconfirmed. Effect and tier were checked against English sources such as Gensopedia. The level rises at points set by story progress, not by the wielder's stats (Game8).

suikoden-kuroi-kage.desc: Strikes all enemies with a shadow of darkness for about 300 damage.
suikoden-kuroi-kage.note: A Lv 2 spell of the Soul Eater. The Japanese name is confirmed only in Game8 (a guide based on the HD Remaster); the spelling in the PS version (kana or kanji) is unconfirmed. Effect and tier were checked against English sources such as Gensopedia. No source states the element; it is classed as Darkness because the Dark Rune (Sega Saturn version only), which has a spell of the same name, deals Darkness damage.

suikoden-meifu.desc: Pulls all enemies into the underworld and kills them instantly (does not work on bosses).
suikoden-meifu.note: A Lv 3 spell of the Soul Eater. The Japanese name is confirmed only in Game8 (a guide based on the HD Remaster); the spelling in the PS version (kana or kanji) is unconfirmed. Effect and tier were checked against English sources such as Gensopedia.

suikoden-sabaki.desc: Deals heavy damage of about 1500 to one enemy.
suikoden-sabaki.note: A Lv 4 spell of the Soul Eater. The Japanese name is confirmed only in Game8 (a guide based on the HD Remaster); the spelling in the PS version (kana or kanji) is unconfirmed. Effect and tier were checked against English sources such as Gensopedia. The element could not be confirmed in any source, so it is listed as none.

suikoden-kaen-no-ya.desc: Hits one enemy with an arrow of fire for about 100 damage.
suikoden-kaen-no-ya.note: A Lv 1 spell of the Fire Rune. The Japanese name is confirmed only in Game8 (a guide based on the HD Remaster); the spelling in the PS version (kana or kanji) is unconfirmed. Effect and tier were checked against English sources such as Gensopedia. Sources differ on the starting wielder: Game8 says Miruihi, The Let's Play Archive says Kureo (who receives it from Rekkunāto at the start of the game), and Gensopedia lists no starting wielder.

suikoden-hono-no-arashi.desc: Hits all enemies with a whirl of flame for about 150 damage.
suikoden-hono-no-arashi.note: A Lv 2 spell of the Fire Rune and a Lv 1 spell of the Rekka Rune. The Japanese name is confirmed only in Game8 (a guide based on the HD Remaster); the spelling in the PS version (kana or kanji) is unconfirmed. Effect and tier were checked against English sources such as Gensopedia. The cost is listed at the level of the lower Rune (the Fire Rune).

suikoden-odoru-kaen.desc: Hits all enemies with dancing flames for about 400 damage.
suikoden-odoru-kaen.note: A Lv 3 spell of the Fire Rune and a Lv 2 spell of the Rekka Rune. The Japanese name is confirmed only in Game8 (a guide based on the HD Remaster); the spelling in the PS version (kana or kanji) is unconfirmed. Effect and tier were checked against English sources such as Gensopedia. The cost is listed at the level of the lower Rune (the Fire Rune).

suikoden-daibakuhatsu.desc: Causes an explosion that deals about 700 damage to all enemies.
suikoden-daibakuhatsu.note: A Lv 4 spell of the Fire Rune and a Lv 3 spell of the Rekka Rune. The Japanese name is confirmed only in Game8 (a guide based on the HD Remaster); the spelling in the PS version (kana or kanji) is unconfirmed. Effect and tier were checked against English sources such as Gensopedia. The cost is listed at the level of the lower Rune (the Fire Rune).

suikoden-saigo-no-hono.desc: Hits all enemies with the Rekka Rune's greatest flame for about 900 damage.
suikoden-saigo-no-hono.note: A Lv 4 spell of the Rekka Rune. The Japanese name is confirmed only in Game8 (a guide based on the HD Remaster); the spelling in the PS version (kana or kanji) is unconfirmed. Effect and tier were checked against English sources such as Gensopedia.

suikoden-ikari-no-ichigeki.desc: Calls down lightning on one enemy for about 150 damage.
suikoden-ikari-no-ichigeki.note: A Lv 1 spell of the Lightning Rune. The PS spelling follows the Suikoden Wiki (Fandom) (confirmed in only one source). Game8 (based on the HD Remaster) writes it as "怒りの一撃". Effect and tier were checked against Game8 and Gensopedia.

suikoden-raiu.desc: Rains lightning on all enemies for about 100 damage.
suikoden-raiu.note: A Lv 2 spell of the Lightning Rune and a Lv 1 spell of the Raimei Rune. The PS spelling follows the Suikoden Wiki (Fandom) (confirmed in only one source). Game8 (based on the HD Remaster) writes it as "雷雨". Effect and tier were checked against Game8 and Gensopedia. The cost is listed at the level of the lower Rune (the Lightning Rune).

suikoden-gekido-no-ichigeki.desc: Strikes one enemy with powerful lightning for about 600 damage.
suikoden-gekido-no-ichigeki.note: A Lv 3 spell of the Lightning Rune and a Lv 2 spell of the Raimei Rune. The PS spelling follows the Suikoden Wiki (Fandom) (confirmed in only one source). Game8 (based on the HD Remaster) writes it as "激怒の一撃". Effect and tier were checked against Game8 and Gensopedia. The cost is listed at the level of the lower Rune (the Lightning Rune).

suikoden-raigekikyu.desc: Hurls a ball of lightning at one enemy for about 1000 damage.
suikoden-raigekikyu.note: A Lv 4 spell of the Lightning Rune and a Lv 3 spell of the Raimei Rune. The PS spelling agrees between the Suikoden Wiki (Fandom) and Game8 (based on the HD Remaster). Effect and tier were checked against Game8 and Gensopedia. The cost is listed at the level of the lower Rune (the Lightning Rune).

suikoden-ikazuchi-no-arashi.desc: Hits all enemies with a storm of lightning for about 900 damage.
suikoden-ikazuchi-no-arashi.note: A Lv 4 spell of the Raimei Rune. The Japanese name is confirmed only in Game8 (a guide based on the HD Remaster); the spelling in the PS version (kana or kanji) is unconfirmed. Effect and tier were checked against English sources such as Gensopedia. The English release uses a different name.

suikoden-nemuri-no-kaze.desc: Puts all enemies to sleep with a drowsy wind (does not work on bosses).
suikoden-nemuri-no-kaze.note: A Lv 1 spell of the Wind Rune. The PS spelling follows the Suikoden Wiki (Fandom) (confirmed in only one source). Game8 (based on the HD Remaster) writes it as "眠りの風". Effect and tier were checked against Game8 and Gensopedia. The Let's Play Archive says its success rate is low and it works best on enemies weaker than the caster.

suikoden-kirisaki.desc: Slashes one enemy with blades of vacuum for about 400 damage.
suikoden-kirisaki.note: A Lv 2 spell of the Wind Rune and a Lv 1 spell of the Senpū Rune. The PS spelling follows the Suikoden Wiki (Fandom) (confirmed in only one source). Game8 (based on the HD Remaster) writes it as "切り裂き". Effect and tier were checked against Game8 and Gensopedia. The cost is listed at the level of the lower Rune (the Wind Rune).

suikoden-iyashi-no-kaze.desc: Fully restores one ally's HP with a healing wind.
suikoden-iyashi-no-kaze.note: A Lv 3 spell of the Wind Rune and a Lv 2 spell of the Senpū Rune. The PS spelling follows the Suikoden Wiki (Fandom) (confirmed in only one source). Game8 (based on the HD Remaster) writes it as "癒しの風". Effect and tier were checked against Game8 and Gensopedia. Gensopedia and The Let's Play Archive say it also cures status ailments. The cost is listed at the level of the lower Rune (the Wind Rune).

suikoden-arashi.desc: Raises a storm that deals about 500 damage to all enemies.
suikoden-arashi.note: A Lv 4 spell of the Wind Rune and a Lv 3 spell of the Senpū Rune. The PS spelling follows the Suikoden Wiki (Fandom) (confirmed in only one source). Game8 (based on the HD Remaster) writes it as "嵐". Effect and tier were checked against Game8 and Gensopedia. The cost is listed at the level of the lower Rune (the Wind Rune).

suikoden-kagayaku-kaze.desc: A shining wind that deals about 500 damage to all enemies and restores about 500 HP to all allies.
suikoden-kagayaku-kaze.note: A Lv 4 spell of the Senpū Rune. The Japanese name is confirmed only in Game8 (a guide based on the HD Remaster); the spelling in the PS version (kana or kanji) is unconfirmed. Effect and tier were checked against English sources such as Gensopedia. Game8 lists only the 500 HP restored to all allies and does not mention damage. Gensopedia and The Let's Play Archive also list 500 damage to all enemies and curing of status ailments, so it is registered as an attack.

suikoden-yasashiki-shizuku.desc: Fully restores one ally's HP with drops of water.
suikoden-yasashiki-shizuku.note: A Lv 1 spell of the Water Rune. The PS spelling follows the Suikoden Wiki (Fandom) (confirmed in only one source). Game8 (based on the HD Remaster) writes it as "優しき雫". Effect and tier were checked against Game8 and Gensopedia. Gensopedia and The Let's Play Archive say it also cures status ailments.

suikoden-mayakashi-no-kiri.desc: Wraps all allies in a mist that makes enemy attacks harder to land.
suikoden-mayakashi-no-kiri.note: A Lv 2 spell of the Water Rune and a Lv 1 spell of the Ryūsui Rune. The PS spelling agrees between the Suikoden Wiki (Fandom) and Game8 (based on the HD Remaster). Gensopedia, The Let's Play Archive and the Suikoden Wiki say it raises all allies' evasion, while Game8 says it lowers enemy accuracy by 20%. The cost is listed at the level of the lower Rune (the Water Rune).
