goldensun-pyuauisshu.note: Water element. The guideline recovery is 400.

goldensun-anchidoute.desc: Cures one ally of Poison and Venom.
goldensun-anchidoute.note: Water element. Mia can use it from the start.

goldensun-atenshon.desc: Cures one ally of status ailments such as Sleep, Stun and Delusion.
goldensun-atenshon.note: Water element. For the ailments it cures, RRPG lists Delusion, Stun and Sleep, while Hyōri Ittai adds Psynergy Seal and Haunt.

goldensun-ribaibu.desc: Revives one knocked-out ally with full HP.
goldensun-ribaibu.note: Earth element. Learned at Lv 19 by many lines.

goldensun-inpakuto.note: Wind element. Raises it by 25% per cast, up to a maximum of 50%.

goldensun-haiinpakuto.note: Wind element. Raises it by 12.5% per cast, up to a maximum of 50%.

goldensun-purotekuto.note: Fire element. Raises it by 25% per cast, up to a maximum of 50%.

goldensun-haipurotekuto.note: Fire element. Raises it by 12.5% per cast, up to a maximum of 50%.

goldensun-rejisuto.desc: Raises one ally's resistance to elemental attacks.
goldensun-rejisuto.note: Wind element. Raises resistance to all elements by 40 per cast, up to a maximum of 80.

goldensun-hairejisuto.desc: Raises all allies' resistance to elemental attacks.
goldensun-hairejisuto.note: Wind element. Raises resistance to all elements by 20 per cast, up to a maximum of 80.

goldensun-uiku.note: Fire element. Works by chance. Lowers it by 25% per cast, up to a maximum of 50%.

goldensun-haiuiku.desc: Lowers the defense of a group of enemies.
goldensun-haiuiku.note: Fire element. Works by chance. Lowers it by 12.5% per cast, up to a maximum of 50%. The range is 3 enemies, and the effect is not weaker at the edges.

goldensun-daru.note: Wind element. Works by chance. Lowers it by 25% per cast, up to a maximum of 50%.

goldensun-darudaru.desc: Lowers the attack power of a group of enemies.

goldensun-haisenshitibu.desc: Lowers the resistance of a group of enemies to elemental attacks.
goldensun-haisenshitibu.note: Wind element. Works by chance. Lowers resistance to all elements by 20 per cast, up to a maximum of 80. The range is 3 enemies.

goldensun-supurasshu.desc: Removes the stat-boosting effects on all enemies.
goldensun-supurasshu.note: Water element. RRPG lists the target as all enemies (Hyōri Ittai says it "wipes out the effects that raised the stats of allies", but the range is all enemies). Learned at Lv 30 by many lines.

goldensun-kishinnoyaiba.note: A Samurai Psynergy. Raises it by 25% per cast.

goldensun-tenjinnoyaiba.note: A Samurai Psynergy. Raises it by 12.5% per cast.

goldensun-shugobosatsu.note: A Samurai Psynergy. Raises it by 25% per cast.

goldensun-iryujon.desc: Wraps a group of enemies in illusions so that normal attacks miss more often.
goldensun-iryujon.note: Wind element. The effective range is 3 enemies (the enemy in the center takes the most damage).

goldensun-desufochun.desc: Possesses one enemy with a death spirit so that it is knocked out after 7 actions.

goldensun-desuchaji.note: Earth element. Learned at Lv 29 by many lines.

goldensun-dorein.desc: Drains one enemy's HP and adds it to your own.

goldensun-enajidorein.desc: Drains one enemy's PP (EP in the Japanese version) and adds it to your own.
goldensun-enajidorein.note: The PP cost is 0. It deals Wind-element damage to the enemy's PP and restores the same amount.

goldensun-ritan.desc: Returns you to the entrance of the dungeon.
goldensun-ritan.note: Earth element. Isaac can use it from the start (Hyōri Ittai).

goldensun-purufu.desc: Keeps you from meeting enemies weaker than your party for a while.

goldensun-mubu.desc: Moves distant pillars, rocks and the like sideways.
goldensun-mubu.note: Isaac and Garet can use it from the start.

goldensun-fosu.desc: Sends a shock to a distant object, knocking down pillars or moving things.
goldensun-fosu.note: Allies equipped with the Fosu Orb (obtained in the waterfall cave of Fuchin Temple) can use it.

goldensun-rifuto.desc: Lifts large rocks and the like upward.
goldensun-rifuto.note: Allies equipped with the Rifuto Jewel (obtained in Altin Mine) can use it.

goldensun-kyari.desc: Lifts a block and carries it to another place.
goldensun-kyari.note: Allies equipped with the Kyarī Stone can use it.

goldensun-kyatchi.desc: Pulls in out-of-reach nuts, keys and the like so you can take them.
goldensun-kyatchi.note: Allies equipped with the Kyatchi Beads (received in Haidia Village) can use it.

goldensun-rido.desc: Reads the minds of people and animals nearby.
goldensun-rido.note: Ivan can use it from the start.

goldensun-imajin.desc: Makes unseen things visible, such as hidden paths, treasure chests and oases.

goldensun-sutoppu.desc: Temporarily stops the movement of people, Djinn, stone statues and the like.
goldensun-sutoppu.note: Allies equipped with the Sutoppu Gem (obtained in the Haidia cave) can use it.

goldensun-shado.desc: Blends into shadows in dark places so that guards do not notice you.
goldensun-shado.note: Allies equipped with the Shadō Orb (obtained in Babi Palace after the Colosseum finals) can use it.

rudra-rato.desc: Attacks one enemy with an Earth-element "quicksand" (does not hit levitating targets).
rudra-rato.note: Base power 30. The Kotodama Kyōten manuscript notes: "There is no strict Earth element; attacks that do not work on levitating targets are called Earth-element."

rudra-pura.desc: Attacks all enemies with an Earth-element "quicksand" (does not hit levitating targets).
rudra-pura.note: Base power 40. The base word of the Earth element, but unlike the other elements, adding rank suffixes does not raise its rank (Guranpurana and the like become Non-elemental). The Kotodama Kyōten manuscript notes: "There is no strict Earth element; attacks that do not work on levitating targets are called Earth-element."

rudra-rebu.desc: Attacks one enemy with an Earth-element "lava" (does not hit levitating targets).
rudra-rebu.note: Base power 60. The Kotodama Kyōten manuscript notes: "There is no strict Earth element; attacks that do not work on levitating targets are called Earth-element."

rudra-purato.desc: Attacks all enemies with an Earth-element "lava" (does not hit levitating targets).
rudra-purato.note: Base power 70. Synonyms: Tōrusoron, Kafū(Kotodama Kyōten manuscript). Kafū is taught by a spirit tree in Riza's chapter (ocn1 glossary). The Kotodama Kyōten manuscript notes: "There is no strict Earth element; attacks that do not work on levitating targets are called Earth-element."

rudra-men.desc: Attacks one enemy with an Earth-element "earthquake" (does not hit levitating targets).
rudra-men.note: Base power 90. The Kotodama Kyōten manuscript notes: "There is no strict Earth element; attacks that do not work on levitating targets are called Earth-element."

rudra-porukusu.desc: A kotodama that borrows the power of nature to attack all enemies. Its power drops if the sea has not been purified.
rudra-porukusu.note: Nature kotodama (the list in God Bird's "Explaining Everything" and the Kotodama Kyōten manuscript agree). Base power 90, graphic: "freezing". Damage is halved until purification (God Bird).

rudra-hegu.desc: A kotodama that borrows the power of nature to attack all enemies. Its power drops if the sea has not been purified.
rudra-hegu.note: Nature kotodama (the list in God Bird's "Explaining Everything" and the Kotodama Kyōten manuscript agree). Base power 125, graphic: "tidal wave". Damage is halved until purification (God Bird). Hegu is a powerful root word and is often used at the end of ultimate-type kotodama such as Kinaniwohegu.

rudra-jiku.desc: A kotodama that borrows the power of nature to attack one enemy. Its power drops if the atmosphere has not been purified.
rudra-jiku.note: Nature kotodama (the list in God Bird's "Explaining Everything" and the Kotodama Kyōten manuscript agree). Base power 60, graphic: "holy light". Damage is halved until purification (God Bird).

rudra-hebun.desc: A kotodama that borrows the power of nature to attack all enemies. Its power drops if the atmosphere has not been purified.
rudra-hebun.note: Nature kotodama (the list in God Bird's "Explaining Everything" and the Kotodama Kyōten manuscript agree). Base power 30, graphic: "angel". Damage is halved until purification (God Bird).

rudra-jio.desc: A kotodama that borrows the power of nature to attack all enemies. Its power drops if the land has not been purified.
rudra-jio.note: Nature kotodama (the list in God Bird's "Explaining Everything" and the Kotodama Kyōten manuscript agree). Base power 80, graphic: "quicksand". Damage is halved until purification (God Bird).

rudra-gurakara.desc: A kotodama that borrows the power of nature to attack all enemies. Its power drops if the land has not been purified.
rudra-gurakara.note: Nature kotodama (the list in God Bird's "Explaining Everything" and the Kotodama Kyōten manuscript agree). Base power 125, graphic: "earthquake". Damage is halved until purification (God Bird).

rudra-meruton.desc: Attacks everyone, allies and enemies alike.
rudra-meruton.note: Synonyms: Atomikku. Base power 110. An all-hitting (indiscriminate) kotodama; used as a prefix, it makes other kotodama indiscriminate too (example: Merutonami). The Kotodama Kyōten manuscript classifies it as an ultimate-type Darkness-element kotodama.

rudra-gyarakushi.desc: Attacks everyone, allies and enemies alike, with the light of the Light element.

rudra-sukarudo.desc: Attacks everyone, allies and enemies alike, and may inflict Burn.
rudra-sukarudo.note: Base power 120. The Kotodama Kyōten manuscript lists it as the ultimate Burn type, while God Bird Episode 3 lists it as an all-hitting type and as a synonym of Irirogu (Burn).

rudra-gurabi.note: Base power 50. The graphic is the Darkness-element "corpse dragon", but it is treated as Non-elemental. A special kotodama whose effect remains even when used as a prefix. Confirmed in only one source (a special attack in the Kotodama Kyōten manuscript).

rudra-moigu.desc: A fireball made stronger by adding the prefix "Mō" to Igu.
rudra-moigu.note: Base power 24 (Igu is 10). The prefix "Mō" has a boost value of 7 (God Bird Episode 1). The MP cost is not given in the sources.

rudra-kontoaku.desc: A water ball made slightly stronger by adding the prefix "Konto" to Aku.
rudra-kontoaku.note: Base power 16 (Aku is 10). The prefix "Konto" has a boost value of 1 (God Bird Episode 1). The MP cost is not given in the sources.

rudra-furuigurusu.desc: A pillar of fire made more than twice as strong by adding the prefix "Furu" to Igurusu.
rudra-furuigurusu.note: Base power 42 (Igurusu is 20). God Bird Episode 1 names "Furu" as a representative prefix. The MP cost is not given in the sources.

rudra-vuakuna.desc: Hurls a water ball, made stronger by adding the prefix "Vu" to Akuna, at all enemies.
rudra-vuakuna.note: Base power 22 (Akuna is 10). "Vu" is an efficient power-boosting prefix (God Bird Episode 2). The MP cost is not given in the sources.

rudra-kopetenukapu.desc: Stacks the prefixes "Ko" and "Pe", which lower MP while raising power, to unleash a powerful blast of flame for 1 MP.
rudra-kopetenukapu.note: Base power 84. Called the "low-cost ultimate type" and a staple of low-level clears (Kotodama Kyōten manuscript). "Ko" is power +10 and MP -1, and "Pe" is power +10 and MP +1 (God Bird Special Edition).

rudra-karukimebito.desc: A single-target attack that stacks power-focused prefixes, among the strongest of the Fire element.
rudra-karukimebito.note: Base power 223. The Fire-element "ultimate type" in the Kotodama Kyōten manuscript. Confirmed in only one source.

rudra-kinaniwominu.desc: A single-target attack that stacks strengthening prefixes on the tidal wave kotodama "Minu", among the strongest of the Water element.
rudra-kinaniwominu.note: Base power 217. "Wo" is a single-target prefix and "Ki" is a power-focused prefix (God Bird Episode 2). The Water-element "ultimate type" in the Kotodama Kyōten manuscript.

rudra-refu.note: The base "Refu" line of healing kotodama (Healing, single, Lv 1 in the Kotodama Kyōten manuscript). Base power 20; the amount healed is set by base power plus Kindness, with no variance.

rudra-refutomu.note: The base "Refu" line of healing kotodama (Healing, single, Lv 2 in the Kotodama Kyōten manuscript). Base power 60; the amount healed is set by base power plus Kindness, with no variance. Synonyms: Nuado.

rudra-refutiumu.note: The base "Refu" line of healing kotodama (Healing, single, Lv 3 in the Kotodama Kyōten manuscript). Base power 120; the amount healed is set by base power plus Kindness, with no variance. Synonyms: Sukuwea.

rudra-refuna.note: The base "Refu" line of healing kotodama (Healing, plural, Lv 1 in the Kotodama Kyōten manuscript). Base power 40; the amount healed is set by base power plus Kindness, with no variance.

rudra-refumuru.note: The base "Refu" line of healing kotodama (Healing, plural, Lv 2 in the Kotodama Kyōten manuscript). Base power 80; the amount healed is set by base power plus Kindness, with no variance.

rudra-refurande.note: The base "Refu" line of healing kotodama (Healing, plural, Lv 3 in the Kotodama Kyōten manuscript). Base power 120; the amount healed is set by base power plus Kindness, with no variance.

rudra-refurusu.desc: Restores one ally's HP. Heals more than Refu.
rudra-refurusu.note: Synonyms: Remu. Base power 40. Same graphic as Refu. Confirmed in only one source (Kotodama Kyōten manuscript).

rudra-refurandevu.desc: Adds "Vu" to the end of Refurande to restore a large amount of all allies' HP for little MP.
rudra-refurandevu.note: Base power 128. The Kotodama Kyōten manuscript calls it "the most balanced of the healing kotodama found so far." Confirmed in only one source.

rudra-megami.desc: Uses the power of nature to restore all allies' HP. Its effect drops if the atmosphere has not been purified.

rudra-ekusupia.desc: Restores a large amount of all allies' HP at the cost of the caster fainting.
rudra-ekusupia.note: Self-sacrifice type. Fixed power of 200 (God Bird, "Explaining Everything"). Synonyms: Zaru(God Bird Episode 3).

rudra-refini.desc: Cures the statuses Burn, Freeze, Shock, Levitation and Auto-heal.
rudra-refini.note: Synonyms: Meha, Eku(Kotodama Kyōten manuscript), Rumehatī(God Bird Episode 3). It cannot cure Contamination. The Kotodama Kyōten manuscript speculates that "Meha" comes from the Dragon Quest spell "Zameha".

rudra-perusuan.desc: Cures "Contamination", which halves all stats and prevents the use of kotodama.
rudra-perusuan.note: Said to be the only kotodama that can cure Contamination. Contamination occurs only from enemy special attacks (God Bird Episode 3).

rudra-animu.note: Base power 1 (the target revives with only a little HP). Revival type, Lv 1 in the Kotodama Kyōten manuscript. Confirmed in only one source.

rudra-animusu.desc: Revives one fainted ally with more HP than Animu.
rudra-animusu.note: Base power 40. Revival type, Lv 2 in the Kotodama Kyōten manuscript. Confirmed in only one source.

rudra-poenikusu.desc: Puts the target in a state where, if knocked out, it automatically revives with one quarter of max HP.
rudra-poenikusu.note: Auto-revival type. Synonyms: Rireizu(God Bird Episode 3).

rudra-irirogu.desc: Deals slight damage and inflicts Burn (damage of 1/16 of max HP after each action).
rudra-irirogu.note: Status change (Burn), Lv 1 in the Kotodama Kyōten manuscript. God Bird Episode 3 lists the same name as a Burn kotodama. The Burn success rate is about 50% regardless of stats (Kotodama Kyōten manuscript). Synonyms: Karu.

rudra-torapikusu.desc: A stronger version of the Burn type. Deals damage and inflicts Burn.
rudra-torapikusu.note: Status change (Burn), Lv 3 in the Kotodama Kyōten manuscript. God Bird Episode 3 lists the same name as a Burn kotodama. The Burn success rate is about 50% regardless of stats (Kotodama Kyōten manuscript).

rudra-ariroku.desc: Deals slight damage and freezes the target so it cannot act.
rudra-ariroku.note: Status change (Freeze), Lv 1 in the Kotodama Kyōten manuscript. God Bird Episode 3 lists the same name as a Freeze kotodama. The Freeze success rate is about 50% regardless of stats (Kotodama Kyōten manuscript). Synonyms: Ami. Defense rises slightly while Frozen.

rudra-epimeteusu.desc: A stronger version of the Freeze type. Deals damage and freezes the target.
rudra-epimeteusu.note: Status change (Freeze), Lv 3 in the Kotodama Kyōten manuscript. God Bird Episode 3 lists the same name as a Freeze kotodama. The Freeze success rate is about 50% regardless of stats (Kotodama Kyōten manuscript).

rudra-torirou.desc: Deals slight damage and inflicts Shock (the target can only make weapon attacks and its aim becomes erratic).
rudra-torirou.note: Status change (Shock), Lv 1 in the Kotodama Kyōten manuscript. God Bird Episode 3 lists the same name as a Shock kotodama. The Shock success rate is about 50% regardless of stats (Kotodama Kyōten manuscript). Synonyms: Moto. Shock wears off naturally in 2 to 3 turns. Shock is not among the site's common subcategories, so it is classified as Confuse because it disrupts aim.

rudra-uokka.desc: A stronger version of the Shock type. Deals damage and inflicts Shock.
rudra-uokka.note: Status change (Shock), Lv 3 in the Kotodama Kyōten manuscript. God Bird Episode 3 lists the same name as a Shock kotodama. The Shock success rate is about 50% regardless of stats (Kotodama Kyōten manuscript). Classified as Confuse for the same reason as Torirou.

rudra-pani.desc: Deals slight damage to all enemies and inflicts Shock.
rudra-pani.note: Status change (Shock), Lv 1 in the Kotodama Kyōten manuscript. God Bird Episode 3 lists the same name as a Shock kotodama. The Shock success rate is about 50% regardless of stats (Kotodama Kyōten manuscript). Classified as Confuse for the same reason as Torirou.

rudra-teririo.desc: Deals slight damage and makes the target levitate, so Earth-element attacks miss it.
rudra-teririo.note: Status change (Levitation), Lv 1. Synonyms: Kuri(Kotodama Kyōten manuscript), Worāre(God Bird Episode 3). Levitation lands almost 100% of the time. Because casting it on allies lets them avoid Earth-element attacks, it is classified as Barriers.

rudra-kiryu.desc: Makes several targets levitate, so Earth-element attacks miss them.
rudra-kiryu.note: Status change (Levitation, plural), Lv 1. The plural version of Teriroo.

rudra-soriroa.desc: Puts the target in an Auto-heal state, restoring 1/8 of max HP after each action.
rudra-soriroa.note: Synonyms: Reparāre(Kotodama Kyōten manuscript and God Bird Episode 3), Jene(God Bird Episode 3). It cannot be made plural with a prefix. It is canceled when hit by a Darkness-element attack.

rudra-nirirohi.desc: Turns the target into a berserker and raises its attack power. Its aim becomes erratic in the meantime.
rudra-nirirohi.note: Synonyms: Erāti, Supiritto(Kotodama Kyōten manuscript), Keru, Tan(God Bird Episode 3). The Kotodama Kyōten manuscript speculates that the names Tan, Min and Keru come from energy-drink brand names.

rudra-burakimu.note: A stat-altering kotodama (Lv 1, single target in the Kotodama Kyōten manuscript). The changes can be stacked and last for the rest of the battle (God Bird Episode 3). God Bird Episode 3 also lists Burakimu as a Strength-up kotodama.

rudra-burakurusu.desc: Greatly raises Strength, doubling attacks for a while.
rudra-burakurusu.note: A stat-altering kotodama (Lv 2, single target in the Kotodama Kyōten manuscript). The changes can be stacked and last for the rest of the battle (God Bird Episode 3). Confirmed in only one source (Kotodama Kyōten manuscript).

rudra-ko.desc: Greatly raises all allies' Strength, doubling attacks for a while.
rudra-ko.note: A stat-altering kotodama (Lv 2, plural in the Kotodama Kyōten manuscript). The changes can be stacked and last for the rest of the battle (God Bird Episode 3). God Bird Episode 3 also lists Kō as a Strength-up kotodama.

rudra-kautu.note: A stat-altering kotodama (Lv 1, single target in the Kotodama Kyōten manuscript). The changes can be stacked and last for the rest of the battle (God Bird Episode 3). Found in a kotodama treasure chest in Gyararu's clock tower (ocn1 glossary).

rudra-femuru.note: A stat-altering kotodama (Lv 1, single target in the Kotodama Kyōten manuscript). The changes can be stacked and last for the rest of the battle (God Bird Episode 3).

rudra-feruusu.note: A stat-altering kotodama (Lv 2, single target in the Kotodama Kyōten manuscript). The changes can be stacked and last for the rest of the battle (God Bird Episode 3). Confirmed in only one source (Kotodama Kyōten manuscript).

rudra-supiri.note: A stat-altering kotodama (Lv 1, single target in the Kotodama Kyōten manuscript). The changes can be stacked and last for the rest of the battle (God Bird Episode 3). Wisdom affects the power of kotodama, guns and staffs (God Bird Episode 3).

rudra-supirumu.note: A stat-altering kotodama (Lv 2, single target in the Kotodama Kyōten manuscript). The changes can be stacked and last for the rest of the battle (God Bird Episode 3). Confirmed in only one source (Kotodama Kyōten manuscript).

rudra-koruborisu.note: A stat-altering kotodama (Lv 1, single target in the Kotodama Kyōten manuscript). The changes can be stacked and last for the rest of the battle (God Bird Episode 3).

rudra-rimu.note: A stat-altering kotodama (Lv 1, single target in the Kotodama Kyōten manuscript). The changes can be stacked and last for the rest of the battle (God Bird Episode 3). Confirmed in only one source (Kotodama Kyōten manuscript). Adding a prefix that stands for an element makes it halve damage of that element (Igurīmu and so on).

rudra-pateie.note: A stat-altering kotodama (Lv 2, single target in the Kotodama Kyōten manuscript). The changes can be stacked and last for the rest of the battle (God Bird Episode 3).

rudra-inbeki.desc: Greatly lowers one enemy's Strength, halving its attacks for a while.
rudra-inbeki.note: A stat-altering kotodama (Lv 2, single target in the Kotodama Kyōten manuscript). The changes can be stacked and last for the rest of the battle (God Bird Episode 3).

rudra-hafu.desc: Greatly lowers all enemies' Strength, halving their attacks for a while.
rudra-hafu.note: A stat-altering kotodama (Lv 2, plural in the Kotodama Kyōten manuscript). The changes can be stacked and last for the rest of the battle (God Bird Episode 3).

rudra-fatto.note: A stat-altering kotodama (Lv 1, single target in the Kotodama Kyōten manuscript). The changes can be stacked and last for the rest of the battle (God Bird Episode 3).

rudra-uirusu.note: A stat-altering kotodama (Lv 1, single target in the Kotodama Kyōten manuscript). The changes can be stacked and last for the rest of the battle (God Bird Episode 3).

rudra-uenborisu.note: A stat-altering kotodama (Lv 1, single target in the Kotodama Kyōten manuscript). The changes can be stacked and last for the rest of the battle (God Bird Episode 3).

rudra-zero.note: A stat-altering kotodama (Lv 1, single target in the Kotodama Kyōten manuscript). The changes can be stacked and last for the rest of the battle (God Bird Episode 3). Confirmed in only one source (Kotodama Kyōten manuscript). The spelling of the advanced form differs between sources (Kotodama Kyōten manuscript: "Pikugazero"; God Bird Episode 3: "Pigugazero").

rudra-pusupeku.note: A stat-altering kotodama (Lv 1, plural in the Kotodama Kyōten manuscript). The changes can be stacked and last for the rest of the battle (God Bird Episode 3).

rudra-igurimu.desc: Raises magic defense and halves Fire-element damage.
rudra-igurimu.note: An elemental defense kotodama made from a base word plus "Rīmu" (Magic defense up). The halving effect ends after 4 actions. God Bird Episode 3 also describes the mechanism of attaching an element prefix to the magic defense up kotodama to halve that element, but only the Kotodama Kyōten manuscript lists it under this name.

rudra-akurimu.desc: Raises magic defense and halves Water-element damage.
rudra-akurimu.note: An elemental defense kotodama made from a base word plus "Rīmu" (Magic defense up). The halving effect ends after 4 actions. God Bird Episode 3 also describes the mechanism of attaching an element prefix to the magic defense up kotodama to halve that element, but only the Kotodama Kyōten manuscript lists it under this name.

rudra-tourimu.desc: Raises magic defense and halves Lightning-element damage.
rudra-tourimu.note: An elemental defense kotodama made from a base word plus "Rīmu" (Magic defense up). The halving effect ends after 4 actions. God Bird Episode 3 also describes the mechanism of attaching an element prefix to the magic defense up kotodama to halve that element, but only the Kotodama Kyōten manuscript lists it under this name.

rudra-teorimu.desc: Raises magic defense and halves Wind-element damage.
rudra-teorimu.note: An elemental defense kotodama made from a base word plus "Rīmu" (Magic defense up). The halving effect ends after 4 actions. God Bird Episode 3 also describes the mechanism of attaching an element prefix to the magic defense up kotodama to halve that element, but only the Kotodama Kyōten manuscript lists it under this name.

rudra-soarimu.desc: Raises magic defense and halves Light-element damage.
rudra-soarimu.note: An elemental defense kotodama made from a base word plus "Rīmu" (Magic defense up). The halving effect ends after 4 actions. God Bird Episode 3 also describes the mechanism of attaching an element prefix to the magic defense up kotodama to halve that element, but only the Kotodama Kyōten manuscript lists it under this name.

rudra-sererimu.desc: Raises magic defense and halves Darkness-element damage.
rudra-sererimu.note: An elemental defense kotodama made from a base word plus "Rīmu" (Magic defense up). The halving effect ends after 4 actions. God Bird Episode 3 also describes the mechanism of attaching an element prefix to the magic defense up kotodama to halve that element, but only the Kotodama Kyōten manuscript lists it under this name.

rudra-porekku.desc: Puts up a barrier that blocks one kotodama attack.
rudra-porekku.note: Synonyms: Rifureku(God Bird Episode 3). It can be made plural by adding "Na" and the like.

rudra-infini.desc: Makes the target invincible, nullifying one attack.
rudra-infini.note: Synonyms: Muteki(God Bird Episode 3). Effective only on the turn it is used and the next turn, and ends after one hit.

rudra-apusonmo.desc: Makes physical attacks always hit for a while.
rudra-apusonmo.note: The effect lasts about 4 actions. God Bird Episode 3 says "Mo" alone has the same effect.

rudra-apusorou.desc: Makes physical attacks always land critical hits for a while.
rudra-apusorou.note: Synonyms: Kuritikaru(God Bird Episode 3). The effect lasts about 4 actions.

rudra-sutera.note: Synonyms: Banpaia(God Bird Episode 3). Base power 40. The amount drained is small.

rudra-purumora.note: Synonyms: Suu(God Bird Episode 3). The amount drained is about one third of its power.

rudra-digu.desc: Instantly kills one enemy. The success rate is on the low side.
rudra-digu.note: Synonyms: Raki(God Bird Episode 3). The success rate is calculated from an individually set power.

rudra-deskopema.desc: Combines the instant-death prefix "Desu" with "Ko", "Pe" and "Ma" to instantly kill all enemies for 1 MP.
rudra-deskopema.note: Because "Ma" fixes it as plural, the single-targeting of Desu is canceled (God Bird Special Edition). God Bird Episode 3 calls it the strongest of the instant-death type.

rudra-tirra.desc: Erases one enemy. No experience or money is gained from an erased enemy.
rudra-tirra.note: Vanish type. Although this is a different effect from instant death, it is classified as Instant death because it removes the enemy from battle. Items can still be obtained (God Bird Episode 3).

rudra-mozefuramu.note: Vanish type. Synonyms: Furamu. The Kotodama Kyōten manuscript speculates that "Furamu" comes from the Dragon Quest spell "Nifuramu".

rudra-adosun.desc: Deals heavy damage to the enemy at the cost of the caster fainting.
rudra-adosun.note: Self-sacrifice type. Base power 240. Synonyms: Nte(God Bird Episode 3).

rudra-inpurusu.desc: Each cast has an unpredictable result, such as an attack or healing of any element.
rudra-inpurusu.note: Unknown-effect type. Synonyms: Punte(God Bird Episode 3). In the Kotodama Kyōten manuscript, the effect is random from among 8 kinds.

rudra-pureka.desc: Escapes from battle for certain (cannot be used in boss battles).
rudra-pureka.note: Escape type. Synonyms: Pīsu, Tera(Kotodama Kyōten manuscript and God Bird Episode 3), Hishouseki(God Bird Episode 3).

rudra-supini.desc: Cancels all status changes and stat boosts and drops of everyone, allies and enemies.

phantasystar-foie.desc: Attacks one enemy with fire, an entry-level technique of the Foie line.
phantasystar-foie.note: Damage is about 15 (Uepon no Game Land). The Fire element comes from the overseas source (Phantasy Star Cave). Names and TP are from rrpg.jp and Uepon no Game Land / Kōryaku Tengoku (the same table); learners and levels were checked against Phantasy Star Cave (overseas version).

phantasystar-gifoie.desc: Attacks one enemy with fire, an intermediate technique of the Foie line.
phantasystar-gifoie.note: Damage is about 40. Names and TP are from rrpg.jp and Uepon no Game Land / Kōryaku Tengoku (the same table); learners and levels were checked against Phantasy Star Cave (overseas version).

phantasystar-nafoie.desc: Attacks one enemy with intense fire, an advanced technique of the Foie line.
phantasystar-nafoie.note: Damage is about 130. Only Rolf learns it. Names and TP are from rrpg.jp and Uepon no Game Land / Kōryaku Tengoku (the same table); learners and levels were checked against Phantasy Star Cave (overseas version).

phantasystar-gurantsu.desc: Attacks one enemy with light, an entry-level technique of the Gurantsu line.
phantasystar-gurantsu.note: Damage is about 30. Only Rolf learns it. The Light element comes from the overseas source (the description of Tsu in Phantasy Star Cave). The Japanese Wikipedia also says the protagonist uses the "Gurantsu line". Names and TP are from rrpg.jp and Uepon no Game Land / Kōryaku Tengoku (the same table); learners and levels were checked against Phantasy Star Cave (overseas version).

phantasystar-gigurantsu.desc: Attacks one enemy with light, an intermediate technique of the Gurantsu line.
phantasystar-gigurantsu.note: Damage is about 80. Names and TP are from rrpg.jp and Uepon no Game Land / Kōryaku Tengoku (the same table); learners and levels were checked against Phantasy Star Cave (overseas version).

phantasystar-nagurantsu.desc: Attacks one enemy with intense light, an advanced technique of the Gurantsu line.
phantasystar-nagurantsu.note: Damage is about 150. Names and TP are from rrpg.jp and Uepon no Game Land / Kōryaku Tengoku (the same table); learners and levels were checked against Phantasy Star Cave (overseas version).

phantasystar-zan.desc: Attacks one group of enemies with wind, an entry-level technique of the Zan line.
phantasystar-zan.note: Damage is about 20. The Wind element comes from the overseas source (Phantasy Star Cave). Names and TP are from rrpg.jp and Uepon no Game Land / Kōryaku Tengoku (the same table); learners and levels were checked against Phantasy Star Cave (overseas version).

phantasystar-gizan.desc: Attacks one group of enemies with wind, an intermediate technique of the Zan line.
phantasystar-gizan.note: Damage is about 30. Names and TP are from rrpg.jp and Uepon no Game Land / Kōryaku Tengoku (the same table); learners and levels were checked against Phantasy Star Cave (overseas version).

phantasystar-nazan.desc: Attacks one group of enemies with intense wind, an advanced technique of the Zan line.
phantasystar-nazan.note: Damage is about 100. TP is given as 11 (the Rolf tables in rrpg.jp, Uepon no Game Land and Phantasy Star Cave). Only the Shir table in Phantasy Star Cave says 12. Names and TP are from rrpg.jp and Uepon no Game Land / Kōryaku Tengoku (the same table); learners and levels were checked against Phantasy Star Cave (overseas version).

phantasystar-gurabuto.desc: Attacks all enemies with gravity, an entry-level technique of the Gurabuto line.
phantasystar-gurabuto.note: Damage is about 20. Gravity is not among the site's common elements, so it is listed as none. Anna's learning level differs: 39 (Uepon no Game Land) versus 40 (Phantasy Star Cave). Names and TP are from rrpg.jp and Uepon no Game Land / Kōryaku Tengoku (the same table); learners and levels were checked against Phantasy Star Cave (overseas version).

phantasystar-gigurabuto.desc: Attacks all enemies with gravity, an intermediate technique of the Gurabuto line.
phantasystar-gigurabuto.note: Damage is about 40. Learning levels differ: Rolf 28 and Anna 48 (Uepon no Game Land) versus Rolf 27 and Anna 50 (Phantasy Star Cave). Names and TP are from rrpg.jp and Uepon no Game Land / Kōryaku Tengoku (the same table); learners and levels were checked against Phantasy Star Cave (overseas version).

phantasystar-nagurabuto.desc: Attacks all enemies with intense gravity, an advanced technique of the Gurabuto line.
phantasystar-nagurabuto.note: Damage is about 80. The Japanese sources (Uepon no Game Land / Kōryaku Tengoku) list only Shir (Lv 45); Rolf (Lv 40) is confirmed only in Phantasy Star Cave. Names and TP are from rrpg.jp and Uepon no Game Land / Kōryaku Tengoku (the same table); learners and levels were checked against Phantasy Star Cave (overseas version).

phantasystar-megido.desc: Deals heavy damage to all enemies, but halves the HP of your allies other than the caster.
phantasystar-megido.note: The strongest attack technique, learned only by Rolf. No source states its element, so it is listed as none (the overseas source describes it as "destructive energy"). Names and TP are from rrpg.jp and Uepon no Game Land / Kōryaku Tengoku (the same table); learners and levels were checked against Phantasy Star Cave (overseas version).

phantasystar-fanbia.desc: Attacks one enemy and drains HP equal to the damage dealt.
phantasystar-fanbia.note: Phantasy Star Cave limits the target to biological enemies (biomonsters), but the Japanese sources give no restriction on targets. Names and TP are from rrpg.jp and Uepon no Game Land / Kōryaku Tengoku (the same table); learners and levels were checked against Phantasy Star Cave (overseas version).

phantasystar-gaji.desc: Damages one mechanical enemy, an entry-level technique of the Gāji line.
phantasystar-gaji.note: Works only on mechanical enemies. Damage is about 20. Names and TP are from rrpg.jp and Uepon no Game Land / Kōryaku Tengoku (the same table); learners and levels were checked against Phantasy Star Cave (overseas version).

phantasystar-gigaji.desc: Damages one mechanical enemy, an intermediate technique of the Gāji line.
phantasystar-gigaji.note: Works only on mechanical enemies. Damage is about 60. Names and TP are from rrpg.jp and Uepon no Game Land / Kōryaku Tengoku (the same table); learners and levels were checked against Phantasy Star Cave (overseas version).

phantasystar-nagaji.desc: Deals heavy damage to one mechanical enemy, an advanced technique of the Gāji line.
phantasystar-nagaji.note: Works only on mechanical enemies. Damage is about 150. Names and TP are from rrpg.jp and Uepon no Game Land / Kōryaku Tengoku (the same table); learners and levels were checked against Phantasy Star Cave (overseas version).

phantasystar-sagaji.desc: Damages all mechanical enemies, an entry-level all-target technique of the Gāji line.
phantasystar-sagaji.note: Damage is about 20. Sources differ on the target: rrpg.jp and Phantasy Star Cave say "all mechanical enemies" while Uepon no Game Land says "the mecha group", so all enemies is used. Names and TP are from rrpg.jp and Uepon no Game Land / Kōryaku Tengoku (the same table); learners and levels were checked against Phantasy Star Cave (overseas version).

phantasystar-gisagaji.desc: Damages all mechanical enemies, an intermediate all-target technique of the Gāji line.
phantasystar-gisagaji.note: Damage is about 60. Sources differ on the target: rrpg.jp and Phantasy Star Cave say "all mechanical enemies" while Uepon no Game Land says "the mecha group", so all enemies is used. Names and TP are from rrpg.jp and Uepon no Game Land / Kōryaku Tengoku (the same table); learners and levels were checked against Phantasy Star Cave (overseas version).

phantasystar-nasagaji.desc: Deals heavy damage to all mechanical enemies, an advanced all-target technique of the Gāji line.
phantasystar-nasagaji.note: Damage is about 150. Sources differ on the target: rrpg.jp and Phantasy Star Cave say "all mechanical enemies" while Uepon no Game Land says "the mecha group", so all enemies is used. Names and TP are from rrpg.jp and Uepon no Game Land / Kōryaku Tengoku (the same table); learners and levels were checked against Phantasy Star Cave (overseas version).

phantasystar-eijia.desc: Damages one group of mechanical enemies.
phantasystar-eijia.note: Damage is about 23. Names and TP are from rrpg.jp and Uepon no Game Land / Kōryaku Tengoku (the same table); learners and levels were checked against Phantasy Star Cave (overseas version).

phantasystar-purosedan.note: The learning level differs: 25 (Uepon no Game Land) versus 26 (Phantasy Star Cave). Names and TP are from rrpg.jp and Uepon no Game Land / Kōryaku Tengoku (the same table); learners and levels were checked against Phantasy Star Cave (overseas version).

phantasystar-rimite.desc: Stops the movement of one mechanical enemy.
phantasystar-rimite.note: Paired with Rimita, which is for biological enemies. Names and TP are from rrpg.jp and Uepon no Game Land / Kōryaku Tengoku (the same table); learners and levels were checked against Phantasy Star Cave (overseas version).

phantasystar-forusa.desc: Makes one mechanical enemy's attacks miss more often.
phantasystar-forusa.note: Sources differ on the effect. Uepon no Game Land says "makes the mecha's attacks miss", rrpg.jp says "drives it haywire (effect unknown)", and Phantasy Star Cave says "confuses". The Japanese "makes attacks miss" is used here, paired with Doranku for biological enemies. Names and TP are from rrpg.jp and Uepon no Game Land / Kōryaku Tengoku (the same table); learners and levels were checked against Phantasy Star Cave (overseas version).

phantasystar-konteru.desc: Seals one mechanical enemy's special attacks.
phantasystar-konteru.note: It seals not only techniques but enemy special abilities in general (Uepon no Game Land and Phantasy Star Cave). rrpg.jp says "makes it quiet (effect unknown)". Names and TP are from rrpg.jp and Uepon no Game Land / Kōryaku Tengoku (the same table); learners and levels were checked against Phantasy Star Cave (overseas version).

phantasystar-jenera.desc: Ages one biological enemy and damages it.
phantasystar-jenera.note: Works only on biological enemies. Uepon no Game Land describes the effect as "aging", while rrpg.jp and Phantasy Star Cave say "deals damage". Names and TP are from rrpg.jp and Uepon no Game Land / Kōryaku Tengoku (the same table); learners and levels were checked against Phantasy Star Cave (overseas version).

phantasystar-sajenera.desc: Ages all biological enemies and damages them.
phantasystar-sajenera.note: The all-target version of Jenera. Names and TP are from rrpg.jp and Uepon no Game Land / Kōryaku Tengoku (the same table); learners and levels were checked against Phantasy Star Cave (overseas version).

phantasystar-boruto.note: Names and TP are from rrpg.jp and Uepon no Game Land / Kōryaku Tengoku (the same table); learners and levels were checked against Phantasy Star Cave (overseas version).

phantasystar-saboruto.desc: Instantly kills one group of biological enemies.
phantasystar-saboruto.note: The area version of Boruto. Sources differ on the target: rrpg.jp and Phantasy Star Cave say one group while Uepon no Game Land says "all biological enemies", so group is used. Names and TP are from rrpg.jp and Uepon no Game Land / Kōryaku Tengoku (the same table); learners and levels were checked against Phantasy Star Cave (overseas version).

phantasystar-rimita.note: TP is given as 3 (Uepon no Game Land and Phantasy Star Cave); rrpg.jp says 2. The learning level differs: 3 (Uepon no Game Land) versus 2 (Phantasy Star Cave). Paired with Rimite, which is for mechanical enemies. Names and TP are from rrpg.jp and Uepon no Game Land / Kōryaku Tengoku (the same table); learners and levels were checked against Phantasy Star Cave (overseas version).

phantasystar-doranku.desc: Makes one biological enemy's attacks miss more often.
phantasystar-doranku.note: The effect is "biological attacks miss" in Uepon no Game Land and "lowers accuracy" in Phantasy Star Cave. rrpg.jp says "drives it haywire (effect unknown)". Names and TP are from rrpg.jp and Uepon no Game Land / Kōryaku Tengoku (the same table); learners and levels were checked against Phantasy Star Cave (overseas version).

phantasystar-shizasu.desc: Seals one biological enemy's special attacks.
phantasystar-shizasu.note: It seals not only techniques but enemy special abilities in general (Uepon no Game Land and Phantasy Star Cave). rrpg.jp says "makes it quiet (effect unknown)". Names and TP are from rrpg.jp and Uepon no Game Land / Kōryaku Tengoku (the same table); learners and levels were checked against Phantasy Star Cave (overseas version).

phantasystar-shinparo.desc: Makes biological enemies flee from battle.
phantasystar-shinparo.note: Sources differ on the target (Uepon no Game Land says "all biological enemies", Phantasy Star Cave says "one biological enemy", and rrpg.jp gives the effect as unknown), so no scope is set. Names and TP are from rrpg.jp and Uepon no Game Land / Kōryaku Tengoku (the same table); learners and levels were checked against Phantasy Star Cave (overseas version).

phantasystar-shifuta.note: Names and TP are from rrpg.jp and Uepon no Game Land / Kōryaku Tengoku (the same table); learners and levels were checked against Phantasy Star Cave (overseas version).

phantasystar-shutsu.note: Names and TP are from rrpg.jp and Uepon no Game Land / Kōryaku Tengoku (the same table); learners and levels were checked against Phantasy Star Cave (overseas version).

phantasystar-sashutsu.note: The all-allies version of Shūtsu. Names and TP are from rrpg.jp and Uepon no Game Land / Kōryaku Tengoku (the same table); learners and levels were checked against Phantasy Star Cave (overseas version).

phantasystar-shunera.note: The learning level differs: 6 (Uepon no Game Land) versus 5 (Phantasy Star Cave). Names and TP are from rrpg.jp and Uepon no Game Land / Kōryaku Tengoku (the same table); learners and levels were checked against Phantasy Star Cave (overseas version).

phantasystar-sashunera.note: The all-allies version of Shunera. Amy learns the single-target Shunera and Anna learns the all-allies version. The learning level differs: 24 (Uepon no Game Land) versus 25 (Phantasy Star Cave). Names and TP are from rrpg.jp and Uepon no Game Land / Kōryaku Tengoku (the same table); learners and levels were checked against Phantasy Star Cave (overseas version).

phantasystar-debando.desc: Wraps all allies in a wall of air to reduce the damage they take.
phantasystar-debando.note: TP is given as 4 (Uepon no Game Land and Phantasy Star Cave); rrpg.jp says 5. The learning level differs: 7 (Uepon no Game Land) versus 4 (Phantasy Star Cave). Names and TP are from rrpg.jp and Uepon no Game Land / Kōryaku Tengoku (the same table); learners and levels were checked against Phantasy Star Cave (overseas version).

phantasystar-resuta.desc: Restores a little of one ally's HP, an entry-level technique of the Resuta line.
phantasystar-resuta.note: It restores 20. Rolf's learning level differs: 8 (Uepon no Game Land) versus 1 (Phantasy Star Cave). Names and TP are from rrpg.jp and Uepon no Game Land / Kōryaku Tengoku (the same table); learners and levels were checked against Phantasy Star Cave (overseas version).

phantasystar-giresuta.desc: Restores a good amount of one ally's HP, an intermediate technique of the Resuta line.
phantasystar-giresuta.note: It restores 60. Names and TP are from rrpg.jp and Uepon no Game Land / Kōryaku Tengoku (the same table); learners and levels were checked against Phantasy Star Cave (overseas version).

phantasystar-naresuta.desc: Fully restores one ally's HP, an advanced technique of the Resuta line.
phantasystar-naresuta.note: Names and TP are from rrpg.jp and Uepon no Game Land / Kōryaku Tengoku (the same table); learners and levels were checked against Phantasy Star Cave (overseas version).

phantasystar-saresuta.desc: Restores a little of all allies' HP, an entry-level all-allies technique of the Resuta line.
phantasystar-saresuta.note: It restores 20. Names and TP are from rrpg.jp and Uepon no Game Land / Kōryaku Tengoku (the same table); learners and levels were checked against Phantasy Star Cave (overseas version).

phantasystar-gisaresuta.desc: Restores a good amount of all allies' HP, an intermediate all-allies technique of the Resuta line.
phantasystar-gisaresuta.note: It restores 60. Names and TP are from rrpg.jp and Uepon no Game Land / Kōryaku Tengoku (the same table); learners and levels were checked against Phantasy Star Cave (overseas version).

phantasystar-nasaresuta.desc: Fully restores all allies' HP, an advanced all-allies technique of the Resuta line.
phantasystar-nasaresuta.note: Names and TP are from rrpg.jp and Uepon no Game Land / Kōryaku Tengoku (the same table); learners and levels were checked against Phantasy Star Cave (overseas version).

phantasystar-sakura.desc: Fully restores one ally's HP at the cost of the caster's life.
phantasystar-sakura.note: The caster is knocked out. Names and TP are from rrpg.jp and Uepon no Game Land / Kōryaku Tengoku (the same table); learners and levels were checked against Phantasy Star Cave (overseas version).

phantasystar-nasakura.desc: Fully restores all allies' HP at the cost of the caster's life.
phantasystar-nasakura.note: The all-allies version of Sākura. In this line alone, "Na" is used to widen the target to everyone rather than to mark a higher rank (the "Sa" of Sākura is part of the word). The caster is knocked out. Names and TP are from rrpg.jp and Uepon no Game Land / Kōryaku Tengoku (the same table); learners and levels were checked against Phantasy Star Cave (overseas version).

phantasystar-anti.note: Names and TP are from rrpg.jp and Uepon no Game Land / Kōryaku Tengoku (the same table); learners and levels were checked against Phantasy Star Cave (overseas version).

phantasystar-ribasa.desc: Revives one knocked-out ally (restores 30 HP to an ally who is alive).
phantasystar-ribasa.note: It cannot be used in battle (rrpg.jp; confirmed in only one source). Anna's learning level differs: 24 (Uepon no Game Land) versus 27 (Phantasy Star Cave). Names and TP are from rrpg.jp and Uepon no Game Land / Kōryaku Tengoku (the same table); learners and levels were checked against Phantasy Star Cave (overseas version).

phantasystar-ryuka.desc: Returns you to the town where you last saved.
phantasystar-ryuka.note: The destination differs: the Japanese sources (rrpg.jp and Uepon no Game Land) say "the place or town where you last saved", while Phantasy Star Cave says "Rolf's house". The Japanese sources are used. Shir's learning level differs: 5 (Uepon no Game Land) versus 6 (Phantasy Star Cave). Names and TP are from rrpg.jp and Uepon no Game Land / Kōryaku Tengoku (the same table); learners and levels were checked against Phantasy Star Cave (overseas version).

phantasystar-hinasu.note: Names and TP are from rrpg.jp and Uepon no Game Land / Kōryaku Tengoku (the same table); learners and levels were checked against Phantasy Star Cave (overseas version).

phantasystar-mushika.desc: A story-progress technique that lets you play keyboard instruments.
phantasystar-mushika.note: It is not learned by leveling but taught in the town of Optano (2000 meseta for men, 5000 meseta for women). Everyone except Rudo can learn it, but the users field lists a representative example. It is not used in battle. Names and TP are from rrpg.jp and Uepon no Game Land / Kōryaku Tengoku (the same table); learners and levels were checked against Phantasy Star Cave (overseas version).

shiningforce-blaze.note: Lv 1 to 4. Lv 1: MP 2, single target, low power / Lv 2: MP 5, 5-tile cross / Lv 3: MP 8, 5-tile cross, medium power / Lv 4: MP 8, single target, high power (up to around 40). Range is 1 to 2. Tao learns each level at Lv 1, 4, 12 and 20; Anri and Aleph learn up to Lv 2; Arthur learns only Lv 1. Anri's Lv 1 is available from the start in Izuito and Walkthrough 1, but the RRPG table can be read as a different value (3).

shiningforce-freeze.note: Lv 1 to 4. Lv 1: MP 3, single target / Lv 2: MP 7, 5-tile cross / Lv 3: MP 10, 5-tile cross, range 2 to 3 / Lv 4: MP 10, single target, high power (up to around 50), range 2 to 3. Anri (Lv 5, 13, 16, 23) and Domingo (start, 4, 13, 26) learn up to Lv 4; Aleph learns up to Lv 2; Arthur learns only Lv 1.

shiningforce-spark.desc: Damages enemies in range with lightning.
shiningforce-spark.note: Lv 1 to 4. Lv 1: MP 8, 5-tile cross / Lv 2: MP 15, 13 tiles / Lv 3: MP 20, 13 tiles, medium power / Lv 4: MP 20, single target, high power (up to around 60). Only Aleph learns up to Lv 4 (start, 17, 22, 30); Anri learns up to Lv 2; Arthur learns only Lv 1. The range of Lv 2 and 3 differs by source: 1 to 2, 1 to 3, or 3. The English release uses a different name.

shiningforce-soulsteal.desc: Instantly kills one enemy with a certain probability.
shiningforce-soulsteal.note: Lv 1: MP 8, single target. Lv 2 (MP 15, 5-tile cross) appears in Uji's Room and in the list in Walkthrough 1, but the lists in RRPG and Izuito show only Lv 1, and no character who learns Lv 2 could be confirmed.

shiningforce-sleep.desc: Puts one enemy to sleep with a certain probability.
shiningforce-sleep.note: Lv 1 only. Range is 1 to 2. Tao learns it at Lv 8; Hanzo has it from when he joins.

shiningforce-antispell.desc: Seals one enemy's magic with a certain probability.
shiningforce-antispell.note: Lv 1 only. Range is 1 to 2. Tao learns it at Lv 16; Hanzo has it from when he joins.

shiningforce-illute.note: Lv 1 only. Range is 1 to 2. Anri learns it at Lv 10 and Domingo at Lv 7.

shiningforce-attack.note: Lv 1 only. Attack +15, range is 1 to 3 tiles including yourself. Tao learns it at Lv 27 and Domingo at Lv 20.

shiningforce-heal.note: Lv 1 to 4. Lv 1: MP 3, restores around 15, range 1 / Lv 2: MP 5, around 15, range 2 / Lv 3: MP 10, around 30, range 3 / Lv 4: MP 20, full recovery, range 1. Lowe (start, 7, 16, 22), Chip (start, 5, 16, 21) and Gong (start, 8, 16, 24) learn up to Lv 4; Torasu learns up to Lv 2.

shiningforce-aura.desc: Restores the HP of allies in range all at once.
shiningforce-aura.note: Lv 1 to 4. Lv 1: MP 7, 5-tile cross, restores around 15 / Lv 2: MP 11, 13 tiles, around 15 / Lv 3: MP 15, 13 tiles, around 30 / Lv 4: MP 18, fully restores all allies. Range is 1 to 3. Only Torasu learns up to Lv 4; Chip learns up to Lv 2 and Gong only Lv 1. The RRPG table can be read as giving Lv 4 a cost of 28, but all other sources say 18.

shiningforce-antidote.note: Lv 1 only. Range is 1. Lowe learns it at Lv 4; Torasu has it from when he joins.

shiningforce-quick.note: Lv 1: MP 5, single target / Lv 2: MP 16, 5-tile cross. The boost is +10 to both speed and defense (RRPG, Uji's Room, Izuito). Walkthrough 1 says "speed +15". Lowe learns Lv 1 at Lv 13 and 25, and Chip at Lv 12.

shiningforce-slow.note: Lv 1: MP 5, single target / Lv 2: MP 20, 5-tile cross. The drop is -10 to both speed and defense (RRPG, Uji's Room). Izuito gives speed only, and Walkthrough 1 says "speed -15". Lowe learns Lv 1 at Lv 10 and 19, and Chip at Lv 8.

shiningforce-spellwall.desc: Puts up a guard on one ally that blocks enemy magic.
shiningforce-spellwall.note: Lv 1 only. Range is 1 to 2. It blocks magic with a certain probability. Torasu has it from when he joins (Walkthrough 1 says he learns it at Lv 12). Hanzo learns it at Lv 15.

shiningforce-return.desc: Leaves the battlefield and takes the whole party back to the church where you last stopped.
shiningforce-return.note: Lv 1 only. Only the hero, Max, can use it.

pokemon-hoono-no-panchi.desc: Attacks with a flame-wrapped fist and may burn the target (power 75).
pokemon-hoono-no-panchi.note: It looks like a punch, but in Gen I it counts as a special move because it is Fire type. There is no TM, and only two Pokémon learn it by leveling up. Which Pokémon learn it is confirmed only in Serebii.

pokemon-hinoko.desc: Attacks with small flames and may burn the target (power 40).
pokemon-hinoko.note: Which Pokémon learn it is confirmed only in Serebii.

pokemon-kaenhousha.desc: Blasts the target with fierce flames and may burn it (power 95).
pokemon-kaenhousha.note: It is not a TM in Gen I. Which Pokémon learn it is confirmed only in Serebii.

pokemon-hoono-no-uzu.desc: Traps the target in a whirl of flame for 2 to 5 turns, during which it cannot move (power 15, accuracy 70).
pokemon-hoono-no-uzu.note: Which Pokémon learn it is confirmed only in Serebii.

pokemon-daimonji.desc: The strongest Fire move, attacking with a flame shaped like the character "大", with a 30% chance to burn (power 120, accuracy 85).
pokemon-daimonji.note: The burn chance is 30% only in Gen I (10% in later games). TM38. Which Pokémon learn it is confirmed only in Serebii.

pokemon-reitou-panchi.desc: Attacks with a fist infused with cold and may freeze the target (power 75).
pokemon-reitou-panchi.note: It looks like a punch, but in Gen I it counts as a special move because it is Ice type. Which Pokémon learn it is confirmed only in Serebii.

pokemon-reitou-biimu.desc: Fires a cold beam and may freeze the target (power 95).
pokemon-reitou-biimu.note: TM13. Which Pokémon learn it is confirmed only in Serebii.

pokemon-fubuki.desc: The strongest Ice move, blasting the target with a fierce blizzard, and may freeze it (power 120, accuracy 90).
pokemon-fubuki.note: TM14. Which Pokémon learn it is confirmed only in Serebii.

pokemon-oorora-biimu.desc: Attacks with a rainbow-colored beam, with a one-in-three chance to lower the target's Attack (power 65).
pokemon-oorora-biimu.note: Which Pokémon learn it is confirmed only in Serebii.

pokemon-kaminari-panchi.desc: Attacks with a fist infused with electricity and may paralyze the target (power 75).
pokemon-kaminari-panchi.note: It looks like a punch, but in Gen I it counts as a special move because it is Electric type. Which Pokémon learn it is confirmed only in Serebii.

pokemon-denki-shokku.desc: Shocks the target with electricity and may paralyze it (power 40).
pokemon-denki-shokku.note: Which Pokémon learn it is confirmed only in Serebii.

pokemon-juumanboruto.desc: Shocks the target with a powerful bolt and may paralyze it (power 95).
pokemon-juumanboruto.note: TM24. Which Pokémon learn it is confirmed only in Serebii.

pokemon-kaminari.desc: The strongest Electric move, striking with lightning, and may paralyze the target (power 120, accuracy 70).
pokemon-kaminari.note: TM25. Which Pokémon learn it is confirmed only in Serebii.

pokemon-tsuru-no-muchi.desc: Attacks by lashing with vines like whips (power 35).
pokemon-tsuru-no-muchi.note: It counts as a special move in Gen I because it is Grass type. Which Pokémon learn it is confirmed only in Serebii.

pokemon-suitoru.desc: Attacks and restores half of the damage dealt to your own HP (power 20).
pokemon-suitoru.note: A Grass-type special move. Which Pokémon learn it is confirmed only in Serebii.

pokemon-megadorein.desc: Attacks more strongly than Suitoru and restores half of the damage dealt to your own HP (power 40).
pokemon-megadorein.note: A Grass-type special move. In Gen I it is learned from TM21. Which Pokémon learn it is confirmed only in Serebii.

pokemon-happa-kattaa.desc: Flings sharp leaves and is likely to land a critical hit (power 55, accuracy 95).
pokemon-happa-kattaa.note: Which Pokémon learn it is confirmed only in Serebii.

pokemon-sooraabiimu.desc: Gathers light on the first turn and fires a powerful beam on the second (power 120).
pokemon-sooraabiimu.note: TM22. Which Pokémon learn it is confirmed only in Serebii.

pokemon-hanabira-no-mai.desc: Attacks for 2 to 3 turns in a dancing manner, then leaves the user confused (power 70).
pokemon-hanabira-no-mai.note: Which Pokémon learn it is confirmed only in Serebii.

pokemon-mizudeppou.note: TM12. Which Pokémon learn it is confirmed only in Serebii.

pokemon-haidoro-ponpu.desc: The strongest Water move, blasting the target with a huge amount of water (power 120, accuracy 80).
pokemon-haidoro-ponpu.note: Which Pokémon learn it is confirmed only in Serebii.

pokemon-naminori.desc: Raises a great wave to attack (power 95). Used in the field, it lets you travel over water.
pokemon-naminori.note: HM03. Which Pokémon learn it is confirmed only in Serebii.

pokemon-baburu-kousen.desc: Shoots bubbles forcefully, with a one-in-three chance to lower the target's Speed (power 65).
pokemon-baburu-kousen.note: TM11. Which Pokémon learn it is confirmed only in Serebii.

pokemon-takinobori.note: It looks like a body slam, but in Gen I it counts as a special move because it is Water type. It has no effect in the field in Gen I. Which Pokémon learn it is confirmed only in Serebii.

pokemon-karade-hasamu.desc: Clamps the target in a shell for 2 to 5 turns, during which it cannot move (power 35, accuracy 75).
pokemon-karade-hasamu.note: Which Pokémon learn it is confirmed only in Serebii.

pokemon-awa.desc: Blows bubbles, with a one-in-three chance to lower the target's Speed (power 20).
pokemon-awa.note: Which Pokémon learn it is confirmed only in Serebii.

pokemon-kurabuhanmaa.desc: Pounds the target with a big claw and is likely to land a critical hit (power 90, accuracy 85).
pokemon-kurabuhanmaa.note: It looks like a claw strike, but in Gen I it counts as a special move because it is Water type. Which Pokémon learn it is confirmed only in Serebii.

pokemon-saike-kousen.desc: Fires a mysterious beam and may confuse the target (power 65).
pokemon-saike-kousen.note: Which Pokémon learn it is confirmed only in Serebii.

pokemon-nenriki.desc: Attacks with the power of thought and may confuse the target (power 50).
pokemon-nenriki.note: Which Pokémon learn it is confirmed only in Serebii.

pokemon-saikokineshisu.desc: Attacks with strong psychic power, with a one-in-three chance to lower the target's Special (power 90).
pokemon-saikokineshisu.note: TM29. Which Pokémon learn it is confirmed only in Serebii.

pokemon-yumekui.desc: Works only on a sleeping target, and restores half of the damage dealt to your own HP (power 100).
pokemon-yumekui.note: A Psychic-type special move. TM42. Which Pokémon learn it is confirmed only in Serebii.

pokemon-saikouweebu.desc: Deals random damage with a psychic wave, from 1 up to less than 1.5 times the user's level (accuracy 80).
pokemon-saikouweebu.note: It is learned only through TM46 (no Pokémon learns it by leveling up; Pokémon Wiki). The users field lists examples of Pokémon that learn it from the TM.

pokemon-ryuu-no-ikari.desc: Always deals a fixed 40 damage, regardless of the target's type.
pokemon-ryuu-no-ikari.note: The only Dragon-type move in Gen I. TM23. Which Pokémon learn it is confirmed only in Serebii.

pokemon-tsurugi-no-mai.desc: Dances a war dance to sharply raise (2 stages) the user's Attack.
pokemon-tsurugi-no-mai.note: TM03. Which Pokémon learn it is confirmed only in Serebii.

pokemon-yoga-no-pooze.desc: Concentrates the mind to raise the user's Attack.
pokemon-yoga-no-pooze.note: Which Pokémon learn it is confirmed only in Serebii.

pokemon-kakubaru.desc: Squares up the body to raise the user's Attack.
pokemon-kakubaru.note: Which Pokémon learn it is confirmed only in Serebii.

pokemon-seichou.desc: Grows the body to raise the user's Special (raising the power of special moves and defense against them).
pokemon-seichou.note: In Gen I it is Normal type, and it raises "Special" by 1 stage (Pokémon Wiki). Which Pokémon learn it is confirmed only in Serebii.

pokemon-dowasure.desc: Empties the mind to sharply raise (2 stages) the user's Special.
pokemon-dowasure.note: In Gen I, Special is a single stat, so the power of special moves and the defense against them rise at once (Pokémon Wiki). Which Pokémon learn it is confirmed only in Serebii.

pokemon-katakunaru.desc: Hardens the body to raise the user's Defense.
pokemon-katakunaru.note: Which Pokémon learn it is confirmed only in Serebii.

pokemon-kara-ni-komoru.desc: Withdraws into its shell to raise the user's Defense.
pokemon-kara-ni-komoru.note: Water type. Which Pokémon learn it is confirmed only in Serebii.

pokemon-marukunaru.desc: Curls up into a ball to raise the user's Defense.
pokemon-marukunaru.note: Which Pokémon learn it is confirmed only in Serebii.

pokemon-bariaa.desc: Creates a barrier to sharply raise (2 stages) the user's Defense.
pokemon-bariaa.note: Psychic type. Which Pokémon learn it is confirmed only in Serebii.

pokemon-tokeru.desc: Liquefies the body to sharply raise (2 stages) the user's Defense.
pokemon-tokeru.note: Poison type. Which Pokémon learn it is confirmed only in Serebii.

pokemon-kousoku-idou.desc: Lightens the body to sharply raise (2 stages) the user's Speed.
pokemon-kousoku-idou.note: Psychic type. Which Pokémon learn it is confirmed only in Serebii.

pokemon-nakigoe.desc: Cries cutely to lower the target's guard and lower its Attack.
pokemon-nakigoe.note: Which Pokémon learn it is confirmed only in Serebii.

pokemon-shippo-wo-furu.desc: Wags its tail to lower the target's guard and lower its Defense.
pokemon-shippo-wo-furu.note: Which Pokémon learn it is confirmed only in Serebii.

pokemon-niramitsukeru.desc: Glares sharply to scare the target and lower its Defense.
pokemon-niramitsukeru.note: Which Pokémon learn it is confirmed only in Serebii.

pokemon-iyana-oto.desc: Makes a grating sound to sharply lower (2 stages) the target's Defense (accuracy 85).
pokemon-iyana-oto.note: Which Pokémon learn it is confirmed only in Serebii.

pokemon-ito-wo-haku.desc: Spits and wraps the target in string to lower its Speed (accuracy 95).
pokemon-ito-wo-haku.note: Bug type. Which Pokémon learn it is confirmed only in Serebii.

pokemon-sunakake.desc: Throws sand in the target's face to lower its accuracy.
pokemon-sunakake.note: It is Normal type in Gen I. Which Pokémon learn it is confirmed only in Serebii.

pokemon-enmaku.desc: Spews smoke to block the view and lower the target's accuracy.
pokemon-enmaku.note: Which Pokémon learn it is confirmed only in Serebii.

pokemon-supuun-mage.desc: Bends a spoon to draw attention and lower the target's accuracy (accuracy 80).
pokemon-supuun-mage.note: Psychic type. Which Pokémon learn it is confirmed only in Serebii.

pokemon-utau.desc: Puts the target to sleep with a soothing song (accuracy 55).
pokemon-utau.note: Which Pokémon learn it is confirmed only in Serebii.

pokemon-nemurigona.desc: Scatters sleep powder to put the target to sleep (accuracy 75).
pokemon-nemurigona.note: Grass type. Which Pokémon learn it is confirmed only in Serebii.

pokemon-saiminjutsu.desc: Hypnotizes the target to put it to sleep (accuracy 60).
pokemon-saiminjutsu.note: Psychic type. Serebii lists the accuracy as 59.8 (internal value 153/256). Which Pokémon learn it is confirmed only in Serebii.

pokemon-akuma-no-kissu.desc: Puts the target to sleep with a frightening kiss (accuracy 75).
pokemon-akuma-no-kissu.note: Normal type. Which Pokémon learn it is confirmed only in Serebii.

pokemon-kinoko-no-houshi.desc: Scatters mushroom spores to put the target to sleep for certain (accuracy 100).
pokemon-kinoko-no-houshi.note: Grass type. Which Pokémon learn it is confirmed only in Serebii.

pokemon-chouonpa.desc: Blasts the target with ultrasonic waves to confuse it (accuracy 55).
pokemon-chouonpa.note: Which Pokémon learn it is confirmed only in Serebii.

pokemon-ayashii-hikari.desc: Shows the target a strange light to confuse it.
pokemon-ayashii-hikari.note: Ghost type. Which Pokémon learn it is confirmed only in Serebii.

pokemon-doku-no-kona.desc: Scatters poison powder to poison the target (accuracy 75).
pokemon-doku-no-kona.note: Poison type. Serebii lists the accuracy as 74.6 (internal value 191/256). Which Pokémon learn it is confirmed only in Serebii.

pokemon-doku-gasu.desc: Sprays poison gas to poison the target (accuracy 55).
pokemon-doku-gasu.note: Which Pokémon learn it is confirmed only in Serebii.

pokemon-dokudoku.desc: Badly poisons the target, so the damage it takes grows each turn (accuracy 85).
pokemon-dokudoku.note: TM06. Which Pokémon learn it is confirmed only in Serebii.

pokemon-shibiregona.desc: Scatters numbing powder to paralyze the target (accuracy 75).
pokemon-shibiregona.note: Grass type. Which Pokémon learn it is confirmed only in Serebii.

pokemon-denjiha.desc: Shocks the target with weak electricity to paralyze it.
pokemon-denjiha.note: Electric type. TM45. Which Pokémon learn it is confirmed only in Serebii.

pokemon-hebi-nirami.desc: Glares with a terrifying look to paralyze the target (accuracy 75).
pokemon-hebi-nirami.note: Which Pokémon learn it is confirmed only in Serebii.

pokemon-kanashibari.desc: Makes one of the target's moves unusable for a while (accuracy 55).
pokemon-kanashibari.note: It seals only one of the target's moves, not all of them. Which Pokémon learn it is confirmed only in Serebii.

pokemon-jikosaisei.desc: Restores half of the user's max HP.
pokemon-jikosaisei.note: Which Pokémon learn it is confirmed only in Serebii.

pokemon-tamago-umi.desc: Restores half of the user's max HP. In the field, the user can share its own HP with allies.
pokemon-tamago-umi.note: TM41, and only Chansey and Mew can learn it (Pokémon Wiki and Serebii agree). The HP shared in the field is one fifth of max HP. Which Pokémon learn it is confirmed only in Serebii.

pokemon-nemuru.desc: Fully restores HP and cures status ailments, but the user falls asleep for 2 turns.
pokemon-nemuru.note: Psychic type. TM44. Which Pokémon learn it is confirmed only in Serebii.

pokemon-hikari-no-kabe.desc: Creates a wall of light to reduce the damage taken from special moves.
pokemon-hikari-no-kabe.note: Psychic type. Which Pokémon learn it is confirmed only in Serebii.

pokemon-rifurekutaa.desc: Creates a wall of light to reduce the damage taken from physical moves.
pokemon-rifurekutaa.note: Psychic type. TM33. Which Pokémon learn it is confirmed only in Serebii.

pokemon-shiroi-kiri.desc: Wraps the user in white mist so that the opponent's moves cannot lower its stats.
pokemon-shiroi-kiri.note: Ice type. Which Pokémon learn it is confirmed only in Serebii.

pokemon-kagebunshin.desc: Shows decoy images to confuse the target and raise the user's evasion.
pokemon-kagebunshin.note: TM32. Which Pokémon learn it is confirmed only in Serebii.

pokemon-chiisakunaru.desc: Shrinks the body to raise the user's evasion.
pokemon-chiisakunaru.note: Which Pokémon learn it is confirmed only in Serebii.

pokemon-terepooto.desc: In the field, instantly takes you to the Pokémon Center where you last healed. It can also be used to flee from a battle with a wild Pokémon.
pokemon-terepooto.note: Psychic type. TM30. It fails in trainer battles. The destination is the Pokémon Center where you last healed your Pokémon, not the one you last visited (Pokémon Wiki). Which Pokémon learn it is confirmed only in Serebii.

pokemon-furasshu.desc: In the field, lights up dark caves. In battle, it lowers the target's accuracy with a strong light (accuracy 70).
pokemon-furasshu.note: HM05. Using it in the field requires the Gray Badge (Pokémon Wiki). Which Pokémon learn it is confirmed only in Serebii.

pokemon-fukitobashi.desc: Blows a wild Pokémon away with a strong wind to end the battle (accuracy 85).
pokemon-fukitobashi.note: It fails in trainer battles (in Gen I the opponent is not switched out). TM04. Which Pokémon learn it is confirmed only in Serebii.

pokemon-hoeru.desc: Roars to drive off a wild Pokémon and end the battle.
pokemon-hoeru.note: It has no effect in trainer battles (Serebii's description: "only effective against wild Pokémon"). Which Pokémon learn it is confirmed only in Serebii.

pokemon-yadorigi-no-tane.desc: Plants a seed on the target and drains a little of its HP each turn to restore your own (accuracy 90).
pokemon-yadorigi-no-tane.note: Grass type. Which Pokémon learn it is confirmed only in Serebii.

pokemon-kuroi-kiri.desc: Uses black mist to reset all stat changes of allies and enemies.
pokemon-kuroi-kiri.note: Ice type. In Gen I, besides stat changes, it also removes states such as confusion, Leech Seed and Reflect, and the opponent's status ailments (paralysis, burn and so on) (Pokémon Wiki). Which Pokémon learn it is confirmed only in Serebii.

pokemon-kiaidame.desc: Focuses the spirit to make critical hits more likely (so it is said).
pokemon-kiaidame.note: In Gen I (excluding Pokémon Stadium 2), a bug actually makes critical hits less likely (Pokémon Wiki). Which Pokémon learn it is confirmed only in Serebii.

pokemon-yubi-wo-furu.desc: Waggles a finger so that one of the other moves comes out at random.
pokemon-yubi-wo-furu.note: TM35. Which Pokémon learn it is confirmed only in Serebii.

pokemon-monomane.desc: Learns one of the target's moves so it can be used for the rest of that battle.
pokemon-monomane.note: TM31. Which Pokémon learn it is confirmed only in Serebii.

pokemon-oumugaeshi.desc: Uses again the move the target used just before.
pokemon-oumugaeshi.note: Flying type. Which Pokémon learn it is confirmed only in Serebii.

pokemon-henshin.desc: Transforms into the target's appearance, type and moves (each move has 5 PP).
pokemon-henshin.note: Which Pokémon learn it is confirmed only in Serebii.

pokemon-tekusuchaa.desc: Changes the user's type to the same type as the target.
pokemon-tekusuchaa.note: In Gen I it changes to the target's type (in later games it changes to the type of one of the user's own moves; Pokémon Wiki). Which Pokémon learn it is confirmed only in Serebii.

pokemon-migawari.desc: Uses a quarter of the user's HP to create a decoy that takes the opponent's attacks in its place.
pokemon-migawari.note: TM50. Which Pokémon learn it is confirmed only in Serebii.

pokemon-haneru.desc: It just hops around, and nothing happens.
pokemon-haneru.note: Which Pokémon learn it is confirmed only in Serebii.

bravely-cure.desc: Restores a little HP to an ally.
bravely-cure.note: White Magic Lv1. Can be cast on all allies. Damages undead. MP cost matches between Gamer Guides and a Dengeki Online article on the demo version.

bravely-poisona.note: White Magic Lv1. MP cost matches between Gamer Guides and a Dengeki Online article on the demo version.

bravely-blindna.note: White Magic Lv1. Corresponds to FF's Buraina. Game8's spell list gives a spelling that reads "Purana", but the White Mage page on Altema, the same site, gives "Burana". MP cost confirmed only in an English-language guide (Gamer Guides).

bravely-protect.note: White Magic Lv2. Can be stacked. Sources differ on the amount: Game8 says 50% (up to 100%), while Gamer Guides says 25%. MP cost confirmed only in an English-language guide (Gamer Guides).

bravely-shell.note: White Magic Lv2. Can be stacked. Sources differ on the amount: Game8 says 50% (up to 100%), while Gamer Guides says 25%. MP cost confirmed only in an English-language guide (Gamer Guides).

bravely-aero.desc: Damages an enemy with Wind magic.
bravely-aero.note: White Magic Lv2. Can be cast on all enemies. The Earo line was Blue Magic in FF V, but here it is an attack spell of White Magic. MP cost confirmed only in an English-language guide (Gamer Guides).

bravely-cura.note: White Magic Lv3. Can be cast on all allies. Damages undead. MP cost confirmed only in an English-language guide (Gamer Guides).

bravely-raise.desc: Revives a fallen ally and restores a little HP.
bravely-raise.note: White Magic Lv3. Used on undead, it causes instant death with a 70% chance. MP cost confirmed only in an English-language guide (Gamer Guides).

bravely-esuna.desc: Cures poison, blindness, silence, sleep, paralysis, fear, confusion and more at once.
bravely-esuna.note: White Magic Lv3. MP cost confirmed only in an English-language guide (Gamer Guides).

bravely-reflect.desc: Puts up a barrier that reflects White, Black and Time Magic.
bravely-reflect.note: White Magic Lv4. Also reflects allies' healing magic and the like. MP cost confirmed only in an English-language guide (Gamer Guides).

bravely-dispel.desc: Removes effects such as Stop, Rifureku, and stat boosts and drops.
bravely-dispel.note: White Magic Lv4. MP cost confirmed only in an English-language guide (Gamer Guides).

bravely-aerora.desc: Damages an enemy with Wind magic (medium).
bravely-aerora.note: White Magic Lv4. Can be cast on all enemies. MP cost confirmed only in an English-language guide (Gamer Guides).

bravely-esunaga.desc: Cures all allies of the same status ailments as Esuna.
bravely-esunaga.note: White Magic Lv5. Is not reflected by Rifureku. MP cost confirmed only in an English-language guide (Gamer Guides).

bravely-curada.desc: Restores a large amount of HP to an ally.
bravely-curada.note: White Magic Lv5. Can be cast on all allies. Damages undead. It sits between Kearura and Kearuga. MP cost confirmed only in an English-language guide (Gamer Guides).

bravely-aeroga.desc: Deals heavy damage to an enemy with Wind magic.
bravely-aeroga.note: White Magic Lv5. Can be cast on all enemies. MP cost confirmed only in an English-language guide (Gamer Guides).

bravely-curaga.desc: Restores a very large amount of HP to an ally.
bravely-curaga.note: White Magic Lv6. Can be cast on all allies. Damages undead. MP cost confirmed only in an English-language guide (Gamer Guides).

bravely-arise.desc: Revives a fallen ally and fully restores HP.
bravely-arise.note: White Magic Lv6. Used on undead, it causes instant death with a 70% chance. MP cost confirmed only in an English-language guide (Gamer Guides).

bravely-holy.desc: Deals heavy damage to an enemy with Light magic.
bravely-holy.note: White Magic Lv6. MP cost confirmed only in an English-language guide (Gamer Guides).

bravely-fire.desc: Damages an enemy with Fire magic.
bravely-fire.note: Black Magic Lv1. Can be cast on all enemies. MP cost matches between Gamer Guides and a Dengeki Online article on the demo version.

bravely-blizzard.desc: Damages an enemy with cold magic.
bravely-blizzard.note: Black Magic Lv1. Can be cast on all enemies. The element in the game is "Water" (there is no Ice element in this game). MP cost matches between Gamer Guides and a Dengeki Online article on the demo version.

bravely-thunder.desc: Damages an enemy with Lightning magic.
bravely-thunder.note: Black Magic Lv1. Can be cast on all enemies. MP cost matches between Gamer Guides and a Dengeki Online article on the demo version.

bravely-poison.note: Black Magic Lv2. Added value 75 (Gamer Guides lists a 75% success rate). MP cost confirmed only in an English-language guide (Gamer Guides).

bravely-sleep.note: Black Magic Lv2. Added value 75. MP cost confirmed only in an English-language guide (Gamer Guides).

bravely-silence.desc: Silences an enemy, sealing its magic.
bravely-silence.note: Black Magic Lv2. Added value 75. MP cost confirmed only in an English-language guide (Gamer Guides).

bravely-fira.desc: Damages an enemy with Fire magic (medium).
bravely-fira.note: Black Magic Lv3. Can be cast on all enemies. MP cost confirmed only in an English-language guide (Gamer Guides).

bravely-blizzara.desc: Damages an enemy with cold magic (medium).
bravely-blizzara.note: Black Magic Lv3. Can be cast on all enemies. The element in the game is "Water". MP cost confirmed only in an English-language guide (Gamer Guides).

bravely-thundara.desc: Damages an enemy with Lightning magic (medium).
bravely-thundara.note: Black Magic Lv3. Can be cast on all enemies. MP cost confirmed only in an English-language guide (Gamer Guides).

bravely-drain.note: Black Magic Lv4. Is not reflected by Rifureku. Used on undead, it hurts the caster instead. MP cost confirmed only in an English-language guide (Gamer Guides).

bravely-aspir.note: Black Magic Lv4. Is not reflected by Rifureku. Used on undead, it lowers the caster's own MP instead. MP cost confirmed only in an English-language guide (Gamer Guides).

bravely-fear.note: Black Magic Lv4. Added value 75. MP cost confirmed only in an English-language guide (Gamer Guides).

bravely-firaga.desc: Deals heavy damage to an enemy with Fire magic.
bravely-firaga.note: Black Magic Lv5. Can be cast on all enemies. MP cost confirmed only in an English-language guide (Gamer Guides).

bravely-blizzaga.desc: Deals heavy damage to an enemy with cold magic.
bravely-blizzaga.note: Black Magic Lv5. Can be cast on all enemies. The element in the game is "Water". MP cost confirmed only in an English-language guide (Gamer Guides).

bravely-thundaga.desc: Deals heavy damage to an enemy with Lightning magic.
bravely-thundaga.note: Black Magic Lv5. Can be cast on all enemies. MP cost confirmed only in an English-language guide (Gamer Guides).

bravely-dark.desc: Deals heavy damage to an enemy with Darkness magic.
bravely-dark.note: Black Magic Lv6. MP cost confirmed only in an English-language guide (Gamer Guides).

bravely-kill.desc: Erases an enemy whose level is at least 10 lower than the caster's.
bravely-kill.note: Black Magic Lv6. No experience or other rewards are gained from enemies defeated this way. Does not work on bosses. On the target, Gamer Guides says all enemies, while Game8 says only "target", so the range could not be confirmed. MP cost confirmed only in an English-language guide (Gamer Guides).

bravely-death.note: Black Magic Lv6. Added value 60 (Gamer Guides lists a 60% success rate). Does not work on bosses. MP cost confirmed only in an English-language guide (Gamer Guides).

bravely-slow.desc: Lowers an enemy's speed for 4 turns.
bravely-slow.note: Time Magic Lv1. Can be stacked. Sources differ on the amount: Game8 says 50% action speed (up to 90%), while Gamer Guides says 25% speed. MP cost confirmed only in an English-language guide (Gamer Guides).

bravely-regen.desc: Restores a little HP at the end of each turn for 4 turns.
bravely-regen.note: Time Magic Lv1. Restores 3% of max HP per turn. MP cost confirmed only in an English-language guide (Gamer Guides).

bravely-quake.desc: Damages an enemy with Earth magic.
bravely-quake.note: Time Magic Lv1. Can be cast on all enemies. MP cost confirmed only in an English-language guide (Gamer Guides).

bravely-haste.note: Time Magic Lv2. Can be stacked (Game8 says action speed up 50%, up to 100%). MP cost confirmed only in an English-language guide (Gamer Guides).

bravely-teleport.desc: Escapes from a dungeon or a battle.
bravely-teleport.note: Time Magic Lv2. Cannot be used in boss battles. Can also be used to flee from a battle. MP cost confirmed only in an English-language guide (Gamer Guides).

bravely-quara.desc: Damages an enemy with Earth magic (medium).
bravely-quara.note: Time Magic Lv2. Can be cast on all enemies. MP cost confirmed only in an English-language guide (Gamer Guides).

bravely-gravity.desc: With a 50% chance, deals damage equal to half of an enemy's max HP.
bravely-gravity.note: Time Magic Lv3. Does not work on bosses. MP cost confirmed only in an English-language guide (Gamer Guides).
