bravely-veil.note: Time Magic Lv3. Can be stacked. A spell unique to this game. MP cost confirmed only in an English-language guide (Gamer Guides).

bravely-slowga.desc: Lowers the speed of all enemies for 4 turns.
bravely-slowga.note: Time Magic Lv3. Is not reflected by Rifureku. On the range, Gamer Guides says all enemies, while Game8 gives no range. MP cost confirmed only in an English-language guide (Gamer Guides).

bravely-hastega.desc: Raises the speed of all allies for 4 turns.
bravely-hastega.note: Time Magic Lv4. Is not reflected by Rifureku. MP cost confirmed only in an English-language guide (Gamer Guides).

bravely-veilga.desc: Raises the evasion of all allies for 4 turns.
bravely-veilga.note: Time Magic Lv4. Is not reflected by Rifureku. MP cost confirmed only in an English-language guide (Gamer Guides).

bravely-comet.desc: Deals Non-elemental magic damage up to 4 times.
bravely-comet.note: Time Magic Lv4. Each hit can miss. Is not reflected by Rifureku. MP cost confirmed only in an English-language guide (Gamer Guides).

bravely-quick.desc: Increases allies' number of attacks for 4 turns.
bravely-quick.note: Time Magic Lv5. Increases the number of attacks by 50% and can be stacked. It differs from FF's Quick (acting again right away). MP cost confirmed only in an English-language guide (Gamer Guides).

bravely-stop.desc: Stops an enemy's time so it cannot move.
bravely-stop.note: Time Magic Lv5. Added value 100 (Gamer Guides lists a 75% success rate, so they differ). MP cost confirmed only in an English-language guide (Gamer Guides).

bravely-quaga.desc: Deals heavy damage to an enemy with Earth magic.
bravely-quaga.note: Time Magic Lv5. Can be cast on all enemies. MP cost confirmed only in an English-language guide (Gamer Guides).

bravely-graviga.desc: With a 50% chance, deals damage equal to 75% of an enemy's max HP.
bravely-graviga.note: Time Magic Lv6. Does not work on bosses. MP cost confirmed only in an English-language guide (Gamer Guides).

bravely-reraise.desc: Lets a character revive automatically once after being knocked out.
bravely-reraise.note: Time Magic Lv6. In FF it is often White Magic, but in this game it is Time Magic. MP cost confirmed only in an English-language guide (Gamer Guides).

bravely-meteor.desc: Deals Non-elemental magic damage 4 times to random enemies.
bravely-meteor.note: Time Magic Lv6. Is not reflected by Rifureku. MP cost confirmed only in an English-language guide (Gamer Guides).

bravely-girtablulu.desc: Summons a creature that deals heavy Earth damage to all enemies.
bravely-girtablulu.note: Summon Magic Lv1. Earth element. Is not reflected by Rifureku. Usable from the moment you obtain the Summoner's asterisk. The Spiritmaster also has an ability called "Shōkan Gattai" with the same name, but it has a different effect (it raises the user's own stats) and is not treated as a spell, so it is not included. MP cost confirmed only in an English-language guide (Gamer Guides).

bravely-hresvelgr.desc: Summons a creature that deals heavy Wind damage to all enemies.
bravely-hresvelgr.note: Summon Magic Lv2. Wind element. Is not reflected by Rifureku. Usable once the hermit of the Wind Temple acknowledges you. The Spiritmaster also has an ability called "Shōkan Gattai" with the same name, but it has a different effect (it raises the user's own stats) and is not treated as a spell, so it is not included. MP cost confirmed only in an English-language guide (Gamer Guides).

bravely-ziusudra.desc: Summons a creature that deals heavy Water damage to all enemies.
bravely-ziusudra.note: Summon Magic Lv3. Water element. Is not reflected by Rifureku. Usable once the hermit of Mount Kireto acknowledges you. The Spiritmaster also has an ability called "Shōkan Gattai" with the same name, but it has a different effect (it raises the user's own stats) and is not treated as a spell, so it is not included. MP cost confirmed only in an English-language guide (Gamer Guides).

bravely-prometheus.desc: Summons a creature that deals heavy Fire damage to all enemies.
bravely-prometheus.note: Summon Magic Lv4. Fire element. Is not reflected by Rifureku. Usable once the hermit of the Fire Temple acknowledges you. The Spiritmaster also has an ability called "Shōkan Gattai" with the same name, but it has a different effect (it raises the user's own stats) and is not treated as a spell, so it is not included. MP cost confirmed only in an English-language guide (Gamer Guides).

bravely-deusex.desc: Summons a creature that deals heavy Lightning damage to all enemies.
bravely-deusex.note: Summon Magic Lv5. Lightning element. Is not reflected by Rifureku. Usable once the hermit of the Undying Tower acknowledges you. The Spiritmaster also has an ability called "Shōkan Gattai" with the same name, but it has a different effect (it raises the user's own stats) and is not treated as a spell, so it is not included. MP cost confirmed only in an English-language guide (Gamer Guides).

bravely-susanoo.desc: Summons a creature that deals heavy Non-elemental damage to all enemies.
bravely-susanoo.note: Summon Magic Lv6. No element. Is not reflected by Rifureku. Usable once the hermit of the Kusutora Islands acknowledges you. The Spiritmaster also has an ability called "Shōkan Gattai" with the same name, but it has a different effect (it raises the user's own stats) and is not treated as a spell, so it is not included. MP cost confirmed only in an English-language guide (Gamer Guides).

starocean-heal.desc: The most basic healing symbol, restoring a little HP to one ally.
starocean-heal.note: Learned by: Rena (starting), Noel (starting) (PlayStation version; cross-checked against ui-nap and RPGClassics).

starocean-curelight.desc: Restores more HP to one ally than Hīru.
starocean-curelight.note: Learned by: Rena (Lv10), Noel (starting) (PlayStation version; cross-checked against ui-nap and RPGClassics).

starocean-fairyheal.desc: Restores a large amount of HP to one ally.
starocean-fairyheal.note: Learned by: Rena (Lv52), Noel (Lv55) (PlayStation version; cross-checked against ui-nap and RPGClassics).

starocean-cureall.note: Learned by: Rena (Lv20), Noel (Lv41) (PlayStation version; cross-checked against ui-nap and RPGClassics). Both PlayStation sources say Noel learns it at Lv41 (AppMedia, for the SE version, says Lv20).

starocean-fairylight.desc: Restores a large amount of HP to all allies.
starocean-fairylight.note: Learned by: Rena (Lv65), Noel (Lv77) (PlayStation version; cross-checked against ui-nap and RPGClassics).

starocean-antidote.note: Learned by: Rena (Lv3) (PlayStation version; cross-checked against ui-nap and RPGClassics).

starocean-dispel.desc: Cures one ally of status ailments such as poison, petrification and paralysis all at once.
starocean-dispel.note: Learned by: Rena (Lv25), Noel (Lv60) (PlayStation version; cross-checked against ui-nap and RPGClassics). Renamed "Kyuakondishon" in the SE version (Wikipedia, AppMedia). The ailments it cures (poison, petrification, paralysis) come from the RPGClassics description.

starocean-raisedead.desc: Revives one fallen ally. This is the only symbol that can revive.
starocean-raisedead.note: Learned by: Rena (Lv60) (PlayStation version; cross-checked against ui-nap and RPGClassics). Only RPGClassics says the revived character comes back with about half HP. Wikipedia also states that this is a revival symbol only Rena can use.

starocean-protection.note: Learned by: Rena (Lv33), Leon (Lv32) (PlayStation version; cross-checked against ui-nap and RPGClassics). Both PlayStation sources say Leon learns it at Lv32 (AppMedia, for the SE version, says Lv33).

starocean-reflection.desc: Raises one ally's defense. Despite its name, it has no reflecting effect.
starocean-reflection.note: Learned by: Celine (Lv19) (PlayStation version; cross-checked against ui-nap and RPGClassics). Celine-only in the PlayStation version. In the SE version Celine no longer learns it, and the name was used for what Anchi was renamed to (a magic resistance boost) (Wikipedia).

starocean-haste.note: Learned by: Rena (Lv42), Leon (Lv42) (PlayStation version; cross-checked against ui-nap and RPGClassics).

starocean-growth.note: Learned by: Rena (Lv47), Leon (Lv50) (PlayStation version; cross-checked against ui-nap and RPGClassics).

starocean-bless.note: Learned by: Celine (Lv28), Noel (Lv72) (PlayStation version; cross-checked against ui-nap and RPGClassics). Only RPGClassics says it lets attacks land head-on against enemies that are guarding with a shield.

starocean-anti.desc: Reduces the damage all allies take from symbols.
starocean-anti.note: Learned by: Rena (Lv54), Celine (Lv59) (PlayStation version; cross-checked against ui-nap and RPGClassics). ui-nap describes it as "halves damage from spells", while RPGClassics describes it as "raises magic defense". Renamed "Rifurekushon" in the SE version (Wikipedia).

starocean-angelfeather.desc: Raises one ally's stats all at once.
starocean-angelfeather.note: Learned by: Rena (Lv72), Celine (Lv76) (PlayStation version; cross-checked against ui-nap and RPGClassics).

starocean-neutral.desc: Removes effects such as Direi and Dīpumisuto, cast by enemies, from one ally.
starocean-neutral.note: Learned by: Celine (Lv27), Noel (Lv45) (PlayStation version; cross-checked against ui-nap and RPGClassics).

starocean-deepmist.desc: Lowers the accuracy of all enemies with a mist.
starocean-deepmist.note: Learned by: Rena (Lv8), Leon (starting) (PlayStation version; cross-checked against ui-nap and RPGClassics).

starocean-silence.desc: Tries to seal the symbols of all enemies.
starocean-silence.note: Learned by: Rena (Lv12), Noel (Lv41) (PlayStation version; cross-checked against ui-nap and RPGClassics). Both PlayStation sources say Noel learns it at Lv41 (AppMedia, for the SE version, says starting).

starocean-forget.desc: Tries to seal an enemy's symbols.
starocean-forget.note: Learned by: Celine (Lv15) (PlayStation version; cross-checked against ui-nap and RPGClassics). Sources differ on the target (RPGClassics says all enemies, ui-nap says single target). The symbol itself was removed in the SE version (Wikipedia).

starocean-fixcloud.desc: Tries to stun all enemies and stop them in place.
starocean-fixcloud.note: Learned by: Rena (Lv18) (PlayStation version; cross-checked against ui-nap and RPGClassics). The spelling follows ui-nap. Jikū no Tō writes "Fifusukuraudo", and AppMedia (SE version) writes "Fikkusukuraudo". The North American release uses a different name.

starocean-delay.note: Learned by: Rena (Lv22), Leon (Lv36) (PlayStation version; cross-checked against ui-nap and RPGClassics).

starocean-acidrain.desc: Lowers the defense of all enemies with acid rain.
starocean-acidrain.note: Learned by: Leon (starting) (PlayStation version; cross-checked against ui-nap and RPGClassics).

starocean-curse.desc: Cancels the effects of symbols on one enemy.
starocean-curse.note: Learned by: Celine (Lv39), Noel (Lv66) (PlayStation version; cross-checked against ui-nap and RPGClassics).

starocean-lostmental.note: Learned by: Celine (Lv22), Noel (starting) (PlayStation version; cross-checked against ui-nap and RPGClassics). Negative element (Jikū no Tō, ui-nap). The North American release uses a different name.

starocean-bloodscula.note: Learned by: Noel (Lv49) (PlayStation version; cross-checked against ui-nap and RPGClassics). Negative element (Jikū no Tō, ui-nap). The spelling follows ui-nap and AppMedia (SE version). Jikū no Tō writes "Buraddosukyura".

starocean-wordofdeath.desc: Tries to instantly kill one enemy.
starocean-wordofdeath.note: Learned by: Leon (starting) (PlayStation version; cross-checked against ui-nap and RPGClassics). Jikū no Tō classifies it as Negative element.

starocean-darkcircle.desc: Wipes out all enemies whose HP is at or below one quarter of their max.
starocean-darkcircle.note: Learned by: Leon (Lv78) (PlayStation version; cross-checked against ui-nap and RPGClassics). Jikū no Tō classifies it as Non-elemental.

starocean-ray.desc: Attacks all enemies with a beam of light.
starocean-ray.note: Learned by: Rena (Lv14), Celine (Lv9) (PlayStation version; cross-checked against ui-nap and RPGClassics).

starocean-lightcross.desc: Attacks all enemies with a cross of light.
starocean-lightcross.note: Learned by: Rena (Lv30) (PlayStation version; cross-checked against ui-nap and RPGClassics).

starocean-starflare.desc: Attacks all enemies with a burning mass of light. Rena's strongest attack symbol.
starocean-starflare.note: Learned by: Rena (Lv63) (PlayStation version; cross-checked against ui-nap and RPGClassics).

starocean-lunalight.note: Learned by: Celine (Lv43) (PlayStation version; cross-checked against ui-nap and RPGClassics). Three sources agree on the Light element: Jikū no Tō, ui-nap and RPGClassics (Star Ocean Wiki lists it as Star element).

starocean-starlight.desc: Attacks all enemies with starlight. A Star-element symbol.
starocean-starlight.note: Learned by: Celine (Lv17), Leon (Lv34) (PlayStation version; cross-checked against ui-nap and RPGClassics). The Star element is not among the site's shared elements, so it is set to none. Changed to Light element in the SE version (Wikipedia).

starocean-southerncross.desc: Attacks all enemies with a shining cross-shaped star. A Star-element symbol.
starocean-southerncross.note: Learned by: Celine (Lv49) (PlayStation version; cross-checked against ui-nap and RPGClassics). Set to none because it is Star element. Changed to Light element in the SE version (Wikipedia).

starocean-meteorswarm.desc: Attacks all enemies by dropping huge meteors. One of the strongest Star-element symbols.
starocean-meteorswarm.note: Learned by: Celine (Cave of Trials) (PlayStation version; cross-checked against ui-nap and RPGClassics). It is not learned by leveling up; you obtain and learn it in the Cave of Trials (ui-nap, RPGClassics). Set to none because it is Star element.

starocean-tractorbeam.desc: Attacks enemies in range by reversing gravity. A Star-element symbol.
starocean-tractorbeam.note: Learned by: Rena (Lv36) (PlayStation version; cross-checked against ui-nap and RPGClassics). Set to none because it is Star element. Changed to Earth element in the SE version (Wikipedia). Only Star Ocean Wiki says it does not work on flying enemies.

starocean-firebolt.desc: Attacks one enemy with a fireball.
starocean-firebolt.note: Learned by: Celine (starting) (PlayStation version; cross-checked against ui-nap and RPGClassics).

starocean-eruption.desc: Attacks enemies in range by spouting lava.
starocean-eruption.note: Learned by: Celine (Lv34) (PlayStation version; cross-checked against ui-nap and RPGClassics). Sources differ on the target (ui-nap says multiple, RPGClassics says all enemies, AppMedia for the SE version says enemy area).

starocean-explode.desc: Attacks all enemies with a huge explosion.
starocean-explode.note: Learned by: Celine (Lv66) (PlayStation version; cross-checked against ui-nap and RPGClassics).

starocean-thunderbolt.desc: Attacks one enemy by dropping lightning.
starocean-thunderbolt.note: Learned by: Celine (starting) (PlayStation version; cross-checked against ui-nap and RPGClassics). In the SE version the Lightning element was merged into Wind (Wikipedia).

starocean-thunderstorm.note: Learned by: Celine (Lv31) (PlayStation version; cross-checked against ui-nap and RPGClassics). Wind element in the SE version (Wikipedia).

starocean-thundercloud.desc: Attacks all enemies by raining lightning from a thundercloud.
starocean-thundercloud.note: Learned by: Celine (Lv55) (PlayStation version; cross-checked against ui-nap and RPGClassics). Wind element in the SE version (Wikipedia).

starocean-windblade.desc: Attacks one enemy with a blade of wind.
starocean-windblade.note: Learned by: Celine (starting), Noel (starting) (PlayStation version; cross-checked against ui-nap and RPGClassics).

starocean-sonicsaber.desc: Fires wind energy in a straight line, hitting enemies along it.
starocean-sonicsaber.note: Learned by: Noel (starting) (PlayStation version; cross-checked against ui-nap and RPGClassics). Noel-only in the PlayStation version. In the SE version Noel no longer learns it (Wikipedia).

starocean-magnumtornado.desc: Attacks enemies in range with a giant tornado.
starocean-magnumtornado.note: Learned by: Noel (starting) (PlayStation version; cross-checked against ui-nap and RPGClassics).

starocean-foehn.desc: Attacks all enemies with a hot wind.
starocean-foehn.note: Learned by: Noel (Lv52) (PlayStation version; cross-checked against ui-nap and RPGClassics).

starocean-grave.desc: Attacks one enemy with blades thrust up from the ground. It does not hit flying enemies.
starocean-grave.note: Learned by: Noel (starting) (PlayStation version; cross-checked against ui-nap and RPGClassics). Only RPGClassics says it does not hit flying enemies.

starocean-earthgrave.desc: Attacks all grounded enemies with rock spears thrust up from the ground.
starocean-earthgrave.note: Learned by: Noel (starting) (PlayStation version; cross-checked against ui-nap and RPGClassics). Only RPGClassics says it does not hit flying enemies.

starocean-earthquake.desc: Attacks all grounded enemies by shaking the earth.
starocean-earthquake.note: Learned by: Noel (Lv82) (PlayStation version; cross-checked against ui-nap and RPGClassics). Only RPGClassics says it does not hit flying enemies. Renamed "Rokkurein" in the SE version (Wikipedia).

starocean-iceneedle.desc: Attacks one enemy with flying icicles.
starocean-iceneedle.note: Learned by: Leon (starting) (PlayStation version; cross-checked against ui-nap and RPGClassics). The in-game element is Water (Jikū no Tō, ui-nap). It is set to ice because it is an ice symbol.

starocean-deepfreeze.desc: Attacks an enemy and the enemies around it by dropping hail.
starocean-deepfreeze.note: Learned by: Leon (starting) (PlayStation version; cross-checked against ui-nap and RPGClassics). The in-game element is Water (Jikū no Tō, ui-nap). It is set to ice because it is an ice symbol.

starocean-noah.desc: Sweeps away all enemies with a great flood.
starocean-noah.note: Learned by: Leon (Lv54) (PlayStation version; cross-checked against ui-nap and RPGClassics).

starocean-wounds.desc: Wounds one enemy with the power of darkness.
starocean-wounds.note: Learned by: Leon (starting) (PlayStation version; cross-checked against ui-nap and RPGClassics).

starocean-shadowbolt.desc: Attacks one enemy with a bolt of darkness.
starocean-shadowbolt.note: Learned by: Leon (starting) (PlayStation version; cross-checked against ui-nap and RPGClassics).

starocean-blacksaber.desc: Fires the power of darkness in a straight line, hitting enemies along it.
starocean-blacksaber.note: Learned by: Leon (starting) (PlayStation version; cross-checked against ui-nap and RPGClassics). On the target, ui-nap says "multiple", RPGClassics says "enemies on a line toward one enemy", and AppMedia (SE version) says "enemy line".

starocean-shadowflare.desc: Attacks all enemies by bursting a mass of darkness.
starocean-shadowflare.note: Learned by: Leon (Lv39) (PlayStation version; cross-checked against ui-nap and RPGClassics).

starocean-tetanuswind.desc: Attacks one enemy repeatedly with a poison-laced wind.
starocean-tetanuswind.note: Learned by: Noel (starting) (PlayStation version; cross-checked against ui-nap and RPGClassics). The Darkness element follows ui-nap and RPGClassics. Jikū no Tō places it in the Wind group of its interference table (interference unconfirmed). The poison side effect is from ui-nap only.

starocean-press.desc: Crushes one enemy with heavy force. The entry-level symbol of the Press line.
starocean-press.note: Learned by: Rena (Lv5) (PlayStation version; cross-checked against ui-nap and RPGClassics). Non-elemental (Jikū no Tō, RPGClassics). Earth element in the SE version (Wikipedia). Only RPGClassics says it occasionally finishes off an enemy.

starocean-gravitypress.desc: Crushes enemies in range with gravity. The upper tier of the Press line.
starocean-gravitypress.note: Learned by: Rena (Lv28) (PlayStation version; cross-checked against ui-nap and RPGClassics). Non-elemental. The spelling follows Jikū no Tō and AppMedia (SE version). ui-nap writes "Gurabidipuresu". That it belongs to the same line as Puresu comes from Wikipedia's description of "Non-elemental Press line".

starocean-gremlinlair.desc: Summons gremlins to attack all enemies.
starocean-gremlinlair.note: Learned by: Leon (Lv60) (PlayStation version; cross-checked against ui-nap and RPGClassics). Non-elemental (Jikū no Tō, RPGClassics). The spelling follows Jikū no Tō and AppMedia (SE version). ui-nap writes "Gureimurinrea".

starocean-demonsgate.desc: Opens a gate to the demon world and attacks all enemies with demonic power.
starocean-demonsgate.note: Learned by: Leon (Lv66) (PlayStation version; cross-checked against ui-nap and RPGClassics). Non-elemental (Jikū no Tō, RPGClassics). Darkness element in the SE version (Star Ocean Wiki).

starocean-extinction.desc: Attacks all enemies with intense energy. Leon's strongest symbol.
starocean-extinction.note: Learned by: Leon (Cave of Trials) (PlayStation version; cross-checked against ui-nap and RPGClassics). It is not learned by leveling up; you obtain and learn it in the Cave of Trials. MP cost is 90 in both PlayStation sources, ui-nap and RPGClassics (AppMedia for the SE version says 65). Non-elemental (Jikū no Tō, RPGClassics).

starocean-energyarrow.desc: Attacks one enemy with an arrow of energy.
starocean-energyarrow.note: Learned by: Celine (Lv12), Noel (starting) (PlayStation version; cross-checked against ui-nap and RPGClassics). Set to none because it is Negative element (Jikū no Tō, ui-nap).

wildarms-shield.desc: Raises one ally's defense. Can be stacked.
wildarms-shield.note: White Magic (low tier) made by writing "Jio × Jio" on the Crest Graph (the Crest combination is confirmed in only one source, RRPG).

wildarms-suction.desc: Puts a state on one ally that absorbs enemy magic they receive and turns it into MP.
wildarms-suction.note: White Magic (low tier) made by writing "Jio × Furei" on the Crest Graph (the Crest combination is confirmed in only one source, RRPG). Some sources (Kōryaku-dō, Kōryaku 1) say the effect lasts only once.

wildarms-hide.desc: Makes one ally invisible so they can dodge normal attacks.
wildarms-hide.note: White Magic (low tier) made by writing "Jio × Uingu" on the Crest Graph (the Crest combination is confirmed in only one source, RRPG). It wears off when the ally attacks, and that attack is always a critical hit (RRPG, Kōryaku 1).

wildarms-protect.desc: Raises one ally's resistance to magic. Can be stacked.
wildarms-protect.note: White Magic (low tier) made by writing "Jio × Myūzu" on the Crest Graph (the Crest combination is confirmed in only one source, RRPG).

wildarms-curse.desc: Makes enemy encounters more likely for a while.
wildarms-curse.note: White Magic (low tier) made by writing "Furei × Jio" on the Crest Graph (the Crest combination is confirmed in only one source, RRPG).

wildarms-lightweapon.desc: Gives one ally's weapon the Light element.
wildarms-lightweapon.note: White Magic (low tier) made by writing "Furei × Furei" on the Crest Graph (the Crest combination is confirmed in only one source, RRPG). Kōryaku 1 writes it as "Raitoueponn".

wildarms-mightbody.desc: Raises one ally's stats every turn, but that character can no longer choose actions.
wildarms-mightbody.note: White Magic (low tier) made by writing "Furei × Uingu" on the Crest Graph (the Crest combination is confirmed in only one source, RRPG). One source (RRPG) says it also grants automatic HP and MP recovery. The top-tier spell Sūpāmaitobodi is the powered-up version.

wildarms-darkweapon.desc: Gives one ally's weapon the Darkness element.
wildarms-darkweapon.note: White Magic (low tier) made by writing "Furei × Myūzu" on the Crest Graph (the Crest combination is confirmed in only one source, RRPG). Kōryaku 1 writes it as "Dākuueponn".

wildarms-reflect.desc: Puts up a barrier on one ally that reflects enemy magic.
wildarms-reflect.note: White Magic (low tier) made by writing "Uingu × Jio" on the Crest Graph (the Crest combination is confirmed in only one source, RRPG). The high-tier Hai Rifurekuto is the all-allies version. Sources differ: one says it reflects only once (Kōryaku-dō, Kōryaku 1), another says it lasts 2 turns (RRPG).

wildarms-escape.desc: Returns to the entrance of the dungeon you are in.
wildarms-escape.note: White Magic (low tier) made by writing "Uingu × Furei" on the Crest Graph (the Crest combination is confirmed in only one source, RRPG).

wildarms-quick.desc: Raises one ally's reaction (speed). Can be stacked.
wildarms-quick.note: White Magic (low tier) made by writing "Uingu × Uingu" on the Crest Graph (the Crest combination is confirmed in only one source, RRPG).

wildarms-airscreen.note: White Magic (low tier) made by writing "Uingu × Myūzu" on the Crest Graph (the Crest combination is confirmed in only one source, RRPG). The top-tier spell Hai Easukurīn is the all-allies version.

wildarms-revive.desc: Brings one ally back from knockout and restores HP.
wildarms-revive.note: White Magic (low tier) made by writing "Myūzu × Jio" on the Crest Graph (the Crest combination is confirmed in only one source, RRPG). The high-tier Hai Rivaibu is the upper version of the same combination and fully restores HP.

wildarms-morningcall.desc: Wakes a sleeping ally and keeps them from falling asleep afterward.
wildarms-morningcall.note: White Magic (low tier) made by writing "Myūzu × Furei" on the Crest Graph (the Crest combination is confirmed in only one source, RRPG). The target is one ally in Kōryaku-dō and Kōryaku 1, but all allies in RRPG. Single target is used here.

wildarms-field.desc: Puts up a barrier that reduces damage of one randomly chosen element.
wildarms-field.note: White Magic (low tier) made by writing "Myūzu × Uingu" on the Crest Graph (the Crest combination is confirmed in only one source, RRPG). The target is one ally in Kōryaku-dō and Kōryaku 1, but all allies in RRPG. Single target is used here.

wildarms-heal.note: White Magic (low tier) made by writing "Myūzu × Myūzu" on the Crest Graph (the Crest combination is confirmed in only one source, RRPG). It is already written on the Crest Graph from the start of the game (along with Fureimu). The high-tier Hai Hīru is the upper version of the same combination.

wildarms-hishield.desc: Raises the defense of all allies. Can be stacked.
wildarms-hishield.note: White Magic (high tier) made by writing "Jio × Jio" on the Crest Graph (the Crest combination is confirmed in only one source, RRPG). The high-tier version of Shīrudo. High-tier spells can be made after reaching the outer sea and talking to the mage of the stray guild.

wildarms-hyper.desc: Doubles attack power for a few turns.
wildarms-hyper.note: White Magic (high tier) made by writing "Jio × Furei" on the Crest Graph (the Crest combination is confirmed in only one source, RRPG). The target is one ally in RRPG and Kōryaku-dō, but all allies in Kōryaku 1. Single target is used here. One source (Kōryaku 1) says it also affects Jack's quick-draw attack.

wildarms-invisible.desc: Makes enemy encounters less likely for a while.
wildarms-invisible.note: White Magic (high tier) made by writing "Jio × Uingu" on the Crest Graph (the Crest combination is confirmed in only one source, RRPG).

wildarms-lifeguard.desc: Puts a state on one ally that revives them automatically once if they are knocked out.
wildarms-lifeguard.note: White Magic (high tier) made by writing "Jio × Myūzu" on the Crest Graph (the Crest combination is confirmed in only one source, RRPG).

wildarms-counterup.desc: Raises one ally's chance of countering.
wildarms-counterup.note: White Magic (high tier) made by writing "Furei × Jio" on the Crest Graph (the Crest combination is confirmed in only one source, RRPG). The top-tier spell Kauntāappu Purasu is the all-allies version.

wildarms-suicidalbomb.desc: Makes one ally always retaliate with an explosion the next time they take a normal attack.
wildarms-suicidalbomb.note: White Magic (high tier) made by writing "Furei × Furei" on the Crest Graph (the Crest combination is confirmed in only one source, RRPG). Kōryaku-dō writes it as "Sūsarudarubomu" (treated as a misprint; the spelling in RRPG and Kōryaku 1 is used).

wildarms-soulsurvive.desc: Protects one ally from instant-death attacks.
wildarms-soulsurvive.note: White Magic (high tier) made by writing "Furei × Uingu" on the Crest Graph (the Crest combination is confirmed in only one source, RRPG). The top-tier spell Sourusabaibu Purasu is the all-allies version.

wildarms-antimagic.desc: Creates a field in which everyone, allies and enemies alike, cannot use magic.
wildarms-antimagic.note: White Magic (high tier) made by writing "Furei × Myūzu" on the Crest Graph (the Crest combination is confirmed in only one source, RRPG).

wildarms-hireflect.desc: Puts up a barrier on all allies that reflects enemy magic.
wildarms-hireflect.note: White Magic (high tier) made by writing "Uingu × Jio" on the Crest Graph (the Crest combination is confirmed in only one source, RRPG). The high-tier version of Rifurekuto (all allies).

wildarms-dummydoll.desc: Creates a doll that takes the place of one ally and absorbs attacks.
wildarms-dummydoll.note: White Magic (high tier) made by writing "Uingu × Furei" on the Crest Graph (the Crest combination is confirmed in only one source, RRPG).

wildarms-teleport.desc: Instantly moves to a town you have visited before.
wildarms-teleport.note: White Magic (high tier) made by writing "Uingu × Uingu" on the Crest Graph (the Crest combination is confirmed in only one source, RRPG). One source (Kōryaku 1) says it can be used only in the field.

wildarms-statuslock.desc: Keeps all allies from suffering status ailments for a few turns.
wildarms-statuslock.note: White Magic (high tier) made by writing "Uingu × Myūzu" on the Crest Graph (the Crest combination is confirmed in only one source, RRPG).

wildarms-hirevive.desc: Brings one ally back from knockout and fully restores HP.
wildarms-hirevive.note: White Magic (high tier) made by writing "Myūzu × Jio" on the Crest Graph (the Crest combination is confirmed in only one source, RRPG). The high-tier version of Rivaibu.

wildarms-healplus.note: White Magic (high tier) made by writing "Myūzu × Furei" on the Crest Graph (the Crest combination is confirmed in only one source, RRPG). Kōryaku 1 writes it as "Hīrupurasu".

wildarms-restore.desc: Cures all of one ally's status ailments.
wildarms-restore.note: White Magic (high tier) made by writing "Myūzu × Uingu" on the Crest Graph (the Crest combination is confirmed in only one source, RRPG). The top-tier spell Resutoa Purasu is the all-allies version.

wildarms-hiheal.note: White Magic (high tier) made by writing "Myūzu × Myūzu" on the Crest Graph (the Crest combination is confirmed in only one source, RRPG). The high-tier version of Hīru.

wildarms-break.desc: Attacks one enemy with the power of Earth.
wildarms-break.note: Black Magic (low tier) made by writing "Jio × Jio" on the Crest Graph (the Crest combination is confirmed in only one source, RRPG). It grows stronger through the high-tier Hai Bureiku to the top-tier Mega Bureiku.

wildarms-slowdown.desc: Lowers the reaction (speed) of one enemy group. Can be stacked.
wildarms-slowdown.note: Black Magic (low tier) made by writing "Jio × Furei" on the Crest Graph (the Crest combination is confirmed in only one source, RRPG).

wildarms-sleep.desc: Puts one enemy group to sleep.
wildarms-sleep.note: Black Magic (low tier) made by writing "Jio × Uingu" on the Crest Graph (the Crest combination is confirmed in only one source, RRPG).

wildarms-armordown.desc: Lowers the defense of one enemy group. Can be stacked.
wildarms-armordown.note: Black Magic (low tier) made by writing "Jio × Myūzu" on the Crest Graph (the Crest combination is confirmed in only one source, RRPG).

wildarms-flash.desc: Lights up all enemies so they cannot dodge attacks.
wildarms-flash.note: Black Magic (low tier) made by writing "Furei × Jio" on the Crest Graph (the Crest combination is confirmed in only one source, RRPG). It inflicts this game's status ailment "Furasshu" (the target can no longer evade).

wildarms-flame.desc: Attacks one enemy with the power of Fire.
wildarms-flame.note: Black Magic (low tier) made by writing "Furei × Furei" on the Crest Graph (the Crest combination is confirmed in only one source, RRPG). It is already written on the Crest Graph from the start of the game. It grows stronger through the high-tier Hai Fureimu to the top-tier Mega Fureimu.

wildarms-confusion.note: Black Magic (low tier) made by writing "Furei × Uingu" on the Crest Graph (the Crest combination is confirmed in only one source, RRPG). Kōryaku 1 writes it as "Konhyūjon". The top-tier spell Hai Konfyūjon is the all-enemies version.

wildarms-blast.desc: Attacks one enemy group with non-elemental power.
wildarms-blast.note: Black Magic (low tier) made by writing "Furei × Myūzu" on the Crest Graph (the Crest combination is confirmed in only one source, RRPG). The high-tier Hai Burasuto is the all-enemies version. RRPG gives no power figure; Kōryaku-dō says SOR×3 and Kōryaku 1 says SOR×2.

wildarms-valkyrie.desc: Unleashes 8 non-elemental attacks on randomly chosen enemies.
wildarms-valkyrie.note: Black Magic (low tier) made by writing "Uingu × Jio" on the Crest Graph (the Crest combination is confirmed in only one source, RRPG).

wildarms-magicseal.desc: Seals the magic of one enemy group.
wildarms-magicseal.note: Black Magic (low tier) made by writing "Uingu × Furei" on the Crest Graph (the Crest combination is confirmed in only one source, RRPG). The top-tier spell Hai Majikkushīru is the all-enemies version.

wildarms-voltec.desc: Attacks one enemy with the power of Wind.
wildarms-voltec.note: Black Magic (low tier) made by writing "Uingu × Uingu" on the Crest Graph (the Crest combination is confirmed in only one source, RRPG). It grows stronger through the high-tier Hai Vorutekku to the top-tier Mega Vorutekku.

wildarms-spark.desc: Attacks one enemy group with the power of Lightning.
wildarms-spark.note: Black Magic (low tier) made by writing "Uingu × Myūzu" on the Crest Graph (the Crest combination is confirmed in only one source, RRPG). The high-tier Hai Supāku is the all-enemies version.

wildarms-analyze.desc: Examines one enemy's level, HP, MP, weaknesses and more.
wildarms-analyze.note: Black Magic (low tier) made by writing "Myūzu × Jio" on the Crest Graph (the Crest combination is confirmed in only one source, RRPG). It does not work on bosses (RRPG, Kōryaku 1).

wildarms-dispel.desc: Removes the effects of support magic on one enemy.
wildarms-dispel.note: Black Magic (low tier) made by writing "Myūzu × Furei" on the Crest Graph (the Crest combination is confirmed in only one source, RRPG). The top-tier spell Hai Disuperu is the all-enemies version.

wildarms-prison.desc: Traps one enemy in a barrier so it cannot move. The barrier shatters, along with the enemy, when attacked.
wildarms-prison.note: Black Magic (low tier) made by writing "Myūzu × Uingu" on the Crest Graph (the Crest combination is confirmed in only one source, RRPG). The high-tier Hai Purizun is the group version.

wildarms-freeze.desc: Attacks one enemy with the power of Water.
wildarms-freeze.note: Black Magic (low tier) made by writing "Myūzu × Myūzu" on the Crest Graph (the Crest combination is confirmed in only one source, RRPG). The name means "freeze", but the element is Water (in all three sources). It grows stronger through the high-tier Hai Furīzu to the top-tier Mega Furīzu.

wildarms-hibreak.desc: Attacks one enemy group with the power of Earth.
wildarms-hibreak.note: Black Magic (high tier) made by writing "Jio × Jio" on the Crest Graph (the Crest combination is confirmed in only one source, RRPG). The high-tier version of Bureiku.

wildarms-eraser.desc: Erases all of an enemy's elemental resistances and weaknesses.
wildarms-eraser.note: Black Magic (high tier) made by writing "Jio × Furei" on the Crest Graph (the Crest combination is confirmed in only one source, RRPG). The target is all enemies in Kōryaku-dō and Kōryaku 1, but one enemy in RRPG. All enemies is used here.

wildarms-lifedrain.desc: Drains HP from one enemy group.
wildarms-lifedrain.note: Black Magic (high tier) made by writing "Jio × Uingu" on the Crest Graph (the Crest combination is confirmed in only one source, RRPG).

wildarms-saint.desc: Attacks one enemy with powerful Light-element force.
wildarms-saint.note: Black Magic (high tier) made by writing "Jio × Myūzu" on the Crest Graph (the Crest combination is confirmed in only one source, RRPG). The top-tier spell Hai Seinto is the powered-up all-enemies version.

wildarms-rainbow.desc: Attacks one enemy with the combined power of all elements.
wildarms-rainbow.note: Black Magic (high tier) made by writing "Furei × Jio" on the Crest Graph (the Crest combination is confirmed in only one source, RRPG). An all-element attack (set to none because it is not among the site's shared elements). The top-tier spell Hai Reinbou is the powered-up all-enemies version.

wildarms-hiflame.desc: Attacks one enemy group with the power of Fire.
wildarms-hiflame.note: Black Magic (high tier) made by writing "Furei × Furei" on the Crest Graph (the Crest combination is confirmed in only one source, RRPG). The high-tier version of Fureimu.

wildarms-darkness.desc: Attacks one enemy with powerful Darkness-element force.
wildarms-darkness.note: Black Magic (high tier) made by writing "Furei × Uingu" on the Crest Graph (the Crest combination is confirmed in only one source, RRPG). The top-tier spell Hai Dākunesu is the powered-up all-enemies version.

wildarms-hiblast.desc: Attacks all enemies with non-elemental power.
wildarms-hiblast.note: Black Magic (high tier) made by writing "Furei × Myūzu" on the Crest Graph (the Crest combination is confirmed in only one source, RRPG). The high-tier version of Burasuto.

wildarms-magicdrain.note: Black Magic (high tier) made by writing "Uingu × Jio" on the Crest Graph (the Crest combination is confirmed in only one source, RRPG).

wildarms-luckyshoot.desc: Attacks one enemy. If this spell delivers the finishing blow, the enemy always drops an item.
wildarms-luckyshoot.note: Black Magic (high tier) made by writing "Uingu × Furei" on the Crest Graph (the Crest combination is confirmed in only one source, RRPG). The top-tier spell Chō Rakkīshūto is the powered-up all-enemies version.

wildarms-hivoltec.desc: Attacks one enemy group with the power of Wind.
wildarms-hivoltec.note: Black Magic (high tier) made by writing "Uingu × Uingu" on the Crest Graph (the Crest combination is confirmed in only one source, RRPG). The high-tier version of Vorutekku.

wildarms-hispark.desc: Attacks all enemies with the power of Lightning.
wildarms-hispark.note: Black Magic (high tier) made by writing "Uingu × Myūzu" on the Crest Graph (the Crest combination is confirmed in only one source, RRPG). The high-tier version of Supāku.

wildarms-punish.desc: Shrinks one enemy, reducing its HP and stats to one quarter.
wildarms-punish.note: Black Magic (high tier) made by writing "Myūzu × Jio" on the Crest Graph (the Crest combination is confirmed in only one source, RRPG). The top-tier spell Hai Panisshu is the all-enemies version.

wildarms-randomizer.desc: Some random spell takes effect, depending on luck. A top-tier spell may come out, or allies may be afflicted with status ailments.
wildarms-randomizer.note: Black Magic (high tier) made by writing "Myūzu × Furei" on the Crest Graph (the Crest combination is confirmed in only one source, RRPG). The higher the luck, the more likely a high-ranking result (RRPG). Top-tier magic can be used only through this or Mystic.

wildarms-hiprison.desc: Traps one enemy group in a barrier so they cannot move.
wildarms-hiprison.note: Black Magic (high tier) made by writing "Myūzu × Uingu" on the Crest Graph (the Crest combination is confirmed in only one source, RRPG). The high-tier version of Purizun.

wildarms-hifreeze.desc: Attacks one enemy group with the power of Water.
wildarms-hifreeze.note: Black Magic (high tier) made by writing "Myūzu × Myūzu" on the Crest Graph (the Crest combination is confirmed in only one source, RRPG). The high-tier version of Furīzu.

wildarms-hihealplus.desc: Fully restores the HP of all allies.
wildarms-hihealplus.note: Top-tier magic (called "special high-tier magic" in Kōryaku 1). It cannot be made on the Crest Graph; it happens only by chance from Randamaizā, or when certain equipment is used through Mystic. No MP cost is listed. The all-allies version of Hai Hīru. Kōryaku 1 writes it as "Hai Hīrupurasu".

wildarms-restoreplus.desc: Cures all status ailments of all allies.
wildarms-restoreplus.note: Top-tier magic (called "special high-tier magic" in Kōryaku 1). It cannot be made on the Crest Graph; it happens only by chance from Randamaizā, or when certain equipment is used through Mystic. No MP cost is listed. The all-allies version of Resutoa. It occurs through the Mystic of Terasu Tiara.

wildarms-regeneration.desc: Brings all knocked-out allies back to their feet.
wildarms-regeneration.note: Top-tier magic (called "special high-tier magic" in Kōryaku 1). It cannot be made on the Crest Graph; it happens only by chance from Randamaizā, or when certain equipment is used through Mystic. No MP cost is listed. It occurs through the Mystic of Ōtokuchūru. Its effect corresponds to an all-allies version of Rivaibu, but the sources do not describe any ranking, so it was placed in the Rivaibu line based on the matching effect.

wildarms-hyperplus.desc: Doubles the attack power of all allies.
wildarms-hyperplus.note: Top-tier magic (called "special high-tier magic" in Kōryaku 1). It cannot be made on the Crest Graph; it happens only by chance from Randamaizā, or when certain equipment is used through Mystic. No MP cost is listed. The all-allies version of Haipā.

wildarms-hiairscreen.desc: Raises the evasion of all allies.
wildarms-hiairscreen.note: Top-tier magic (called "special high-tier magic" in Kōryaku 1). It cannot be made on the Crest Graph; it happens only by chance from Randamaizā, or when certain equipment is used through Mystic. No MP cost is listed. The all-allies version of Easukurīn.

wildarms-counterupplus.desc: Raises all allies' chance of countering.
wildarms-counterupplus.note: Top-tier magic (called "special high-tier magic" in Kōryaku 1). It cannot be made on the Crest Graph; it happens only by chance from Randamaizā, or when certain equipment is used through Mystic. No MP cost is listed. The all-allies version of Kauntāappu.

wildarms-soulsurviveplus.desc: Protects all allies from instant-death attacks.
wildarms-soulsurviveplus.note: Top-tier magic (called "special high-tier magic" in Kōryaku 1). It cannot be made on the Crest Graph; it happens only by chance from Randamaizā, or when certain equipment is used through Mystic. No MP cost is listed. The all-allies version of Sourusabaibu. It occurs through the Mystic of Purinsesu Rotto.

wildarms-supermightbody.desc: Gives all allies the effect of Maitobodi.
wildarms-supermightbody.note: Top-tier magic (called "special high-tier magic" in Kōryaku 1). octopath-hi-no-rune.desc: For 3 turns, adds a Fire follow-up to the user's weapon attacks.
octopath-hi-no-rune.note: Only one Rune can be active at a time (Gamer Guides). The English release uses a different name. The reading could not be confirmed in sources.

octopath-kori-no-rune.desc: For 3 turns, adds an Ice follow-up to the user's weapon attacks.
octopath-kori-no-rune.note: Only one Rune can be active at a time (Gamer Guides). The English release uses a different name. The reading could not be confirmed in sources.

octopath-kaminari-no-rune.desc: For 3 turns, adds a Lightning follow-up to the user's weapon attacks.
octopath-kaminari-no-rune.note: Only one Rune can be active at a time (Gamer Guides). The English release uses a different name. The reading could not be confirmed in sources.

octopath-kaze-no-rune.desc: For 3 turns, adds a Wind follow-up to the user's weapon attacks.
octopath-kaze-no-rune.note: Only one Rune can be active at a time (Gamer Guides). The English release uses a different name. The reading could not be confirmed in sources.

octopath-hikari-no-rune.desc: For 3 turns, adds a Light follow-up to the user's weapon attacks.
octopath-hikari-no-rune.note: Only one Rune can be active at a time (Gamer Guides). The English release uses a different name. The reading could not be confirmed in sources.

octopath-yami-no-rune.desc: For 3 turns, adds a Darkness follow-up to the user's weapon attacks.
octopath-yami-no-rune.note: Only one Rune can be active at a time (Gamer Guides). The English release uses a different name. The reading could not be confirmed in sources.

octopath-kakusan-no-rune.desc: For 3 turns, makes skills that affect only the user affect all allies.
octopath-kakusan-no-rune.note: The English release uses a different name.

octopath-balogar.desc: Attacks one enemy in succession with six elements: Fire, Ice, Lightning, Wind, Light and Darkness.
octopath-balogar.note: EX Skill (learned after learning all 7 other abilities of the job; usable only at maximum Boost). Because it uses all six elements, it is set to none among the site's shared elements. The English release uses a different name.

octopath-ryusei.desc: Attacks all enemies in succession with three elements: Wind, Light and Darkness.
octopath-ryusei.note: The elements hit in the order Wind, Light, Darkness (Gamer Guides). Because it uses three elements, it is set to none among the site's shared elements. The English release uses a different name.

octopath-bp-boost-no-meguri.desc: For 2 turns, increases one ally's BP by 2 each turn.
octopath-bp-boost-no-meguri.note: Gamer Guides says "SP increases by 2", but BP is used here to match Kamige Kōryaku, Game Ranbu and the name. The English release uses a different name.

octopath-kaishin-no-meguri.desc: For 2 turns, raises one ally's critical hit rate.
octopath-kaishin-no-meguri.note: The English release uses a different name.

octopath-hoshiyomi-no-uta.desc: For 2 turns, raises one ally's physical defense, elemental defense, action speed and evasion all at once.
octopath-hoshiyomi-no-uta.note: The spelling varies: Kamige Kōryaku writes 星詠みの唄 in its list and 星詠みの歌 in its learning order, while Game Ranbu writes 星読みの唄 in its table and 星詠みの唄 in its heading. 星詠みの唄, which appears in both sources, is used. The English release uses a different name.

octopath-uchikeshi-no-meguri.desc: For 2 turns, keeps one enemy from being buffed, or keeps one ally from being debuffed.
octopath-uchikeshi-no-meguri.note: You can choose whether to use it on an enemy or an ally. The English release uses a different name.

octopath-keizoku-kaifuku-mahou.desc: For 2 turns, restores a little HP to all allies each turn.
octopath-keizoku-kaifuku-mahou.note: The English release uses a different name.

octopath-okaeshi-no-meguri.desc: Puts one ally in a stance to counter one physical attack.
octopath-okaeshi-no-meguri.note: Game Ranbu says "reflects one physical attack", while Kamige Kōryaku and Gamer Guides say "counters one instance of physical damage". The English release uses a different name.

octopath-steorra.desc: Attacks all enemies with Non-elemental power. The more BP your allies have, the greater the power.
octopath-steorra.note: EX Skill (learned after learning all 7 other abilities of the job; usable only at maximum Boost). Kamige Kōryaku writes 占星師ステオーラの予言, but 星占師, as in Game Ranbu's table and the boss name (星占師ステオーラ), is used. The English release uses a different name.

xenogears-shidan.desc: Fires a ball of ki, dealing Non-elemental damage to one enemy.
xenogears-shidan.note: Fei's kikō (ki technique). Usable from the start. The reading could not be confirmed in sources.

xenogears-naiyoukou.note: Fei's kikō. The reading could not be confirmed in sources.

xenogears-gouki.note: Fei's kikō. The reading could not be confirmed in sources.

xenogears-juuki.desc: From then on, the user counters enemy attacks.
xenogears-juuki.note: Fei's kikō. Sources word it differently, as "counters when it dodges" or "counters attacks". The reading could not be confirmed in sources.

xenogears-koukei.desc: Greatly raises the user's defense at the cost of lower attack power.
xenogears-koukei.note: Fei's kikō. It is a separate technique from Citan's 光香, which has the same effect. It is also unrelated to the deathblow 超武技光勁. The reading could not be confirmed in sources.

xenogears-ankei.desc: Greatly raises the user's attack power at the cost of lower defense.
xenogears-ankei.note: Fei's kikō. It is a separate technique from Citan's 闇香, which has the same effect. It is also unrelated to the deathblow 超武技闇勁. The reading could not be confirmed in sources.

xenogears-senkou.desc: Gathers the ki of the universe and releases it in an explosion, dealing heavy Non-elemental damage to one enemy.
xenogears-senkou.note: Fei's kikō. The reading could not be confirmed in sources.

xenogears-ginga.desc: Deals Non-elemental damage to all enemies and also removes support effects on them.
xenogears-ginga.note: Fei's kikō. One source (EXCEED THE LIMIT!!) writes it as 銀河, but 銀牙 from the other three sources is used. The reading could not be confirmed in sources.

xenogears-rig-bolt.desc: Drops lightning, dealing Wind damage to one enemy.
xenogears-rig-bolt.note: Elly's ether. Learned from the start. The prefix "Rigu" indicates the Wind element, and within the same element they are learned in the order single target, area, all enemies. The effect looks like lightning, but the in-game element is Wind.

xenogears-rig-burn.desc: Strikes a section of the enemies with intense lightning, dealing Wind damage.
xenogears-rig-burn.note: Elly's ether. Learned at Lv20. The prefix "Rigu" indicates the Wind element, and within the same element they are learned in the order single target, area, all enemies. The range is "area" (the targeted enemy and those around it). The effect looks like lightning, but the in-game element is Wind.

xenogears-rig-wave.desc: Deals Wind damage to all enemies with an electric discharge.
xenogears-rig-wave.note: Elly's ether. Learned at Lv55. The prefix "Rigu" indicates the Wind element, and within the same element they are learned in the order single target, area, all enemies. The effect looks like lightning, but the in-game element is Wind.

xenogears-rud-lance.desc: Sends a wave of ether up from the ground, dealing Earth damage to one enemy.
xenogears-rud-lance.note: Elly's ether. Learned from the start. The prefix "Rudo" indicates the Earth element, and within the same element they are learned in the order single target, area, all enemies.

xenogears-rud-storm.desc: Rains down rocks, dealing Earth damage to a section of the enemies.
xenogears-rud-storm.note: Elly's ether. Learned at Lv20. The prefix "Rudo" indicates the Earth element, and within the same element they are learned in the order single target, area, all enemies. The range is "area" (the targeted enemy and those around it).

xenogears-rud-ghost.desc: Traps all enemies in rock, dealing Earth damage.
xenogears-rud-ghost.note: Elly's ether. Learned at Lv55. The prefix "Rudo" indicates the Earth element, and within the same element they are learned in the order single target, area, all enemies.

xenogears-era-cube.desc: Wraps one enemy in flames, dealing Fire damage.
xenogears-era-cube.note: Elly's ether. Learned from the start. The prefix "Era" indicates the Fire element, and within the same element they are learned in the order single target, area, all enemies.

xenogears-era-dragon.desc: Deals Fire damage to a section of the enemies with a high-temperature explosion.
xenogears-era-dragon.note: Elly's ether. Learned at Lv20. The prefix "Era" indicates the Fire element, and within the same element they are learned in the order single target, area, all enemies. The range is "area" (the targeted enemy and those around it).

xenogears-era-largo.desc: Deals Fire damage to all enemies with a huge explosion.
xenogears-era-largo.note: Elly's ether. Learned at Lv55. The prefix "Era" indicates the Fire element, and within the same element they are learned in the order single target, area, all enemies.

xenogears-rei-ice.desc: Freezes one enemy, dealing Water damage.
xenogears-rei-ice.note: Elly's ether. Learned from the start. The prefix "Rei" indicates the Water element, and within the same element they are learned in the order single target, area, all enemies. The effect looks like ice, but the in-game element is Water.

xenogears-rei-mist.desc: Freezes the surrounding space, dealing Water damage to a section of the enemies.
xenogears-rei-mist.note: Elly's ether. Learned at Lv20. The prefix "Rei" indicates the Water element, and within the same element they are learned in the order single target, area, all enemies. The range is "area" (the targeted enemy and those around it). The effect looks like ice, but the in-game element is Water.

xenogears-rei-road.desc: Drops a huge block of ice, dealing Water damage to all enemies.
xenogears-rei-road.note: Elly's ether. Learned at Lv55. The prefix "Rei" indicates the Water element, and within the same element they are learned in the order single target, area, all enemies. The effect looks like ice, but the in-game element is Water.

xenogears-sazanami.note: Citan's secret art. Usable from the start. The reading could not be confirmed in sources.

xenogears-renki.desc: Makes the next single-target secret art you use affect all targets, just once.
xenogears-renki.note: Citan's secret art. The reading could not be confirmed in sources.

xenogears-fuuseii.desc: Makes one ally resistant to Earth attacks.
xenogears-fuuseii.note: Citan's secret art. One source (Kyarakutā-betsu Shūtokuwaza to Shūtoku Tokugi!) says it instead makes the ally weak to Wind. The reading could not be confirmed in sources.

xenogears-chiseii.desc: Makes one ally resistant to Wind attacks.
xenogears-chiseii.note: Citan's secret art. One source (Kyarakutā-betsu Shūtokuwaza to Shūtoku Tokugi!) says it instead makes the ally weak to Earth. The reading could not be confirmed in sources.

xenogears-kaseii.desc: Makes one ally resistant to Water attacks.
xenogears-kaseii.note: Citan's secret art. One source (Kyarakutā-betsu Shūtokuwaza to Shūtoku Tokugi!) says it instead makes the ally weak to Fire. The reading could not be confirmed in sources.

xenogears-suiseii.desc: Makes one ally resistant to Fire attacks.
xenogears-suiseii.note: Citan's secret art. One source (Kyarakutā-betsu Shūtokuwaza to Shūtoku Tokugi!) says it instead makes the ally weak to Water. The reading could not be confirmed in sources.

xenogears-ryokushou.desc: Cures one ally's physical status ailments.
xenogears-ryokushou.note: Citan's secret art. It targets physical ailments such as poison, as well as stat drops. The reading could not be confirmed in sources.

xenogears-reishou.desc: Cures one ally's mental status ailments.
xenogears-reishou.note: Citan's secret art. It targets mental ailments such as confusion, sleep and silence. The reading could not be confirmed in sources.

xenogears-koukou.desc: Greatly raises defense at the cost of lower attack power.
xenogears-koukou.note: Citan's secret art. The target differs by source (one ally: Gēmu Nandemo Dētabēsu and Stateless Zone; self: EXCEED THE LIMIT!!). The reading could not be confirmed in sources.

xenogears-ankou.desc: Greatly raises attack power at the cost of lower defense.
xenogears-ankou.note: Citan's secret art. The target differs by source (one ally: Gēmu Nandemo Dētabēsu and Stateless Zone; self: EXCEED THE LIMIT!!). The reading could not be confirmed in sources.

xenogears-senkei.desc: Halves the time until one ally's next turn.
xenogears-senkei.note: Citan's secret art. The reading could not be confirmed in sources.

xenogears-wild-smile.note: Bart's ether. Usable from the start.

xenogears-gold-shot.desc: Fires a coin like a bullet, dealing Non-elemental damage to one enemy.

xenogears-white-glove.desc: Taunts the enemy to draw attacks to the user.
xenogears-white-glove.note: Bart's ether. The target differs by source (self: Stateless Zone; one enemy: Gēmu Nandemo Dētabēsu).

xenogears-blue-colon.desc: Raises the user's accuracy and evasion.

xenogears-white-colon.desc: From then on, the user counters enemy attacks.

xenogears-wind-mode.desc: Adds the Wind element to one ally's attacks.
xenogears-wind-mode.note: Bart's ether. The spelling differs by source: Wiindomōdo (Kyarakutā-betsu Shūtokuwaza to Shūtoku Tokugi!) and Uinguomōdo (Gēmu Nandemo Dētabēsu). "Uindomōdo" from Stateless Zone is used.

xenogears-earth-mode.desc: Adds the Earth element to one ally's attacks.

xenogears-fire-mode.desc: Adds the Fire element to one ally's attacks.

xenogears-water-mode.desc: Adds the Water element to one ally's attacks.

xenogears-hagane-no-kobushi.desc: Raises the user's attack power through fighting spirit.
xenogears-hagane-no-kobushi.note: Rico's fighting spirit (kiai). Usable from the start. The reading could not be confirmed in sources.

xenogears-hagane-no-nikutai.desc: Raises the user's defense through fighting spirit.
xenogears-hagane-no-nikutai.note: Rico's fighting spirit (kiai). Usable from the start. The reading could not be confirmed in sources.

xenogears-hagane-no-seishin.desc: Raises the user's ether defense through fighting spirit.
xenogears-hagane-no-seishin.note: Rico's fighting spirit (kiai). The reading could not be confirmed in sources.

xenogears-hagane-no-touki.desc: Fires a rapid series of spirit shots, dealing Non-elemental damage to one enemy.
xenogears-hagane-no-touki.note: Rico's fighting spirit (kiai). The reading could not be confirmed in sources.

xenogears-jouka-no-hikari.desc: Cures all of one ally's status ailments.
xenogears-jouka-no-hikari.note: Billy's ether. The reading could not be confirmed in sources.

xenogears-iyashi-no-hikari.note: Billy's ether. The reading could not be confirmed in sources.

xenogears-seinaru-hikari.note: Billy's ether. It could not be confirmed in sources whether it is the all-allies version of 癒しの光, so it is registered as a separate line. The reading could not be confirmed in sources.

xenogears-megami-no-yell.desc: Halves the time until one ally's next turn.
xenogears-megami-no-yell.note: Billy's ether. The reading could not be confirmed in sources.

xenogears-megami-no-manazashi.note: Billy's ether. The reading could not be confirmed in sources.

xenogears-kaze-no-tate.desc: Makes one ally resistant to Earth attacks.
xenogears-kaze-no-tate.note: Billy's ether. The reading could not be confirmed in sources.

xenogears-chi-no-tate.desc: Makes one ally resistant to Wind attacks.
xenogears-chi-no-tate.note: Billy's ether. The reading could not be confirmed in sources.

xenogears-hi-no-tate.desc: Makes one ally resistant to Water attacks.
xenogears-hi-no-tate.note: Billy's ether. The reading could not be confirmed in sources.

xenogears-mizu-no-tate.desc: Makes one ally resistant to Fire attacks.
xenogears-mizu-no-tate.note: Billy's ether. The reading could not be confirmed in sources.

xenogears-megami-no-kiai.desc: Revives one knocked-out ally with half their HP restored.
xenogears-megami-no-kiai.note: Billy's ether. The 50% HP figure is confirmed in only one source (Kyarakutā-betsu Shūtokuwaza to Shūtoku Tokugi!). The reading could not be confirmed in sources.

xenogears-robo-beam.desc: Fires a beam from Seibzehn's head, dealing Non-elemental damage to one enemy.
xenogears-robo-beam.note: Maria's gear commands (she orders Seibzehn to fight). The term "gear commands" (機操) is confirmed in only one source (Stateless Zone).

xenogears-robo-missile.desc: Fires a missile from Seibzehn's back, dealing Non-elemental damage to one enemy.

xenogears-graviton-hou.desc: Deals heavy Non-elemental damage to all enemies with Seibzehn's graviton beam.
xenogears-graviton-hou.note: Maria's gear commands. It is not learned by level; it becomes usable after the battle with Achtzehn. The reading could not be confirmed in sources.

xenogears-mori-no-odori.note: Chu-Chu's sorcery. Usable from the start. The reading could not be confirmed in sources.

xenogears-korun-no-inori.desc: Cures one ally's physical status ailments.
xenogears-korun-no-inori.note: Chu-Chu's sorcery. Like Citan's 緑掌, it targets physical ailments. The reading could not be confirmed in sources.

xenogears-murumu-no-inori.desc: Cures one ally's mental status ailments.
xenogears-murumu-no-inori.note: Chu-Chu's sorcery. Like Citan's 霊掌, it targets mental ailments. The reading could not be confirmed in sources.

xenogears-shinda-furi.desc: Plays dead so that enemies stop targeting the user.
xenogears-shinda-furi.note: Chu-Chu's sorcery. While it is active, only Defend and Items can be chosen. It cannot be used when the user is the only ally left. The reading could not be confirmed in sources.

xenogears-otome-no-kiss.note: Chu-Chu's sorcery. Stateless Zone writes it as 乙女キッス. The 30% HP on revival is confirmed in only one source (Kyarakutā-betsu Shūtokuwaza to Shūtoku Tokugi!). The reading could not be confirmed in sources.

xenogears-mori-no-kaze.desc: Throws a ball of compressed air, dealing Wind damage to one enemy.
xenogears-mori-no-kaze.note: Chu-Chu's sorcery. The reading could not be confirmed in sources.

xenogears-daichi-no-juunin.desc: Summons a demon that lives in the earth, dealing Earth damage to a section of the enemies.
xenogears-daichi-no-juunin.note: Chu-Chu's sorcery. The range is "area". The reading could not be confirmed in sources.

xenogears-taiko-no-shinpi.desc: Causes an explosion with ancient power, dealing Non-elemental damage to all enemies.
xenogears-taiko-no-shinpi.note: Chu-Chu's sorcery. The reading could not be confirmed in sources.

xenogears-rig-dahm.desc: Deals Wind damage to one enemy with a nanomachine electric shock.
xenogears-rig-dahm.note: Emeralda's ether (via nanomachines). Usable from the start. The prefix "Rigu" indicates the Wind element, named the same way as Elly's.

xenogears-rig-omega.desc: Turns space into plasma, dealing Wind damage to all enemies.
xenogears-rig-omega.note: Emeralda's ether (via nanomachines). Usable from the start. The prefix "Rigu" indicates the Wind element, named the same way as Elly's. The all-enemies version, learned at the same time as the single-target version.

xenogears-rud-fist.desc: Deals Earth damage to one enemy with a nanomachine cube.
xenogears-rud-fist.note: Emeralda's ether (via nanomachines). Usable from the start. The prefix "Rudo" indicates the Earth element, named the same way as Elly's.

xenogears-rud-horus.desc: Buries space itself in the ground, dealing Earth damage to all enemies.
xenogears-rud-horus.note: Emeralda's ether (via nanomachines). Usable from the start. The prefix "Rudo" indicates the Earth element, named the same way as Elly's. The all-enemies version, learned at the same time as the single-target version.

xenogears-era-gold.desc: Turns the enemy itself into flame, dealing Fire damage to one enemy.
xenogears-era-gold.note: Emeralda's ether (via nanomachines). Usable from the start. The prefix "Era" indicates the Fire element, named the same way as Elly's.

xenogears-era-gist.desc: Burns the air in a chain reaction, dealing Fire damage to all enemies.
xenogears-era-gist.note: Emeralda's ether (via nanomachines). Usable from the start. The prefix "Era" indicates the Fire element, named the same way as Elly's. The all-enemies version, learned at the same time as the single-target version.

xenogears-rei-aluom.desc: Turns the air into water and drops it, dealing Water damage to one enemy.
xenogears-rei-aluom.note: Emeralda's ether (via nanomachines). Usable from the start. The prefix "Rei" indicates the Water element, named the same way as Elly's.

xenogears-rei-dome.desc: Turns the ground into water and sends it surging up, dealing Water damage to all enemies.
xenogears-rei-dome.note: Emeralda's ether (via nanomachines). Usable from the start. The prefix "Rei" indicates the Water element, named the same way as Elly's. The all-enemies version, learned at the same time as the single-target version.

valkyrie-baan-sutoomu.desc: Attacks enemies with a fiery explosion and launches them into the air.
valkyrie-baan-sutoomu.note: 1 hit. Used from the battle command (the magic menu opened with the SELECT button), it targets all enemies. When set as an attack spell and used with the button attack, it is single-target (gcgx, Game Log, Aotama no Hoshiboshi). CT increases by 2 after use (Game Log, Aotama no Hoshiboshi and gcgx agree). In finishing moves it becomes a stronger version of the same spell (intermediate magic), and with a staff that can use grand magic equipped, it becomes the grand magic "Ifurīto Kyaresu" (grand magic is a finishing move, so it has no separate entry). The English release uses a different name. Initial learners: Jerādo, Nanami. The initial learners are confirmed in only one source, the per-character pages of gcgx.games.

valkyrie-faia-ransu.desc: Hurls two spears of fire at one enemy.
valkyrie-faia-ransu.note: 2 hits. CT increases by 3 after use (Game Log, Aotama no Hoshiboshi and gcgx agree). In finishing moves it becomes a stronger version of the same spell (intermediate magic), and with a staff that can use grand magic equipped, it becomes the grand magic "Karamiti Burasuto" (grand magic is a finishing move, so it has no separate entry). The English release uses a different name. Initial learners: Rorenta, Ganossa, Rezādo. The initial learners agree between gcgx.games and an English-language wiki. The English-language wiki also lists CT 3, 2 hits and Fire element.

valkyrie-kuuru-danseru.desc: Summons an ice spirit to attack one enemy, with a chance to freeze it.
valkyrie-kuuru-danseru.note: 3 hits; the added effect is freeze. CT increases by 5 after use (Game Log, Aotama no Hoshiboshi and gcgx agree). In finishing moves it becomes a stronger version of the same spell (intermediate magic), and with a staff that can use grand magic equipped, it becomes the grand magic "Abusoryūto Zero" (grand magic is a finishing move, so it has no separate entry). The English release uses a different name. Initial learners: 夢瑠. The initial learners are confirmed in only one source, the per-character pages of gcgx.games.

valkyrie-aishikuru-ejji.desc: Rains down sharp icicles to attack, with a chance to freeze.
valkyrie-aishikuru-ejji.note: 3 hits; the added effect is freeze. Used from the battle command (the magic menu opened with the SELECT button), it targets all enemies. When set as an attack spell and used with the button attack, it is single-target (gcgx, Game Log, Aotama no Hoshiboshi). CT increases by 5 after use (Game Log, Aotama no Hoshiboshi and gcgx agree). In finishing moves it becomes a stronger version of the same spell (intermediate magic), and with a staff that can use grand magic equipped, it becomes the grand magic "Deruta Sutoraiku" (grand magic is a finishing move, so it has no separate entry). The English release uses a different name. Initial learners: 夢瑠. The initial learners are confirmed in only one source, the per-character pages of gcgx.games.

valkyrie-raitoningu-boruto.note: 3 hits. Used from the battle command (the magic menu opened with the SELECT button), it targets all enemies. When set as an attack spell and used with the button attack, it is single-target (gcgx, Game Log, Aotama no Hoshiboshi). CT increases by 9 after use (Game Log, Aotama no Hoshiboshi and gcgx agree). In finishing moves it becomes a stronger version of the same spell (intermediate magic), and with a staff that can use grand magic equipped, it becomes the grand magic "Burūtisshu Boruto" (grand magic is a finishing move, so it has no separate entry). The English release uses a different name. Initial learners: Nanami. The initial learners are confirmed in only one source, the per-character pages of gcgx.games.

valkyrie-purizumikku-misairu.desc: Fires five shots of light, with a chance to inflict one of poison, freeze, paralysis, petrification or silence.
valkyrie-purizumikku-misairu.note: 5 hits; the added effects are poison, freeze, paralysis, petrification and silence. The element is Lightning in both Game Log and gcgx. CT increases by 10 after use (Game Log, Aotama no Hoshiboshi and gcgx agree). In finishing moves it becomes a stronger version of the same spell (intermediate magic), and with a staff that can use grand magic equipped, it becomes the grand magic "Gurabiti Buresu" (grand magic is a finishing move, so it has no separate entry). The English release uses a different name. Initial learners: Ganossa, Rezādo. The initial learners are confirmed in only one source, the per-character pages of gcgx.games.

valkyrie-kurosu-eareido.desc: Attacks by firing a holy cross.
valkyrie-kurosu-eareido.note: 4 hits. Used from the battle command (the magic menu opened with the SELECT button), it targets all enemies. When set as an attack spell and used with the button attack, it is single-target (gcgx, Game Log, Aotama no Hoshiboshi). CT increases by 6 after use (Game Log, Aotama no Hoshiboshi and gcgx agree). In finishing moves it becomes a stronger version of the same spell (intermediate magic), and with a staff that can use grand magic equipped, it becomes the grand magic "Seresutiaru Sutā" (grand magic is a finishing move, so it has no separate entry). The English release uses a different name. Initial learners: Rorenta, Merutīna, Riseria, Rezādo. The initial learners are confirmed in only one source, the per-character pages of gcgx.games.

valkyrie-igunito-jaberin.desc: Rains down spears of holy flame on one enemy.
valkyrie-igunito-jaberin.note: 5 hits. CT increases by 3 after use (Game Log, Aotama no Hoshiboshi and gcgx agree). In finishing moves it becomes a stronger version of the same spell (intermediate magic), and with a staff that can use grand magic equipped, it becomes the grand magic "Serafikku Rōsaito" (grand magic is a finishing move, so it has no separate entry). The English release uses a different name. Initial learners: Merutīna, Riseria. The initial learners are confirmed in only one source, the per-character pages of gcgx.games.

valkyrie-daaku-seivaa.desc: Summons a giant sword to slash one enemy.
valkyrie-daaku-seivaa.note: 3 hits. CT increases by 3 after use (Game Log, Aotama no Hoshiboshi and gcgx agree). In finishing moves it becomes a stronger version of the same spell (intermediate magic), and with a staff that can use grand magic equipped, it becomes the grand magic "Fainaru Cherio" (grand magic is a finishing move, so it has no separate entry). The English release uses a different name. Initial learners: Merutīna, Rezādo. The initial learners are confirmed in only one source, the per-character pages of gcgx.games.

valkyrie-shadu-saavanto.desc: Summons dark monsters to attack enemies.
valkyrie-shadu-saavanto.note: 3 hits. Used from the battle command (the magic menu opened with the SELECT button), it targets all enemies. When set as an attack spell and used with the button attack, it is single-target (gcgx, Game Log, Aotama no Hoshiboshi). CT increases by 5 after use (Game Log, Aotama no Hoshiboshi and gcgx agree). In finishing moves it becomes a stronger version of the same spell (intermediate magic), and with a staff that can use grand magic equipped, it becomes the grand magic "Meteo Suwōmu" (grand magic is a finishing move, so it has no separate entry). The English release uses a different name. Initial learners: Ganossa. The initial learners are confirmed in only one source, the per-character pages of gcgx.games.

valkyrie-poizun-burou.desc: Attacks with a poison mist and poisons the enemy.
valkyrie-poizun-burou.note: 1 hit; the added effect is poison (English-language sources say it drains 10% of max HP each turn). The element is "poison" in the sources, which is not among the site's shared elements, so it is set to none. Used from the battle command (the magic menu opened with the SELECT button), it targets all enemies. When set as an attack spell and used with the button attack, it is single-target (gcgx, Game Log, Aotama no Hoshiboshi). CT increases by 3 after use (Game Log, Aotama no Hoshiboshi and gcgx agree). In finishing moves it becomes a stronger version of the same spell (intermediate magic), and with a staff that can use grand magic equipped, it becomes the grand magic "Petoro Disurapushon" (grand magic is a finishing move, so it has no separate entry). The English release uses a different name. Initial learners: Ganossa, Rezādo. The initial learners are confirmed in only one source, the per-character pages of gcgx.games.

valkyrie-sutoon-touchi.desc: Attacks one enemy, with a chance to petrify it.

CT increases by 3 after use (Game Log, Aotama no Hoshiboshi and gcgx agree). In finishing moves it becomes a stronger version of the same spell (intermediate magic), and with a staff that can use grand magic equipped, it becomes the grand magic "Karunēji Ansemu" (grand magic is a finishing move, so it has no separate entry). The English release uses a different name. Initial learners: 夢瑠, Rezādo. The initial learners are confirmed in only one source, the per-character pages of gcgx.games.

valkyrie-kyua-puramusu.desc: Restores about 80% of max HP (DME) to all allies.
valkyrie-kyua-puramusu.note: CT increases by 5 after use (Game Log and gcgx agree). The healing amount is 80% of max DME. The English release uses a different name. The English-language guide (Almar's Guides) lists the target as one ally, but "all allies" from Game Log and gcgx is used. Initial learners: Jerādo, Rorenta, Shiho. The initial learners are confirmed in only one source, the per-character pages of gcgx.games.

valkyrie-oodinarii-sheipu.desc: Cures one ally's status ailments other than knockout.
valkyrie-oodinarii-sheipu.note: CT increases by 1 after use (Game Log and gcgx agree). Cures poison, paralysis, petrification, freeze and silence (English-language source). The English release uses a different name. gcgx's Nanami page writes the name as "Ōtinari Sheipu", but the spelling from the same site's spell list and spellbook list and from Game Log is used. Initial learners: Nanami, Merutīna, Shiho. The initial learners are confirmed in only one source, the per-character pages of gcgx.games.

valkyrie-evooku-fezaa.desc: Revives one knocked-out ally with 80% HP (DME).

valkyrie-gaado-reinfoosu.desc: Multiplies all allies' defense (RDM) by 1.5 for 10 turns.

The initial learners are confirmed in only one source, the per-character pages of gcgx.games.

valkyrie-maito-reinfoosu.desc: Multiplies all allies' attack power (ATK) by 1.5 for 10 turns.

valkyrie-puribento-soosarii.desc: Seals the magic of all enemies for 3 turns.

The English release uses a different name. Initial learners: Ganossa, Rezādo. The initial learners are confirmed in only one source, the per-character pages of gcgx.games.
